_about: ROUND-5 SURVEY BACKLOG (2026-10-02): what is genuinely world-class in web design right now. 10 lenses, Fable scouts, each direction grounded in real screenshots of the exemplar sites (findings/worldclass-survey-2026-10/shots/<lens>/, local only). status: todo | merged (duplicate of dupOf) | building | built | parked. refShots are calibration references for builders and judges, never layouts to clone: every template gets its own fictional brand, palette shift and content model.

asia-and-beyond.landscape: The strongest non-Western work in 2026 does not perform 'culture'; it uses the native script as the layout engine. In Japan the best sites (Ougiya, Mikaku Henshu, Joshibi Crafts) set real vertical-rl mincho on paper strips or page edges, keep display and body sizes close (30px vs 14px) and build hierarchy from orientation, ruled cells and ma instead of scale. A second Japanese pole is loud and joyful: Showa-retro centenary indexes (Nittoh 100 Picnic), Edo brush-lettering billboards (Shunputei Yoichi) and hand-cut paper frames with live weather microcopy (Musu sauna), all with one saturated colour and heavy custom lettering. Korean studios (Everyday Practice, Ordinary People, Sulki and Min) run the site as a working archive: one type size, app-like panes, acid tag chips, posters as the only imagery. Arabic and Thai excellence lives in type-foundry and independent-studio sites (40MUSTAQEL, 29LT, TPTQ Arabic, Cadson Demak), where the script is shown at 200px+ on flat colour and the Latin is deliberately the secondary voice, while Gulf institutions (Art Jameel, Qatar Museums) are at their best when Arabic and Latin are stacked or interlaced as one lockup. Taiwan contributes packaging-maximal brand worlds (Suzaku Curry) with four-side marquee frames and modular CJK glyphs. The quiet extreme is also alive: a near-empty white page with one hand-drawn walker (ishikawa.co), a festival built on the idea of 'the in-between' with a mono definition list and a revision pill (Featured Projects 2026), a black field holding one printed object (Wang Zhi-Hong). What is absent across all of them: hero CTAs, card shadows, gradient blobs, stock icon rows. Regional portfolios that chase Awwwards with glass 3D 'hello' objects and crosshair grids (seen in China and India lists) are technically fine but culturally anonymous, and several famous studio homes (Plus X, homunculus, Toby Ng) show nothing but a dark splash at scroll 0, which is useless for a thumbnail-led library.

asia-and-beyond.motionNotes: Evidence is still frames at scroll 0, mid-scroll and mobile, so easing values are inferred. Entrances are slow and material: text arrives by blur-to-sharp (Yoichi mid-scroll frame shows headline and body still blurred while resolving line by line), photos sit slightly rotated and settle (mount), paper elements appear as if hung or placed. Scroll is mostly plain document scroll with reveal-on-enter rather than hijacked pinning; the loud sites add perpetual marquees (Nittoh top band, Suzaku four-side frame, Musu weather pill text ticking inside the nav capsule) so the page is alive without input. Objects carry the 3D: a spinning coin and chrome logo charms (Suzaku), a street-sign pole (Hiroto Sato), bas-relief creatures drifting behind type (Garden Eight). Hover language is typographic: pills invert, tag chips are flat colour, underlines are dotted, buttons are inverse-video mono or parenthesis shapes. Carousels use tick-mark pagers and arrow glyphs, not dots. The quiet sites use one continuous idle motion (a walking figure, a slowly sliding strip of tiles with the centre one enlarged) and almost nothing else. Timing character: 800 to 1600ms, ease-out expo or cubic for reveals, linear for marquees, no bounce.

avant-garde.landscape: The sharpest convention-breaking work of 2025-2026 is quiet, not loud: authorship now shows as one rule pushed to its limit on an otherwise bare page, never as stacked effects. Across about 65 sites captured (Hoverstat.es 2025-2026 features, Siteinspire unusual-layout and typographic, Brutalist Websites, art-school and fashion seeds) the recurring move is a violent scale collision inside a single typeface: 95-165px headlines beside 11-12px metadata with nothing in between (Visual Society, Ballet national de Marseille, MSCHF, lament.tv). Second, navigation has become the composition itself: nav words stretched to fill the viewport (Julien von Schultzendorff, Special Offer Inc, PIN-UP), a roster woven into a justified manifesto paragraph (Anorak), a spreadsheet as the exhibition (Beckmans), a pile of work as a frame around a clean index (tiger.exposed). Third, browser defaults are worn as couture: Times New Roman at 13px, visited-purple and default-blue underlined links, native buttons and selects, hand-shaped concrete-poetry paragraphs (Eilidh Duffy, AGE hh, Most Beautiful Swiss Books, BLESS all-beige archive). Fourth, type is treated as matter with weather: stippled dust letters that focus on interaction (Soft Labor, July 2026), wind-hatched caps driven by live wind speed (Three Zero Five), inflated bubble fonts (Sandberg Instituut), ink-bleed scripts (Small Talk). Institutions are the boldest clients this year: the Yale School of Art site relaunched in September 2026 with deliberately mismatched live widgets, and schools commission student-made remixes of system fonts (Werkplaats Typografie uses 'Arial Narrow Pool' and 'Courier New Service'). Palettes are almost always white or one flat odd colour (peach, lilac, kraft, warm grey) plus black and exactly one RGB-pure accent (link blue #0000ee-ish, electric blue, red). What is absent defines the level: no cards, no shadows, no gradients, no icons, no hero image, no smooth-scroll theatrics, frequently no margins. Fashion's mainstream edge (Acne, Our Legacy, Kiko Kostadinov) has normalised into tidy e-commerce; the real experimentation sits with small labels, magazines (Buffalo Zine, Real Review, PIN-UP), artists and schools.

avant-garde.motionNotes: Evidence base: static captures at scroll 0 plus two scrolled stops, cross-read with Hoverstat curator notes; I did not record video, so timings below are design prescriptions consistent with what the frames show. The best sites in this lens move by LAYOUT, not by decoration: columns re-proportion and letterforms stretch or squeeze as a consequence (Schultzendorff, muda.co), a scattered pile sorts itself into a list (tiger.exposed), a page scales back to reveal the next (AGE hh), cells expand inside a grid. Entrances are abrupt and mechanical: text sets line by line, type-out pacing, elements appear by display toggle rather than fade; where easing exists it is a single fast ease-out (200-400ms), never springy. Scroll is native and un-hijacked; choreography comes from position: sticky layering (Ballet de Marseille's fixed giant nav against a scrolling box stack, lament.tv's stacking bands) and from headers that collapse from slab to strip (PIN-UP). Hover is a hard swap: instant colour inversion, an image appearing at the cursor with no transition, a paragraph dimming to leave only names (Anorak). Live data is used as a motion source instead of timelines: wind speed (Three Zero Five), clock hands pointing at names (RISD Here For Now), calendar and weather widgets (Yale), a playhead (xk.studio, Werktitel). Texture motion is stepped, low-frame-rate grain re-rolling like a photocopier, not smooth noise. Cursor is treated as an instrument (slide-rule cursor on the Lido site plan, pixel arrow on nodate) rather than a decorated follower. Reduced-motion variants are trivial for this genre because the still state is already the design.

award-studios-now.landscape: Index used: Awwwards Sites of the Month Jun 2025 to Aug 2026, the Sep 2026 SOTM nominee list and the Aug-Oct 2026 SOTD run, CSSDA WOTM 2025-2026, Awwwards 2025 annual winners; about 55 live sites were captured and read. The frontier has split in two. One half is still the heavy WebGL set piece (Lusion's Oryzo, Immersive Garden, basement's USAvionix, 60fps The Watch, Lightweight, SHIFTBRAIN /zeroz), but the wow has moved from abstract shader spectacle to ONE physically lit, believable object or scene with real art direction and a sense of humour or product truth. The other half, which is where the taste is right now, wins with almost no 3D: ERA Residence and Son Daven (The First The Last, SOTM Aug and Jun 2026) are two-colour typographic systems with a single owned graphic device; Aspen Search is a hairline cell grid with dithered canvases; Paul Kalkbrenner is one bold name with an inline media chip on white; Gil Huybrecht is a black contact sheet set entirely in one 16px size. Common grammar across the winners: a committed two or three colour palette with one acid or pastel accent, one grotesk at weight 450-700 tracked -3 to -5 percent paired with either a mono for labels or one extreme display voice (condensed didone, swash serif, inscriptional roman, copperplate script), display to body ratios of 10:1 and up, and body copy that is small (12-16px) and often bold. Chrome is now part of the composition: nav built as table cells, joined tabs or colour swatches, live clocks, scroll-percent numerals, registration marks, visible guide lines, designed cookie cards. Word-level mixing of two typefaces inside one headline (Lando Norris, Oimachi, ERA, Renaissance Edition) is the signature typographic move of 2025-2026. Entrance gates with a sound prompt are standard on campaign work (Miu Miu, Tie-break, Colonia Zacamil, Tuscan Journey), and persistent audio bars appear on brand sites. Layout shape-language has shifted from rounded cards to notched tabs, chamfered frames, arches and ruled cells. What is conspicuously absent from the best work: bento grids, gradient-mesh auroras, glass cards, card shadows, generic stock heroes, and centred hero plus three feature columns.

award-studios-now.motionNotes: ENTRANCE: the preloader is a designed ritual tied to the identity, never a generic bar. Observed: Locomotive L.I.S.A. slides duplicated text lines horizontally into register; Obys zooms a nested tunnel of its own screenshots with a small counter at the right edge; The Monolith Project draws giant outlined numerals with a bouncing red ball; Malvah builds a rotating sphere out of its own wordmark with Enter Site and 01/02/03 steps; Son Daven assembles its wordmark column by column from stitch bars; Kalkbrenner opens the word space to admit the media chip. Campaign sites gate behind Enter plus a sound prompt. Timing is slow and confident: 800-1400ms, expo or quart out, one element at a time, hairlines drawing before content. SCROLL: Lenis-style inertia remains but the choreography is chapter based: palette flips between chapters (ERA aubergine to powder blue, Lando off-white to olive to black, Lightweight black to fog grey), the hero element persists and transforms rather than scrolling away (media chip grows to full bleed, arch aperture rises, wordmark docks into the nav, object rotates while type passes in front of and behind it). Section boundaries are shaped: pixel-skyline block wipes, arch masks, rounded panel overlaps, an iris of light that whites out the screen (/zeroz). Text reveals are line-level opacity ramps from 40-55 percent grey to full (Aspen, Seasats) or per-letter roll on an arc (Lightweight), plus typed last-letter accent (Terminal). Progress is shown as content: scroll-percent numeral on a rail, colour-segmented scrollbar, chapter rail with a growing line, tick-mark nav. HOVER: restrained and structural: a table row inverts and swaps a preview cell, siblings dim to 30 percent, hairline circle CTAs rotate a label or fill radially, notched cards lift their tab; cursors are mostly native, with a small crosshair or dot only where it means something. TRANSITIONS: shared-element continuity (thumbnail expands in place, FLIP between Grid, Gallery and perspective-crawl modes), and theme toggles as first-class controls. SOUND: explicit Sound ON/OFF text toggle plus a Now playing bar with a 5-bar equaliser; never autoplay without the gate. REDUCED MOTION: the best sites degrade to static composed frames, which is why the scroll=0 frame must already be a finished poster.

contrarian-excluded.landscape: The strongest work outside the avant-garde / minimal / luxury canon in 2026 wins by being unmistakably made by someone, for a specific place or purpose, and by letting the content model be the design. The Tiny Awards 2026 shortlist (Cursor Camp, Geokash, Train Jazz, solarpanel.scrapthe.world) and The HTML Review issue 05 show the handmade web has moved from nostalgia to craft: default Times and Arial, but used on one audacious structural idea (a CSS 3D staircase as a table of contents, a Venn map of hyperlinks, a split page hinged on one button). Independent commerce with taste (Choosing Keeping, The Kernel, Labour and Wait, Printed Matter, Ffern) refuses the DTC template entirely: no lifestyle hero, no card grid; instead an illustrated portrait of the actual shopfront, two bottle labels on kraft stripes, a typewriter chronology overprinted with fluoro slab, or a ledger rail with a live countdown and a waiting-list status. Restaurants at the top of the game (Quo Vadis, Cafe Cecilia, Noble Rot, Chez Panisse) are illustration-led and nearly image-free: one linocut street scene, one gouache lemon, one boxed botanical plate, with menus set as real typeset sheets. Low-carbon is no longer a dither filter but an instrument: Low-tech Magazine tints the page background as a battery gauge and prints its page weight; Branch exposes a grid-intensity mode switch in the header. Information density reads as beauty when it is honest (Printed Matter text-only catalogue rows with highlighter tags, Puzzmo three columns of live puzzle boards, Gwern dotted-box nav and annotated lists, McMaster-Carr thumbnail taxonomy). Typography is characterful and specific rather than neutral: Trinite, Bembo, Gill Sans tracked wide, Share, a blackletter (Robin Sloan), a fat soft serif (The Pudding), and plain system Times, almost never Inter. Colour is paper-based: warm whites (#f8f3ea, #fdfaf6), kraft, cream plus one or two inks, or strict 1-bit black on white. Live, local facts replace marketing copy: open/closed stamps with todays hours, todays weather with two swallows, battery percent, days until the next seasonal release, yesterdays puzzle records. Runner-up directions seen but not written up below, worth mining later: a city-brand civic homepage with a wave-edged colour slab and one giant search (Helsinki, Oslo); a research lab whose hero is a drifting row of pastel pencil-hatched organisms (Arcadia Science); periwinkle field of cut-out objects with mono icon lists (Geokash); a photographed bookshelf as the whole interface (Dynamicland); a lesson page whose figures are playable clip grids (Ableton Learning Music); a three-voice zine masthead with a live personal telemetry ticker and 1-bit pixel art (henry.codes); a kids brand headline with glossy stickers replacing letters (Toca Boca).

contrarian-excluded.motionNotes: Caveat: evidence is three static scroll stops per site plus fingerprints, so timing values below are design recommendations inferred from structure, not measurements. What was observable: the best sites in this lens barely animate and never hijack scroll. Motion is either structural or physical. Structural: The HTML Review staircase rotates and advances with scroll so new treads reach reading position (rows 01-04 at scroll 0, rows 04-09 one stop later); Noble Rot places its nav at the bottom of the first screen and docks it to the top on scroll; Choosing Keeping and Printed Matter keep one strip sticky (category objects; boxed name plus search) while hairline rows pass beneath; Ffern keeps a fixed ledger rail whose countdown ticks every second; henry.codes runs a one-line telemetry ticker and a ghost-repeated marquee heading; Low-tech Magazine holds the battery line fixed against scrolling content. Physical: things behave like paper, ink and stamps, not like UI: labels drop with a tiny rotation settle, stamps hit in 100-150ms with steps() easing and slight misregistration, paint and ink reveal slowly (600-1200ms, ease-out) once and then stay still, tiles squash on press (180ms spring). Hover is plain: underline, invert to a black block, a highlighter sweep, italic swap. No page loaders (the one loader seen, Michelberger, cost it the capture), no parallax heroes, no cursor followers, no smooth-scroll libraries. Live data is the micro-interaction: open/closed by local time, weather cell, battery percent, countdowns, yesterdays records. For templates: one entrance choreography that looks like printing or assembling the page (150-900ms total, staggered 40-80ms), one continuous slow ambient loop (stripe drift, battery drift, pulsing status dot), one tactile interaction that is actually functional, and a reduced-motion state that is the finished print.

editorial-culture.landscape: Surveyed 70+ culture sites by real screenshot on 2026-10-02 (museums, galleries, magazines, publishers, film, labels, festivals, theatres, long-form). The best work right now is typographic infrastructure, not decoration: the programme, the index or the archive IS the homepage, set at display size (Stedelijk rows at 104px, Visual (Archives) Society list at 95px, Ballet national de Marseille nav at 164px) with body copy pushed down to 11-16px, so the display-to-text ratio sits at 6:1 to 15:1 instead of the templated 3:1. Institutions own one custom or customised face and use it at one or two sizes only (Union at Stedelijk, Studio Museum Black, HDK Variable Fragment, KWGrotesk, SI Favorit, Pfauen Plakat, MSN Qwerty), mostly at weight 400-500: scale and tight tracking carry the hierarchy, not bold. Colour is flat and total: a whole band or page floods with one process ink (Werktitel's yellow, ochre, cobalt and vermilion bands; Sleutelaar's cyan reading mode; Julia Stoschek's ruled blue; Surfer's Journal pastel pink) and there are no gradients, shadows, glass or rounded SaaS cards anywhere. Rules do the structural work: 1px hairlines at publishers and reviews (Roma Publications, NYRA, MSN Warsaw), 6px bars at Stedelijk, dashed boxes at Marseille. The wordmark is treated as a living object (Haus der Kunst's interlocking outlined ligatures, Nieuwe Instituut switching typeface mid-word, Hans Sleutelaar's name sliced into stepped crops, Stedelijk with a sticker slapped on it) and it usually collapses into the header on scroll. Navigation is honest text: bracket checkboxes, facet counters, an A-Z wheel, a sortable ledger; the hamburger is secondary. The blue-chip galleries (Gagosian, White Cube, Zwirner, Hauser and Wirth, Mennour) are the conservative end: full-bleed artwork, centred name, dates, one button; refined but not where the invention is. The invention is at kunsthalles, performing-arts houses, small publishers and archive sites, where anti-design defaults (Arial, Times, system blue links at Roma, Buchholz, Volksbuhne, System) are used as a deliberate luxury signal. Imagery, when present, is un-styled documentation (installation views, covers as objects on flat ground), never art-directed lifestyle photography.

editorial-culture.motionNotes: Observed from scroll-state deltas in the captures plus the Hoverstat.es curator notes (no video was recorded, so easing values are inferred). 1) Masthead collapse: Stedelijk, Nieuwe Instituut and NYRA all open with a viewport-wide wordmark that, by the first scroll stop, has shrunk into the centre of a slim sticky header (same letterforms, same sticker); this is a scale/position scrub tied to scroll, not a fade. 2) Rows as tickers: Stedelijk's programme rows are wider than the viewport and translate on X (title, thumbnail, arrow, secondary label run off the right edge); Unsound, Schema, Wiener Festwochen and XL run a single thin marquee strip as a ruled band, slow and constant (roughly 40-60px/s), never bouncing. 3) Page-colour flood: Sleutelaar goes from white to full process cyan between scroll stops with archival photos sitting tinted BEHIND the running text; Werktitel changes colour band by band; HKW swaps its accent pair per event. Colour changes are hard cuts or short linear fades, not gradient sweeps. 4) Mechanical index devices: Fantastic Man's alphabet wheel rotates with the scroll position of the A-Z list (arrow fixed at 12 o'clock, 'Spin the wheel' caption); Surfer's Journal steps one cover at a time while the corner numerals change; The Gentlewoman shows '1 / 9' with a ruled caption bar. These move in discrete steps with a firm ease-out, like turning a physical dial. 5) Identity easter eggs: Haus der Kunst re-sets its interlocking wordmark with a different message and pastel fill at each stop; Kunsthalle Basel (per BP&O, not captured) has elastic carousels and a draggable menu; Walter Tiemann Preis flips language by horizontal shift. 6) What is absent: no parallax, no staggered fade-up of every paragraph, no scroll-jacking, no preloader counters; entrances are instant or a single hard reveal (lines unmasking top-down in under 400ms). Hover is typographic: underline, colour inversion to the accent ink, or a small image appearing beside the row; durations feel like 80-150ms linear.

luxury-maison.landscape: Seen across 50 live captures (2026-10-02), the houses that read most expensive right now do it by subtraction of chrome and by committing to ONE loud decision, not by dark-and-gold styling. Quiet-restraint fashion has almost no display typography at all: The Row sets the whole site in one 13px grotesque and the homepage is a single photograph three viewports tall; Sophie Buhai is 12px Univers under black-and-white hard-shadow still lifes; Phoebe Philo ships the browser default Times New Roman with a pure #FF0000 wordmark. Heritage and hospitality sit on linen and cream, never black (Aman #F3EEE7 with 14px serif tracked 0.8px, Vacheron #F8F0E5 with brown ink, Les Grands Chenes #F0ECE6 with a hand-inked wordmark and a rotated wax-seal reserve button), and they delay the first image with a large empty top margin. Haute horology is the one register that owns darkness, and it does so with extreme macro: the dial fills the viewport, hands are longer than the screen, and type is hairline (H. Moser sets Inter at weight 150, Audemars Piguet pairs Helvetica weight 100 caps with italic serif caps). High jewellery and independents share an engraver's stationery voice: wide light gothic capitals (Sackers Gothic at Boucheron, ITC Blair at De Bethune, Termina at Akrivia, Novecento Wide at Buccellati) over white with one sculptural object. The 2026 award winners that actually feel new are colour-and-letterform led rather than WebGL led: ERA Residence (Awwwards Site of the Month, Aug 2026) is aubergine, sky blue and bougainvillea with condensed didone capitals, copperplate script and an arch portal; House of Honey (SOTD Jul 2026) splices an ultra-black grotesque wordmark with a hairline script and then floods a section with 300px hot-pink script; Son Daven (SOTM Jun 2026) renders mountains and its wordmark as cross-stitch bars in two colours; White Desert (SOTD Sep 2026) keeps its column rules visible through the whole page under a 256px place name. Copperplate script is back as a structural element (ERA, House of Honey, Sobha Privy), mono captions carry provenance data (Heirest configuration strings, Unimatic live time and moon phase, bracketed coordinates at White Desert and Feadship), and illustration has returned at campaign level (Gucci La Famiglia mansion, Max Mara crayon city). What reads as luxury template is the opposite set: black marble with gold hairlines, Cinzel capitals, sparkle particles, preloader counters and scattered thumbnails with handwriting accents. Blocked and therefore NOT evidence in this report: Hermes, Bottega Veneta, Cartier, Celine, Brunello Cucinelli, Frederic Malle, Six Senses, Loro Piana. Runner-up grammars seen but not promoted to directions (nearest library slugs already cover them): Capricorn 01 Zagato's car roofline rising out of a black-to-sage gradient with ghost 01 numerals (ev-automotive-cinematic-hero), Unimatic's grey frosted utility panels over an embossed macro (spec-sheet-instrument), Vero's white plaster relief on tangerine (bas-relief-light), the GQ x Audemars Piguet white wireframe archive lab (blueprint-svg, trace-diagram), 60fps The Watch with giant type occluded by a turning 3D watch (luxury-watch-callouts).

Wordmark-only hero with nothing else on screen (ERA does it as a 2 second intro, but as a resting frame it is an empty thumbnail)
Stacked modals at entry (region picker plus cookie wall plus newsletter): observed on most real houses and it destroys the first frame; a template must not imitate it
luxury-maison.motionNotes: Evidence base: three scroll stops per site plus video counts from the fingerprint and two agency case studies; no frame-by-frame capture, so timing values are inferred. The common character is slow, linear-feeling and unbouncy: long ease-out fades (roughly 0.8-1.4s), no spring, no overshoot, nothing scales past 1.03. Entrances are rituals of drawing rather than flying in: ERA draws a vertical hairline, then opens an arch portal from the centre while the wordmark dissolves; Feadship rotates a compass then draws a horizon line; Son Daven assembles its wordmark from stitch bars. Scroll behaviour is mostly native-feeling document scroll with pinned set pieces: line-by-line or word-by-word text that turns from pale grey to ink as it crosses the viewport centre (White Desert, Audemars Piguet, Capricorn), an object that rotates or rises on scrub while type passes behind it (60fps The Watch, Capricorn roofline over ghost numerals), full-bleed looping macro video that simply plays (H. Moser 24 video elements, Sanlorenzo 21, The OWO 53). Hover and micro-interaction are almost invisible: 1px underlines that draw from the left, a short underline stub under a bold caps link that extends on hover (H. Moser), opacity 1 to 0.5 on sibling links (WWAKE sets the shop link at half opacity inside the headline), image crossfades instead of zooms. Nav chrome changes state instead of animating: House of Honey collapses its nav into a blush chip when it passes onto the dark section; The Row keeps one fixed 13px line and lets the wordmark fade under the image. Jewellery case study language (makemepulse for Cartier) is explicit: motion stays understated and supports discovery; the signature gesture is a reveal of the gouache drawing beneath the finished jewel. The one loud motion per page is typographic or chromatic: a full-section colour flood, a marquee between double rules, a 300px script word sliding laterally with scroll.

minimal-reductive.landscape: Seen across roughly 75 captured sites (architects, industrial designers, galleries, foundries, design-engineer pages; Siteinspire / Minimal Gallery / Hoverstat.es picks from late 2025 to September 2026), elite minimalism in 2026 is not 'less stuff', it is one structural idea executed with print-level typographic precision. The strongest pages replace the hero with an information structure: an opus-numbered grid of plan drawings (Office KGDVS), a sortable eight-column project ledger under a cropped 800px wordmark (Etablissement), a persistent hairline-ruled CV pane in 12px serif (Emi Takahashi), a year-ruled writing index (Benji Taylor). Type is almost always ONE family at one or two sizes, and the sizes are deliberately 'wrong' by template standards: either very small (Buchholz 11px, Sort Office 7px labels, Dubuis 12px, Fukasawa 14px weight 200) or uniformly mid-size with no display tier at all (Olgiati 18px, Pawson 27px, 6a 22px, Pezo 24px), or one utilitarian text blown up to fill the viewport (Schemata's address at about 104px, Kaspar's 112px lowercase statement). Margins are tight and exact (10 to 30px page gutters, zero-gutter image pairs) while vertical gaps are enormous (240 to 400px of nothing between blocks at OGATA, Chipperfield, Toogood); the luxury is in the unequal ratio, never in even padding. Alignment systems are visible and literal: full-height hairline columns (Kaspar), ruled table cells used as navigation (Studio OL, Groth, Mac Moss), black 1px cell borders (KGDVS index), dotted row rules (Tiger Dingsun). Colour is paper-white, warm paper (#F2ECDF, #F3EEE8, #F5F1E5) or pure black, with at most one flat accent used once (Rauno's yellow disc, Gerosa's acid strip, Buchholz's yellow links). Navigation is demoted to plain words: a comma-separated sentence (6a, Mesura), three tiny underlined links (Schemata), a single name in the corner (Pawson), or nothing until scroll (Van Duysen, OK-RM). What is absent matters most: no CTA buttons, no cards, no shadows, no radius, no icons, no section headings that sell, no gradient, no scroll-reveal theatre; each site keeps exactly one precise interaction (a Drawings/Images toggle, a sort arrow, a minimap ruler, a focus-pull blur, a footnote that travels in the margin). The lazy version of minimal (centred logo, three links, big Inter headline, beige) fails because it removes content without adding a system; the elite version adds a system and then removes everything that is not the system.
dated: Centred giant sans headline (Inter / Neue Montreal) + muted subline + pill CTA on white: the 2022 SaaS-minimal hero
Mixed serif-italic and grotesque in one headline ('a thoughtful *design studio*') with inline pill images: now a template (seen on this.design, still handsome, but it reads 2023)
Hover-a-project-name-and-an-image-follows-the-cursor list ('Selected Work 2019 - 2024'): the default portfolio mechanic of 2021 to 2023
Thin-weight uppercase with 0.3em tracking on everything, hairline icons, 'less is more' quotes: 2016 minimal
Fade-up-and-translate reveal on every block plus slow lerped smooth scroll; preloader counter 0 to 100

Three-column feature rows with icons, numbered '01 / 02 / 03' service blocks, testimonial sliders on a studio site
minimal-reductive.motionNotes: Evidence is scroll-stop stills plus DOM fingerprints (video / canvas counts, page heights) and the Hoverstat.es curator notes, so timing values are inferred, not measured. Entrance: the best sites barely animate on load; content is simply present (Olgiati, Benji Taylor, Buchholz), or a single full-bleed image holds with a lone name (Pawson, Van Duysen: page height exactly 1 viewport, crossfading slideshow). Where there is an entrance it is one move: OK-RM shows a centred two-line Times statement on black which dims to nothing as you scroll and the first project object appears in its place; Kaspar draws an ASCII figure on a canvas behind the statement. Scroll: structural, not decorative. Etablissement's cropped wordmark re-crops and shrinks as the page moves (the 'Eta' at scroll 0 becomes 'Etab' with the table rising beneath it); Rauno converts vertical scroll into horizontal travel across white cards with a tick-ruler minimap whose viewport rectangle moves in sync; KGDVS lets photo halves and plan halves pass each other at different column positions with a fixed header overprinting them; Chipperfield, 6a and Toogood rely on nothing but generous asymmetric placement while scrolling natively. Hover / micro-interaction: one precise behaviour per site: sort arrows on table headers, a Drawings/Images toggle fixed bottom-centre, grey-to-black row activation, focus-pull blur where non-hovered images wash out to near-white (Krisztian Eder), footnote text that sits in the right margin level with its reference (Studio OL), a live local clock (Groth, Mac Moss, Benji Taylor, Lebedev), 'sort by random / chronological' re-layout (Kerez, Elisa Breyer). Transitions between states are short crossfades or hard cuts (150 to 300ms, linear or gentle ease-out); nothing bounces, nothing overshoots, no parallax. Reduced-motion versions are trivial because the static state is already the design.

tech-craft.landscape: Surveyed 62 live sites by screenshot on 2026-10-02 (Linear, Vercel, Cursor, Zed, Amp, Cognition, Oxide, Teenage Engineering, Analogue, Playdate, Daylight, interfaces.dev, rauno.me and others). The single biggest shift versus 2022-2024 is that the best product companies went LIGHT and WARM: Cursor (#f7f7f4), Cognition (#f7f6f5), Anthropic (#faf9f5), Mistral (#fbfbf8), Poolside (#fbfaf6), Zed, Paper, Granola, Factory, Vercel (now #fafafa with a flat black triangle) all sit on paper tones; dark survives only where it is flat and glowless (Linear #08090a, Oxide oklch(0.16 0.01 260)). Display type shrank and calmed: Cursor's hero headline is 26px, Poolside 32px, Cognition 36px, Runway 40px, ElevenLabs 48px at weight 300; hierarchy is carried by a two-tone sentence (ink lead, grey continuation) instead of size. Serif came back as a deliberate counter-signal to AI sterility: Zed (IBM Plex Serif italic in one ink blue), Amp (Sagittaire roman plus italic), Resend (Domaine 96px), Railway, Exa, Perplexity (GT Canon 180px), Cognition and Thinking Machines (serif BODY under a grotesk head). Product UI is rendered as real DOM at 11-13px fidelity and is the hero image (Cursor's three-pane agent window on a painted landscape, Linear's issue view, Zed, Attio, Poolside's terminal), not a tilted screenshot with a glow. Structure became ornament: visible construction lines with intersection nodes (Zed), ticked column guides and margin numerals 01/02/03 (Cognition), dotted column rules (Amp), FIG 0.1 captions over hairline isometrics (Linear) and boxed FIG. 1 labels (Oxide), logo walls as ruled tables rather than marquees (Cognition, PlanetScale, interfaces.dev, Mistral). Keyboard-first affordances are printed on the buttons themselves (Zed's keycaps D, C, S and Cmd-Shift-P). Hardware pages split into two registers: the object on a seamless studio ground with almost no chrome (Analogue, Playdate, Teenage Engineering's black stage) and the warm, photographed, humane calm-tech register with floating modules (Daylight, Sandbar, Light Phone). Design-engineer personal sites remain a 640px column of 16px text (Paco, Emil, Benji, Jakub) where all the craft is in micro-interaction, while the frontier of that school (rauno.me, Devouring Details, interfaces.dev) turns tool chrome itself (minimaps, artboards, selection handles, redlines) into the art direction. Pixel and dither returned as a brand system, not nostalgia: Mistral's big-pixel sunset mosaic and pixel cat, Poolside's cell clusters, Factory loading Geist Pixel, Linear Now's dithered block thumbnails.

Glassmorphism cards: backdrop-blur plus 1px white/10 border plus animated gradient 'shine' border

Infinite logo marquee as first-fold filler (best sites now use a static ruled logo table)
3D-tilted dashboard screenshot with perspective, glow and floor reflection

Sparkle-emoji pill badge with shimmer border ('Introducing X') above the headline

Tweet-wall testimonial masonry (replaced by calm flat quote grids: Cursor 3x2, Zed with one highlighted card)

Dark-mode-only identity; the 2026 default is warm paper light with an optional flat dark
tech-craft.motionNotes: Caveat: evidence is stills (several caught mid-transition) plus known behaviour of these sites; millisecond values below are build recommendations, not measurements. The best sites in this lens move LITTLE and move the PRODUCT, not the page. Entrance: no hero text theatrics; text is simply there or fades 200-400ms with at most 8px rise, while the DOM product window performs (Cursor's agent thread streams log lines, Oxide's console types, OpenAI's prompt placeholder cross-fades between suggestions, captured mid-fade). Structural elements draw on: hairline rules scale from 0, isometric strokes animate via stroke-dashoffset, nodes pop after lines meet. Scroll: sticky text column while a UI window scrolls its own content; two-tone statements fill word by word (Daylight caught at 'We refuse to accept' half-revealed; Linear's grey continuation); rauno.me maps vertical scroll to a horizontal artboard strip with a tick minimap whose viewport rectangle slides (seen moving between captures); Devouring Details runs an orange playhead line down a tick ruler. Live data as motion: odometer digits rolling in a mono chip (Ramp's '0.907361%' captured mid-roll, Stripe's GDP counter, comma's miles driven) and a bottom status ticker. Hover and micro-interaction are fast and physical: 60-150ms, no bounce on chrome, springs only on objects; buttons press down 1-2px with shadow collapse; keyboard shortcuts printed on buttons actually fire; rows highlight instantly in and ease out. Easing character: ease-out-quint or expo for draws, linear or stepped for digital things (pixels, LCDs, counters), springs (stiffness ~300, damping ~30) for dragged or tool-like elements. Hardware pages are nearly still: slow 1.2-1.6s scale-settle on photography, spotlight fade-ups on black stages, and the object's own functional micro-animation (LCD game running, LED blink) as the only loop. Reduced motion is treated as first-class: final states are the default render and motion is additive.

technique-and-motion.landscape: The frontier in late 2026 is not the feature demo; it is platform capability used invisibly, in service of one committed art direction. The strongest pages I captured turn chrome into an instrument: Devouring Details runs a tick ruler and a full-width orange reading hairline down a one-size-of-type manual, Rauno Freiberg replaces navigation with a 16-tick scrubber, and the Geist specimen pins metric tags (710 / 530 / 0 / -150) to real font metrics on a hairline construction grid. Corner and outline geometry has become a design variable rather than a radius token: ToyFight sets every headline word on its own pill or square tile, ERA Residence and Hubtown frame the viewport in chamfered hairlines, and corner-shape, shape() and border-shape make those forms native, responsive and animatable. WebGPU with TSL is now the default award-level renderer (Oryzo, IVRESS, Shader.se, almost every September 2026 Codrops demo), but the winners spend it on ONE tactile object or material under careful light (a cork coaster on a cutting mat), never on particle storms. Colour is committed and wide gamut: a single saturated field (Config green, ERA oxblood, Nabla ultramarine) or thousands of hair-fine P3 strands on a pale ground (Stripe Sessions), with OKLCH interpolation keeping transitions clean. Type splits into two camps: featherweight giant display with hard negative tracking (Sessions: 100px, weight 250, -4px, leading 0.85; Daylight: 60px, weight 300, -4.2px) and single-size grotesk pages where hierarchy is position only; pixel and raster faces are the current display accent (FK Raster at ToyFight, Geist Pixel, the Codrops hub wordmark). Chrome habits worth copying: docked bottom control bars with a sound toggle, corner registration marks around text blocks and buttons, live clocks, nav that becomes a glass bar only once stuck, logos that morph into pills on scroll. Fixture result for builders (probed on the factory's own headless Chromium 148.0.7778): corner-shape and superellipse(), text-box trim, shape(), border-shape, sibling-index(), view() timelines, scroll-triggered animation triggers, anchor positioning, interpolate-size, scroll-state queries, ::scroll-marker, scroll-target-group, if(), font-palette with palette-mix(), display-p3, relative colour, dynamic-range-limit, linear(), @starting-style and element-scoped view transitions all report supported; text-fit, row-rule gap decorations, random() and navigator.gpu (headless) do NOT, so those four need fallbacks. Three directions I would otherwise have filed are already filed by sibling lenses and should simply inherit the technique: the ERA arch portal (use shape() for the arch, border-shape for its concentric hairline outlines, corner-shape: bevel for the frame), the Daylight scrubbed letter inking (one scroll timeline plus sibling-index() offsets), and the Rauno plate strip (sticky stage plus scroll() timeline, ticks as scroll markers). What is absent from all of the best work: glow gradients, bento-plus-accent, smoothed scroll hijacking, and motion that exists only because a library made it cheap.
dated: Dark SaaS hero with purple or blue glow gradient, shiny-border glass cards and a 24px-radius bento (the 2022-2023 Linear clone; Linear itself has moved to hairline FIG plates with no glow)
Lenis smooth scroll plus the same SplitText line-rise with the same expo ease on every heading of every section
WebGL hero as atmosphere only: particle storms, noise orbs, aurora blobs, mesh-gradient backgrounds with no object and no story
Platform-feature demo pages with no art direction (a scroll progress bar, parallax cards, a view-transition card flip) presented as the design
Preloader counting 0 to 100 percent over a black screen that pays off with nothing (two of my captures were only this)
Blob cursor with mix-blend-difference, magnetic buttons, rotating 'available for work' badge, infinite marquee ticker as filler
Full-page scroll-jacked section snapping and velocity-skewed horizontal galleries
Gradient-filled headline text (purple to pink) and sparkle icons as an AI signifier
Claymorphic 3D mascots and emoji as generic friendliness
Variable-font weight wobble on hover as the only idea on the page
Glassmorphism applied to every card; in current work glass appears on exactly one element (the stuck nav or one docked card)
Spring bounce on everything; current craft uses bounce only on small tactile objects and zero bounce on layout
technique-and-motion.motionNotes: Caveat first: I captured stills at three scroll stops, not video, so the timings below are a prescription assembled from mid-state frames (Daylight caught mid letter-reveal, Obys and IVRESS mid preloader, Leo Parpeix mid tile-to-band expansion), from numbers printed on the sites themselves (motion.dev shows stagger(0.04) and type=spring in its own UI) and from published craft guidance (Emil Kowalski: UI animation under 300ms, ease-out for enter and exit, never animate keyboard-initiated actions, keep everything interruptible). ENTRANCE: one ritual, 0.8 to 1.4s total, never blocking input; type arrives by per-line mask rise of 16 to 24px over 500 to 700ms with 60 to 90ms line stagger; a hero frame or object settles from scale 0.96 to 1 with an over-damped curve; small UI (chips, pills, dock) 150 to 250ms. If a preloader exists it must morph INTO the hero (Leo Parpeix: a tilted rounded tile of the hero render scales to the full-bleed band) rather than fade away. EASING FAMILIES: expo-style ease-out for arrivals, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) or (.19,1,.22,1); cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1) for sheets and cards; ease-in-out only for things already on screen moving between states; linear() springs with bounce 0.15 to 0.25 and 400 to 600ms for small physical objects (tiles, dots, toggles), zero bounce for layout; steps(6 to 12) for print-like stipple or pixel material. STAGGER: sibling-index() times 40 to 60ms, total cascade capped near 400ms; grids of looping specimens run on offset phases so they never sync. SCROLL: two modes that must not share an element. (1) Scrubbed and strictly linear, tied 1:1 to scroll with no smoothing: reading hairline, letter inking, arch opening, colour-field interpolation in OKLCH, font axis depth. (2) Scroll-triggered, time-based, played once: 12 to 24px rises with opacity, hairlines drawing left to right in 500ms. State changes ride scroll-state queries: nav becomes a glass bar only when stuck (Stripe Sessions), a logo morphs into a labelled pill and a progressive blur appears behind the filter row once scrolled (Detail). Whole-page colour fields change per chapter (ERA oxblood to pale blue, Daylight silver to amber, Oryzo wood to black void). HOVER MICRO-PHYSICS: colour 120 to 150ms; underline redraw left to right 250ms; press scale 0.97 in 100ms; neighbours of a hovered tile or tick react with a 3 to 4 element falloff (dock-style); cursor becomes a 1px crosshair on instrument sites; ghost cursors act out demos until the real pointer arrives. TRANSITIONS: same-document view transitions at 250 to 350ms with shared-element morphs, outgoing content fading in about 150ms; element-scoped transitions for filter reflow so the rest of the page stays interactive. WEBGL: damped camera (lerp 0.06 to 0.1), pointer parallax at or under 2 degrees, one hero move per chapter (Oryzo: top-down flat-lay, then the object lifts and tilts into darkness). SOUND: off by default, toggled from persistent chrome (R-K dock, Hubtown footer, Josh Comeau header); ticks under 60ms and quiet. RESTRAINT: Devouring Details opens by asking whether some interactions feel better with no motion at all; the best pages have one signature motion and keep everything else under 300ms; ambient loops are slow (20 to 40s) or stepped at about 12fps. REDUCED MOTION: keep scroll-linked position mapping (it is user-driven), remove springs, loops, parallax and autoplaying ghost cursors, and gate rAF and inline transforms in JS as well as CSS.

type-and-graphic-studios.landscape: The best foundry and studio sites of 2025-2026 have stopped behaving like shops with a hero and behave like printed specimens that happen to be interactive: one typeface, one idea, one palette, executed as a system. The strongest work captured (the GT Mechanik and GT Standard minisites, CcType's CcTimeline, Klim's Die Grotesk page, Lineto's catalogue, Hot Type's Exat) fills the viewport with letterforms at 200-620px and puts the craft into the furniture around them: hairline rules, bordered cells, 9-12px mono labels, numbered ticks, metric lines. Colour is flat and decisive, usually one saturated field per section (GT Standard #FE3500, GT Pantheon #5B04E7, Klim #D33C03, Exat #FF6201) or a small plate palette used like spot inks (Mechanik's pink, olive, mint, acid yellow, cornflower); gradients, glass, glow and drop shadows are simply absent. Navigation is treated as a designed object, not a bar: file-folder tabs that accumulate as you scroll, a ruler scrubber with tick marks, label-maker chips stacked down the left edge, a nav line pinned to the vertical centre of the screen, 164px nav words that occupy half the page. Studios split two ways: the photo and showreel led giants (Pentagram, Wolff Olins, Collins, Order) are competent but conventional, while the inventive ones go dense or go silent: DIA's 13-column greyscale contact sheet, Base Design's zoomable feed mosaic, OK-RM's single Times sentence on black, Base Off Mute's image-free episode index with guest names set in ringed letters. Body type is small and confident (9-16px, often mono or the house grotesque) against display type 10-40x larger, with display tracking aggressively negative (-0.02 to -0.09em) and leading at 0.75-0.95. A second 2026 thread is the hyperreal 3D mascot object on white (Dinamo's Schengen truck fleet, Sharp Type's corner shop, Blaze's pocket knife, trulytype's frog, Plomb's tin boxer): it is everywhere and already close to a formula. What separates world-class from trendy in this lens is that the layout device is derived from the typeface's own concept (mono-to-poly spacing becomes a gauge, a width axis becomes a ruler of m's, a timeline becomes four ruled rows), so nothing reads as a template and nothing needs a photograph.

Full-bleed autoplay showreel slider with dot pagination and a caption bottom-left (Pentagram, Wolff Olins): competent and anonymous
Hyperreal 3D mascot object floating on white with pill buttons: at least five foundries deep now, novelty spent unless the object carries the concept
Sticker-bomb specimen: starbursts, speech bubbles, rotated badges on cream (fictional-typeface.com)
AI-video hero behind white type (Fontwerk's Shibuya chrome sphere)
Glassmorphism nav pills, gradient mesh blobs, glow, 24px-radius bento card grids

type-and-graphic-studios.motionNotes: Captured as stills at three scroll stops per site, so this is inferred from state changes between frames, loaded-asset fingerprints and gallery write-ups, not from watching video. The pattern is state-machine motion rather than decorative easing: chrome changes state at section boundaries (GT Standard adds a coloured index tab per section; CcType's header appends the section name and the whole page flips from #CDCDCD to near-black; Klim's 20px orange frame floods into a full orange page and the nav gains black tick separators; Koto's nav collapses into a single 'HOME +' pill). Scroll position is shown as data: GT Mechanik's fixed ruler moves a pink needle along numbered stations (87.8, 91.2, 95.6, 97.7, 99.2) while stepped readouts ('97.7 - POLY') type out in a staircase. Entrances are mechanical: hairlines wipe, type sets on, steps() easing, overprint layers slide at different rates (Mechanik's pink '04' passing over a blue plate with multiply blending); almost nothing fades up softly. Variable axes are the hero animation: weight and width interpolate on hover or scroll (CcTimeline's ladder was caught mid-interpolation in the capture; Exat documents a cursor field with seven concentric rings of weight influence; Typotheque draws live axis sliders as vertical lines across its hero). Live data doubles as micro-interaction: ticking city clocks (Porto Rocha, Koto, Bureau Rouge), an 'N online' presence chip (Dinamo), live wind speed driving a hatched variable font (Three Zero Five), fuzzy type that sharpens on interaction (Soft Labor). Hover is instant and binary (chip or tile colour inversion, greyscale to colour on a thumbnail) at roughly 80-200ms, linear or stepped; long luxurious eases (1s+ cross-dissolves) appear only on photo-led sites. Reduced-motion fallbacks come almost free because every state is a legible static layout.

directions.name: Tategaki Paper-Strip Confectioner
directions.signature: At scroll 0 on a pale grey #EEEEEE page: one macro product image clipped by a huge circle arc (radius about 1100px, centre off the bottom-left) fills the lower two thirds; bottom-right, two white paper strips (each about 60px wide, 330 and 380px tall, 6px apart, the right one starting higher) each carry one line of the headline in vertical-rl mincho 30px weight 600. Above the arc: a single dated news line with a bullet. Top-left: a tiny vertical three-character shop mark. On 390px the strips move to the upper-left over the image and a faint asanoha pattern lens overlaps the arc.
directions.grammar: Grid: 12 columns, 135px side margins at 1440, header 80px with mincho text nav at 15px and 40px gaps, line icons right. Type scale is deliberately flat: display 30px vertical, section heads 28px vertical bold centred, product names 15px, body 14px/1.5, labels 11px white on black; hierarchy comes from orientation and paper, not size. Spacing: 200px+ of empty grey between sections. Colour: #EEEEEE ground, #1A1A1A ink, pure white strips and tiles, zero accent colour (the food is the colour). Imagery: studio macro and square product tiles on white with soft shadow. Chrome: horizontal shelf with arrow glyphs and a tick-mark pager. Absent: Latin hero headline, CTA buttons, gradients, card shadows, any red-sun or brush cliche.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Zen Old Mincho (display and body), Zen Kaku Gothic New, Oswald for dates, Lora; elsewhere Shippori Mincho B1, Libre Baskerville, Lusitana. All are already free on Google Fonts, so use them directly. Thai note: Thai has no vertical tradition; a Thai variant should keep the strips but set them horizontally stacked in Noto Serif Thai or Trirong, so this direction is strongest kept Japanese or Chinese (Noto Serif TC).
directions.motion: Entrance: the two strips unroll downward one after the other (clip-path inset from top, 900ms, ease-out expo, 140ms stagger) while characters fade in top to bottom; the arc image eases from scale 1.08 to 1 over 1600ms. Scroll: vertical section headings write in character by character as they enter; the shelf drags horizontally with inertia and the tick pager advances; arc image has 6 percent parallax. Hover: product tile label slides up 4px, arrows nudge 6px. Signature moment: the paper strips hanging themselves over the photograph. Reduced motion: everything static in final state.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Kagetsu-an, a wagashi house founded 1907 in Kanazawa. IA: dated notice line; hero; 'Recommended' horizontal shelf with price, pack sizes and delivery-type tags; 'Standards' vertical-headed grid; a 24 micro-season calendar showing which sweet is made now; wrapping and noshi options; the house story as a two-column vertical essay; shop hours and access; footer with vertical shop name and seal.
directions.photoBrief: One hero macro of a sugar-dusted or translucent confection on white porcelain, soft north-window light, very shallow depth of field, near white-on-white with a single warm tone, shot wide enough to be cropped by a big arc. Five or six square product shots on white seamless at a 45 degree top angle with soft contact shadow (whole plus cut-open showing filling). One gift box flat-lay in ochre. Fallback if no stock fits: draw the sweets in SVG (radial gradients plus feTurbulence sugar grain); wagashi are geometric enough to survive this.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is the clearest current proof that vertical writing can be the structure of a commerce page instead of an ornament, with restraint that reads as inherited rather than styled.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: ukiyo-e-woodblock, bilingual-epigraph, silent-luxury-restraint. Those are a movement pastiche, a quote layout and a Western quiet-luxury grid; this is contemporary Japanese shop grammar where writing-mode vertical-rl, paper strips and an arc crop do the work.
directions.buildRisk: Vertical text looks amateur if punctuation, numerals and long vowels are not handled (needs writing-mode vertical-rl, text-orientation mixed, text-combine-upright for digits) and if the strips are sized by guess rather than by character count. Without a convincing macro image the hero is an empty grey arc; commit early to either a sourced photo or a large CSS-drawn sweet with grain. Keep type small: enlarging the headline destroys the character.

directions.name: Edo Brush-Name Billboard
directions.signature: At scroll 0: a flat cobalt field framed by 1px cream hairlines with a narrow left rail. The performer's name in cream heavy brush lettering runs edge to edge at about 240px high and is physically interrupted by a centred cut-out figure standing in front of it; the romanised name in orange wide grotesque (about 64px, weight 700) is overprinted across the brush name at mid-height; a smaller orange brush role label sits above-left; bottom-right a 220px circular text ring rotates around a brush 'booking' stamp; bottom-left a 9px bold caption block. On 390px the name stacks into two lines behind the figure and the seal stays bottom-right.
directions.grammar: Grid: hairline frame inset 0 with a 94px left rail and an inner column at 270-1265px for text; everything else is poster composition. Type: brush display about 240px vs body 14-16px (15:1), Latin overprint 64px, micro caption 9px with 0.05em tracking, date ticker 16px bold. Colour: cobalt #003F8B, cream #FFFFED, orange #F26A3D, one chartreuse object accent; no gradients. Imagery: one studio cut-out figure with soft floor shadow, later one dark stage photo full-bleed inside the frame. Chrome: next-show ticker row under the hero (date, title, city tag in outlined box). Absent: cards, icons, Latin headline hierarchy.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Shippori Antique and Syne (both Google Fonts), plus custom brush lettering for the name. Free stand-ins for the brush display: Potta One or Dela Gothic One (Japanese), Yuji Boku for a drier brush; Latin overprint Syne 700 or Unbounded. Thai strength is high here: a likay or mor lam performer billboard with the name in Chonburi, Pattaya or Kanit 900, overprinted with Latin in Syne, is a native Thai vernacular (temple-fair signage) and would feel authentic rather than borrowed.
directions.motion: Entrance: the brush name wipes on stroke by stroke left to right behind the figure (mask 1100ms, ease-out quart), the figure rises 24px and settles, the orange Latin types on last. Idle: the circular seal rotates continuously (linear, 18s); the figure has a subtle 2px breathing float. Scroll: text blocks resolve from blur to sharp line by line; the frame hairlines stay fixed while content moves inside. Hover: seal speeds up and the arrow in it flips; ticker row inverts. Signature moment: the name being written behind the performer. Reduced motion: no wipe, seal static.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Katsura Hinode, a rakugo storyteller (or for a Thai build, a mor lam singer 'Bua Thong'). IA: hero billboard; next appearance ticker; a short creed in large type; profile with lineage and awards; repertoire list by title with duration; schedule table by month; press and video; booking via the seal.
directions.photoBrief: One full-figure cut-out of a seated performer in a dark kimono (or stage costume) on a chartreuse cushion, flat studio light, clean alpha edge, soft contact shadow, neutral expression; a second smiling variant for mobile or hover; one dark stage photo with microphone for the second section. Fallback: replace the figure with an SVG still life (cushion, folded fan, hand towel) which keeps the overlap trick.
directions.whyWorldClass: It turns a centuries-old poster lettering tradition into a web hero with three colours and one photo, and it is funny, which almost no luxury-minimal site dares to be.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: festival-lineup-poster, knockout-video-type, mid-century-saul-bass. Those are Western poster systems; this is Edo or temple-fair brush lettering with a figure occluding the type, a bilingual overprint and a rotating seal inside a hairline frame.
directions.buildRisk: Free brush fonts are weaker than custom lettering; at 240px a font like Potta One can look childish. Dodge by converting the name to an SVG path and roughening it (feTurbulence displacement) or choosing Dela Gothic One and leaning on scale and overlap. The figure cut-out is essential to the depth; without a photo use the still-life fallback, never an empty gap.

directions.name: Showa Centenary Progress Index
directions.signature: At scroll 0: cream page ruled by 1px red lines. A 44px red marquee band of script runs across the top; below a news row with a date pill and a pill search field; then the masthead: an arched, heavy condensed two-word wordmark with a roundel between the words, sitting on a giant fat-slab anniversary numeral about 300px tall; left column holds the heritage logo, a gold concentric-ring emblem and a four-item nav stack with a small flat illustration; right column holds a circular 'pick' photo with a speech-bubble tag and a progress counter 'NN/100' in bold Didone numerals. The first row of colour-block cards peeks in at the bottom. On 390px the masthead keeps full width and cards go two-up.
directions.grammar: Grid: full-bleed three equal cells at 1440 (480px each) divided by 1px red rules, two cells at 390. Card anatomy top to bottom: colour block 640px tall holding either a photo with a 14px inset, a geometric pattern or a cartouche-masked photo; pill tag plus date; title 22px bold red, two lines; author and department 14px; a red roundel icon and a serial numeral 96px. Type: masthead numeral about 300px vs body 14-16px (20:1), counter 112px with -0.02em tracking. Colour: cream ground, red for every piece of text and rule, card fields in yellow #F5CF1E, sky #6DB7D3, orange #F08030, gold #B79B4A only for the emblem. Chrome: pill chips with red outline, filled when active; sticky compact header with the tiny masthead. Absent: black text, grey, shadows, rounded cards.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Unna 700 for numerals, Raleway for Latin UI (both Google Fonts), Morisawa Gothic BBB and Midashi Go for Japanese, custom arched lettering. Free stand-ins: Unna and Raleway as is; Japanese Zen Kaku Gothic New 700 or Dela Gothic One; arched wordmark built from Anton or Big Shoulders Display on an SVG warp; fat numeral from Abril Fatface or Bowlby One. Thai strength: a Thai heritage brand centenary (tea, soy sauce, balm) with Chonburi or Kanit 800 headlines and Sriracha for the hand-script notes maps one to one, and Thai retro packaging is a deep well.
directions.motion: Entrance: the arched wordmark drops in letter by letter with a slight overshoot-free settle (700ms, ease-out cubic, 40ms stagger); the anniversary numeral scales up from 0.9; the counter rolls from 00 to its value like an odometer. Idle: top marquee runs linear; the pick bubble wobbles 2 degrees every few seconds. Scroll: cards rise 24px and fade in per row; serial numerals count down as you go deeper; header compacts into a single ruled bar. Hover: card colour block shifts 6px diagonally exposing a red offset, chip fills red. Signature moment: the odometer counter and a thin red progress line filling toward 100. Reduced motion: marquee paused, counters static.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Hoshino Tea Company, 100 years in 2026, publishing 100 stories in its anniversary year. IA: marquee slogan; latest notice; masthead with progress NN/100; category chips (product, content, journal, report); story cells each numbered; 'tea friends' collaborator strip; about the anniversary; contact. The numbered-to-100 structure is the content model.
directions.whyWorldClass: A corporate anniversary site that reads like a beloved tin from a kitchen shelf: one red, heavy lettering, strict ruled cells, and a counter that gives the whole archive a reason to exist.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: cpg-food-brand-bold-color, mid-century-saul-bass, broadsheet-newspaper. Differs by the Showa packaging register, the single-ink red on cream, the ruled three-cell index with serial numerals and the progress-to-100 device.
directions.buildRisk: Falls flat if the masthead is just a font at large size: the arch and the fat numeral need SVG lettering work, and the cards need at least three distinct treatments (pattern, cartouche mask, inset image) or it reads as a generic blog grid. Card images can be flat illustrations or CSS product drawings (carton, can, signboard) so no photography is required. Hold the one-red rule strictly.

directions.name: Walkable Line Atlas
directions.signature: At scroll 0: a white page that is about 85 percent empty. A single ground line made of hand-placed pebble dots crosses the full width at roughly three quarters height; a small hand-drawn figure (about 110px tall, 2px pencil line) is mid-stride on it; the first hand-drawn landmark with a handwritten label is already entering from the right edge so the mechanic reads in a still. Top-left: a tiny dotted mini-map of the route with the current position, a text link and a language toggle. Nothing else. On 390px the line sits at 70 percent height and the figure is centred.
directions.grammar: No grid: one horizon line and absolute placement along it. Type: handwriting face at 15-16px for labels, 58px for the rare chapter title (about 4:1), body leading 1.85, letterspacing 0.01em; UI text 12px grey at 30 percent opacity. Colour: white, graphite #2F302D, pebble greys, one pale watercolour tint per chapter. Imagery: only line drawings as SVG paths with slight wobble. Chrome: almost invisible; a route mini-map of dots replaces navigation. Absent: boxes, buttons, photos, headline hero.
directions.typeStack: Observed: custom 'Ishikawa Klee' handwriting face, Avenir Next and Helvetica Neue for UI. Free stand-ins: Klee One (Google Fonts, the same Klee lineage) for Japanese and Latin, Inter Tight for UI. Thai strength: Mali, Itim or Playpen Sans Thai give the same pencil-note voice and a Thai walker (a monk's umbrella, a vendor's cart) localises naturally.
directions.motion: The page scrolls on the document root; scroll progress drives a horizontal world. Entrance: the pebble line draws itself left to right in 1200ms, then the figure fades in already walking. Scroll: a 6-frame SVG walk cycle advances with scroll delta (direction flips when scrolling up), landmarks slide past at two parallax depths, labels write on with stroke-dashoffset, the mini-map dot advances. Idle: the figure shifts weight and the hat bobs. Hover: landmarks jiggle and reveal a two-line note. Signature moment: the walker stopping at a landmark while its label writes itself. Reduced motion: no walk cycle; chapters become a simple vertical list along a static line.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Mio Hasegawa, an illustrator and map-maker presenting a 'walkable index' of projects. IA is a route, not sections: departure (name and one sentence), six to eight landmarks (each a project with year, medium, a two-line note and a link), a rest stop (about), a postbox (contact), and the end of the road looping back.
directions.whyWorldClass: Radical emptiness with one living line: it makes navigation itself the illustration and is unmistakably Japanese in its use of ma without a single cliche.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: svgmap-journey, game-map-room-nav, scrollytelling-chapter. Those are map or game UI; this is a hand-drawn side-walk on a blank page where the walker is the scrollbar and 85 percent of the viewport stays empty.
directions.buildRisk: The thumbnail can look blank or unfinished: place the first landmark and its handwritten label inside the first viewport and make the pebble line rich (varying dot sizes). The drawing quality is everything; stiff geometric SVG kills it, so add path wobble and uneven stroke. The exemplar is key-driven with no scroll; the factory version must map document scroll to the walk and still keep a sensible vertical fallback on mobile.

directions.name: Run-In Manifesto with Lettering Sticker
directions.signature: At scroll 0: white page, a single run-in paragraph at 30px/42px fills the viewport from margin to margin with no breaks; every project name inside it is an outlined pill (1.5px border, full radius) and every new thought starts with a small circular numeral glyph in the second script. Over the centre of the text sits a huge black lettering piece in the non-Latin script (about 700px wide) with diamond dots, a white keyline and thin construction rectangles, slightly covering the words. Top and bottom edges carry three nav words each on a hairline. A round badge is pinned bottom-right. On 390px the text drops to 20px and the same composition holds.
directions.grammar: Grid: none beyond 24px page margins and three equal nav cells top and bottom (items left-aligned at 0, 33 and 66 percent). Type: one size for everything (30px, weight 500, leading 1.4), brand name in 700; the only scale contrast is the lettering piece at about 20 times body. Colour: pure black on pure white, nothing else. Imagery: none; the lettering is the image. Chrome: hairlines under the top nav and over the bottom nav, both fixed while the paragraph scrolls between them. Absent: headings, sections, images, cards, footer, colour.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Suisse Intl 500 for the paragraph, a custom 'Mustaqel' font for the numeral glyph, hand-drawn Arabic lettering as vector. Free stand-ins: Switzer or General Sans (Fontshare) or Inter Tight 500 for the paragraph; lettering drawn as SVG from Aref Ruqaa Ink, Rakkas or Reem Kufi with added diamond dots and construction lines. Thai strength: very high. A Thai studio manifesto in Anuphan or IBM Plex Sans Thai 500 with a giant Thai lettering sticker (built from Chonburi or custom SVG) and a circled Thai numeral as bullet works bilingual EN/TH in the same paragraph.
directions.motion: Entrance: the paragraph types in word by word at reading speed for the first three lines then the rest fades up (600ms); the lettering sticker drops with a 4 degree rotation and settles (800ms, ease-out back kept under 1.05). Idle: the round badge rotates slowly. Scroll: text scrolls under the fixed nav rails; the sticker lags at 0.85 speed so it slides across different lines. Hover: a pill inverts to black and a 240px project thumbnail (CSS-drawn poster) follows the cursor; the sticker is draggable and shows its construction boxes while dragged. Signature moment: dragging the lettering piece across the manifesto. Reduced motion: no type-in, sticker static, hover thumbnail appears without movement.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Daftar Studio, an independent bilingual design studio and small press. IA is one paragraph: who we are, what we believe, clients as inline pills grouped by discipline (identity, editorial, art direction, digital), the publication, the print shop, how to reach us; six nav words (Home, Work, Contact, About, Publication, Shop) on the two rails. Scrolling past the paragraph reveals a plain index table of the same pills.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is the most confident non-Western studio statement seen in this survey: the site is literally a manifesto you can click, and the calligraphic piece asserts the Arabic voice over a Swiss paragraph instead of beside it.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: manifesto-essay, readme-manifesto, editorial-index. Those are structured essays or lists; this is a single unbroken run-in paragraph used as navigation, with inline pills and an oversized draggable script lettering sticker, plus nav rails at both edges.
directions.buildRisk: The lettering piece decides everything: plain font text at large size will look like a watermark. Build it as SVG with diamond dots, keyline and construction boxes. The paragraph must be real, well-written copy long enough to fill 1440x900 and 390 tall screens; lorem ipsum or short copy collapses the idea. Keep one size; any added heading ruins it.

directions.name: Bi-Script Specimen Bands
directions.signature: At scroll 0: a 60px white nav row, then a white band with a typeface name in weight-100 Latin capitals so large (about 250px) that it runs off both edges; a thick dashed rule; then a hot pink band filling the rest of the viewport with four or five Thai characters in weight 900 at about 400px, cropped by the band edges, and a diagonal acid-green band crossing the lower right with a second Thai word rotated about 30 degrees. Small light text at the bottom-left lists the scripts covered. On 390px only two or three letter fragments fit, on cyan, which is the point.
directions.grammar: Grid: full-bleed bands, no container; below them a three-column card grid with 90px side margins and 18px gaps, cards 408x510 with 16px radius and 22px padding. Type: display 250-400px vs body 18px/27px (about 20:1), nav 12px weight 600, card kicker 12px, card title 28px weight 700. Colour: white, black, hot pink #FA0050, acid green #5CFF5C, cyan #00D8FF, cream #FFF3C4; each band exactly one flat colour. Imagery: none; glyphs are the image, including outlined echo stacks and keyboard-key grids. Chrome: nav centred as seven plain words, search icon right. Absent: photos, gradients, body copy above the fold.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Graphik TH and Graphik Thai Loop (Cadson Demak, commercial), 29LT Bukra and Zarid, Greta Sans (TPTQ). Free stand-ins: Thai display Kanit 900, Noto Sans Thai 900 or Prompt 900; hairline Latin Sofia Sans Extra Condensed 100 or Encode Sans Condensed 100; body IBM Plex Sans Thai. A real feature to build: a Loopless/Looped toggle switching IBM Plex Sans Thai and IBM Plex Sans Thai Looped (or Noto Sans Thai and Noto Sans Thai Looped), mirroring the 29LT three-segment style switch. Thai-script typography is the entire point of this direction: strongest Thai fit in the lens.
directions.motion: Entrance: the hairline name slides in from the right as a slow marquee and parks; the pink band wipes up; glyphs scale from 1.15 to 1 with a 60ms stagger; the green diagonal band swings in from the corner (700ms, ease-out expo). Idle: the hairline name drifts linearly. Scroll: each band is sticky for half a viewport while its glyphs cross-fade through weights (variable axis scrub) and the band colour hard-cuts to the next; cards rise in rows. Hover: card posters animate their own type (outline to solid fill, key caps press). Micro: the style toggle swaps the font with a 120ms cross-fade; a live type-tester line is editable. Signature moment: scrubbing a Thai word from weight 100 to 900 with scroll. Reduced motion: static bands, toggle still works.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Rueang Type, a Bangkok foundry for Thai, Lao and Latin. IA: nav (Type, Custom, Thoughts, Activity, Goods, Contact); three specimen bands (one family each with script coverage and style toggle); an editable tester; article cards mixing Type and Thought pieces with bylines; custom-font case list for brands; footer with licence tiers.
directions.whyWorldClass: It shows Thai (and Arabic) letterforms at a scale and confidence usually reserved for Latin grotesques, and treats script coverage as the brand, which is exactly what world-class regional foundries do in 2026.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: specimen-lab, variable-font-axis-playground, swiss-poster. Those are Latin specimen or axis demos on neutral grounds; this is script-first (Thai primary, Latin as hairline counterpoint), flat acid colour bands with diagonal cuts and extreme cropping, plus looped versus loopless as the interactive axis.
directions.buildRisk: Free Thai fonts at 400px expose poor outlines and clumsy vowel and tone-mark stacking; test the exact words (choose ones with stacked marks for drama but check clipping at band edges, line-height at least 1.5 for the glyph box). Without commercial faces the bands can look like a generic colour-block page; the diagonal band, dashed cut line and brutal cropping are what make it specific. Variable weight scrub needs a variable Thai font (Noto Sans Thai, Anuphan).

directions.name: Split-Pane Poster Archive
directions.signature: At scroll 0: a #131313 page divided by a thin vertical double line at two thirds width. Left pane: a top row with the studio name in caps, a language toggle and the email, all the same size; a second row of filter words where only the active one is white; a search line, a year select and a result count; then three posters of different heights aligned on a common bottom edge, in acid yellow, cobalt, red and green, each with a one-line title and flat colour tag chips. Right pane: Contact, Profile, Client tabs, a paragraph in the second script, four label and value rows and the start of an underline-only form. On 390px the right pane collapses behind a plus icon and posters go two-up.
directions.grammar: Grid: two panes (66/34) with 10px padding, hairlines #3A3A3A under every row; left pane masonry of three columns with 10px gaps, items bottom-aligned per row. Type: a single size (21px, weight 400, tight leading 1.2) for nav, body and titles; only chips (13px) and the result count (14px) are smaller. Active is #E2E2E2, inactive #6B6B6B. Colour: near-black chrome, all colour comes from posters and chips (#39FF14, #FFE94A, #8C8CFF, #FF9BD2, #7FE7FF with black text, 3px radius). Imagery: posters only, never photos of people or spaces on the index. Chrome: grid/list toggle, draggable pane divider, underline inputs. Absent: hero, big headline, hover overlays, rounded cards.
directions.typeStack: Observed: custom EP Sans and EP Gothic (Everyday Practice), Calibre with Orpheus Pro (Ordinary People), Diatype Semi-Mono (Wang Zhi-Hong). Free stand-ins: Switzer or General Sans (Fontshare) or Inter Tight at 21px; Hangul via Pretendard (OFL, jsDelivr) or Noto Sans KR; for a Thai build Anuphan or IBM Plex Sans Thai at the same single size, which suits Thai well because it needs no display face.
directions.motion: Entrance: rows draw their hairlines left to right (400ms), then posters rise from the baseline one by one (500ms, ease-out cubic, 70ms stagger) so the bottom-aligned edge is felt. Scroll: the left pane scrolls with the document while the right pane is sticky; the result count ticks as filters change. Micro: clicking a filter word re-flows the masonry with a FLIP transition (350ms); grid to list toggle morphs posters into 48px rows with title, year and chips; dragging the divider resizes both panes live; form underlines thicken on focus. Each poster has its own tiny loop (a blob wobble, a stripe shift) only on hover. Signature moment: the filter re-flow where posters slide to new columns and re-align on their bottom edge. Reduced motion: instant re-flow, no poster loops.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Botong Practice, a small graphic design collective. IA: left = archive (types: Graphic, Editorial, Website, Identity, Space, Motion, Press, Everyday; search; year; count; posters with title and chips; list view). Right = Contact (bilingual intro, address, email, tel, social, enquiry form with title, description, name, budget), Profile (members, awards, exhibitions as a dated list), Client (plain alphabetical list). No separate about or contact page: the pane is the site.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is a studio site that behaves like a tool and trusts the work to be the only spectacle: one type size, real filtering over a thousand items, and the Seoul poster avant-garde supplying all the colour.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: split-master-detail, cmd-k-portfolio, bento. Those are product UI patterns; this is a Korean studio archive with a single-size type system, bottom-aligned poster masonry, flat acid tag chips and a permanent bilingual contact pane with a draggable divider.
directions.buildRisk: The posters must be good. Twelve to sixteen CSS or SVG generated posters with genuinely different systems (stripes, blobs, type-only, dot grids, chrome shapes) are needed; weak or repetitive posters make it a dark card grid. Resist adding a headline. Mixed-script line-height needs tuning so Hangul or Thai and Latin share one baseline rhythm at 21px.

directions.name: Ma Interval Festival Strip
directions.signature: At scroll 0: white page. A band of seven small grayscale tiles (about 207x276, 16px gaps) runs across the viewport at mid-height and off both edges; in the centre one tile is blown up to a 640x852 colour portrait that overlaps the band and almost touches the top and bottom of the viewport. The tiles show the same quiet object study in variations. Corners carry the only text: festival logo and year top-left; an inverse-video button and a mono menu label top-right; venue and date in mono bottom-left; a two-line bilingual theme bottom-right; a small black pill with a revision date bottom-centre. On 390px the big tile is 86 percent wide and the strip peeks out left and right behind it.
directions.grammar: Grid: 32px margins; hero is strip plus one overlapping tile; content sits in the right 60 percent column (starting at 512px) with a blank left 35 percent. Type: mono 16px weight 300 with 32px leading for everything, labels in bold gothic 16px, logo about 40px; no display size at all (hierarchy by position and emptiness). Colour: white, black, the hero tile's tan #C9AE98 and concrete grey; revision pill text in lilac #B9B4FF on black. Imagery: one object-study series, grayscale except the active one. Chrome: inverse-video rectangles for the two actions, dotted underlines for links. Absent: headline, colour UI, icons, cards, rounded corners (except the pill).
directions.typeStack: Observed: custom FPMono, Morisawa Gothic BBB and Futo Go B101, Shuei Yobu Mincho, a grotesque logo with custom joins. Free stand-ins: Geist Mono or JetBrains Mono 300 for Latin and numerals, Zen Kaku Gothic New 500/700 for Japanese, Zen Old Mincho for the theme line, logo in Inter Tight with two custom ligatures drawn in SVG.
