Thai: IBM Plex Sans Thai with IBM Plex Mono keeps the same engineered calm; a bilingual EN/TH theme line bottom-right works directly.
directions.motion: Entrance: the strip slides in from the right and decelerates (1400ms, ease-out expo); the centre tile grows from strip size to full height (900ms) while turning from grayscale to colour. Idle: the strip advances one tile every 4 seconds; each time, the next tile enlarges through the centre slot and the previous shrinks back and desaturates. Scroll: the big tile shrinks back into the strip and the strip docks under the header as a 60px ribbon; definition rows draw their hairline then reveal label and value. Hover: tiles lift 4px and show a mono caption; inverse buttons flip to outline. Signature moment: the tile passing through the centre slot, growing and gaining colour. Reduced motion: no auto-advance, static centre tile.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Aida Design Fair 2026, a three-day design festival whose theme is 'the interval where things take shape'. IA: hero strip; theme statement (bilingual); outline as definition list (name, dates and hours per day, venue with address, admission tiers); programme by day in mono table; exhibitors as a plain two-column list; access; a visible changelog ('Revision: date') listing what changed on the site, which is the pill's target.
directions.whyWorldClass: A festival site with no headline that still communicates its theme instantly: the enlarged tile inside the strip is 'ma' made literal, and the revision pill and mono definition list show a level of editorial honesty rare anywhere.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: conference-schedule-grid, native-carousel-filmstrip, coverflow-3d. Differs by the flat strip with one overlapping enlarged tile, corner-only typography in mono, a definition-list outline in an off-centre column and a public revision pill.
directions.buildRisk: The object study carries the page. Seven variations of a stacked-blocks-and-plant still life must be drawn convincingly in CSS or SVG (isometric concrete cubes with subtle noise, a simple potted plant) or sourced as a consistent photo series; clip-art objects will sink it. Keep all text at 16px; the temptation to add a big title must be refused.

directions.name: Four-Side Marquee Packaging World
directions.signature: At scroll 0: the viewport is a label. A 30px dark frame on all four sides carries one continuous marquee of brand phrases and tiny icons that travels clockwise. Inside, on flat vermilion, the brand name in two giant modular block glyphs fills the upper half in sand gold with the Latin name in wide-tracked caps across the lower half; a 300px enamel coin with an embossed crest spins slowly at centre; a column of outlined warning-triangle icons and a vertical capsule of outlined caps sit on the right; a rounded-rectangle inset bottom-left shows the product texture next to a black modular sub-logo. On 390px the two glyphs stack vertically, the coin sits between them and the frame marquee remains.
directions.grammar: Grid: a fixed frame (30px) and a layered poster inside it; content sections below reuse the same ground with 300px side insets for copy. Type: block glyphs about 480px, Latin caps 180px with 0.15em tracking, body 30px bold in gold with 1.6 leading (CJK), frame marquee 14px bold caps. Colour: vermilion #E63A00, sand gold #D2A873, maroon #751717, one hot pink only on the 3D charms. Imagery: 3D objects (coin, charms), icon triangles, one food texture inset; a plated dish photo appears on scroll. Chrome: a round 'TOP' plate button; no visible nav bar. Absent: white space, grey, thin type, conventional header.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Noto Sans TC 700, Myriad Pro (condensed to semi-extended), Ubuntu Sans, custom modular logotype. Free stand-ins: Noto Sans TC 900 for copy; the modular glyphs built on a CSS grid of squares or drawn as SVG; Latin caps in Archivo (width axis 125) or Unbounded; marquee in Archivo Narrow 700. Thai strength: high. A Thai curry paste or street-food brand with squared Thai lettering in Chakra Petch 700 or a custom block alphabet, plus Thai warning-label humour, lands naturally and is a register the library's Thai set (gilding, benjarong, stele) does not cover.
directions.motion: Idle: the frame marquee travels clockwise continuously (linear, about 40s per lap); the coin spins on its Y axis with a specular sweep; the charms bob out of phase. Entrance: block glyphs assemble square by square (grid cells flip in, 20ms stagger), then the coin drops and rings like a struck coin (damped rotation). Scroll: the coin tilts with scroll velocity; a plate slides in from the top over it; warning triangles flip one by one; background glyphs swap to the next pair. Hover: triangles shake, the coin flips to its reverse face. Signature moment: the clockwise four-side marquee with the coin spinning inside it. Reduced motion: marquee and coin static, glyphs pre-assembled.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Hong Yun Curry Works, a curry sauce maker with a shop and a 'lab' line. IA: label hero; what it is (three sentences, big); heat levels as warning-triangle scale; the sauces as product stickers with spice notes; shop and hours as a ticket stub; 'lab' experiments list; stockists; footer as the back of the pack (ingredients-style small print).
directions.whyWorldClass: Maximalism with discipline: two inks, one frame device and lettering built from a module, so the chaos reads as a designed pack rather than hyperpop noise. It is the best Taiwanese street-packaging-to-web translation in the survey.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: cpg-food-brand-bold-color, hyperpop-chromatic-overload, la-carta-restaurant-character. Differs by the four-side travelling frame marquee, modular block-glyph lettering, enamel coin and charm objects and the strict two-ink palette.
directions.buildRisk: The exemplar uses canvas 3D; the coin and charms can be done with CSS 3D transforms and layered gradients, but a flat disc will look cheap, so give the coin thickness (stacked layers), an embossed SVG crest and a moving highlight. The side marquees need writing-mode or rotated tracks synced so the text reads as one loop. On mobile the frame eats width: reduce to 22px. Too many decorative icons becomes noise; cap at one column.

directions.name: Entwined Bilingual Exhibition Lockup
directions.signature: At scroll 0: under a white header whose nav items are two-line labels (second script above, Latin caps below), a full-width field in muted sage carries an organic procedural pattern in coral. Over it, the exhibition title appears twice, once per script, deliberately interlaced: Latin unicase serif words and the second script's calligraphic words alternate line by line and overlap, both in one slate ink; where pattern and letters intersect the letters switch to red (mix-blend). A black caption slab centred on the bottom edge states the title, dates and venue with a row of hollow dots. Curator credits sit bottom-right in both scripts. On 390px the lockup stacks to five lines and the slab becomes full width.
directions.grammar: Grid: header 140px with logo left and seven nav cells justified across; hero 620px tall full-bleed; below, a two-column then four-column image grid with 30px gutters and bold 18px captions. Type: lockup words about 110px (Latin) and about 130px (second script) vs body 18px/28.8px (about 6:1); nav 18px bold; caption slab 20px light. Colour: sage #C9D2CC, coral #F7B3A3, slate #5A6B7A, red #E0453A at overlaps, black slab, white page. Imagery: the lockup is the image; venues appear lower as photographs. Chrome: stacked bilingual nav labels, a flat yellow or black action button, language switch as a word in the other script. Absent: slider arrows as decoration, gradients, uppercase tracking on the non-Latin script.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Greta Text Arabic and Graphik (Art Jameel), DIN Next and DIN Next Arabic (Qatar Museums), custom calligraphy for the title. Free stand-ins: Latin lockup in Cormorant Unicase or Bodoni Moda with SVG swashes; Arabic in Aref Ruqaa or Gulzar; UI in Hanken Grotesk with IBM Plex Sans Arabic. Thai strength: high for the owner. A Thai and English exhibition lockup (Thai in Trirong or Noto Serif Thai, with Charm for a brush line) with two-line TH over EN nav labels is a direct and under-used bilingual pattern; unlike Arabic there is no RTL mirroring to manage.
directions.motion: Entrance: the pattern grows outward like coral (SVG mask or canvas reaction front, 1800ms), the two scripts write on alternately line by line (stroke reveal 500ms each, ease-in-out), and the red overlap colour blooms last. Idle: the pattern drifts slowly so the red overlaps travel through the letters. Scroll: the lockup parallaxes at 0.9 and the slab sticks as a compact title bar; grid captions fade up. Hover: nav labels swap emphasis between the two scripts (the top line goes bold); pager dots fill. Language switch performs a mirrored re-layout with a 300ms cross-fade. Signature moment: red overlaps migrating through the interlaced bilingual title. Reduced motion: pattern static, lockup shown complete.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Dar Al Bahr Arts Centre presenting the exhibition 'Salt Wind, Tide Rooms'. IA: stacked bilingual nav (Visit, What's On, Collection, Learning, Stories); exhibition hero lockup with dates; curatorial paragraph in two parallel columns (one per script, equal weight); artists list; public programme by date; visit info; other venues as large captioned images; newsletter.
directions.whyWorldClass: It treats two scripts as one drawing instead of a translation pair, and uses colour interaction between pattern and letter to make the lockup feel alive: the most sophisticated bilingual gesture seen in the Gulf institutional sites.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: bilingual-epigraph, museum-collection-explorer, svg-paint-order-poster. Differs by interlacing the scripts into a single title lockup over a moving pattern with blend-driven colour change, and by stacked two-script navigation labels.
directions.buildRisk: Font-set Arabic or Thai next to a swashy Latin will look like two unrelated lines unless the lockup is composed by hand: fix line breaks, overlap offsets and add drawn swashes in SVG. The blend effect needs a solid fallback colour (mix-blend-mode on text over SVG can fail in screenshots; pre-compute overlap with clip-path or duplicate layers). If Arabic is used, set dir=rtl only on that script's elements and never letter-space it.

directions.name: Overflow Ledger Index
directions.signature: At scroll=0 the viewport is a ledger: 9 to 10 rows of sentence-case medium grotesk at 6.6vw (95px at 1440) on 0.83 leading, each row starting with its content type ('Product', 'Press', 'Campaign') and deliberately running past the right edge with no wrap and no ellipsis. To the left, a 250px rail of 12px label/value pairs per row, values wrapped in square brackets and coloured link blue. Above, one line of '[ ]' text checkboxes; top bar in one saturated blue with the active tab notched out in white.
directions.grammar: Two columns only: 250px meta rail and a fluid title column; 16px outer margin, zero gap between rows so descenders touch the next cap line. One family, two sizes, ratio 8:1 (95px weight 500 vs 12px weight 400, meta leading 1.25). Palette: white, black, one RGB blue (about #1a00ff) shared by header bar and link values. No images at desktop scroll=0 (they arrive as a thumbnail strip under a hovered row; on mobile as a strip above each title). Chrome is typographic syntax: brackets, checkboxes, file extensions as filters. Absent: cards, icons, rules between rows, rounded corners (except the one tab notch), hero, footer blocks.
directions.typeStack: Observed: SBM (custom neo-grotesk, Visual Society), MSCHF Sans Mono, Archivo Narrow (lament.tv). Free stand-ins: Switzer 500/400 (Fontshare) or Inter Tight 500 (Google) for the ledger; DM Mono for a mono variant; Archivo Narrow is itself on Google Fonts.
directions.motion: Entrance: rows appear top-down as instant line sets, 40ms stagger, steps() timing, meta rail a beat later. Scroll: native; header and filter line sticky. Hover: the row inverts to a full-bleed blue band and its clipped title slides left linearly until its end is revealed (speed proportional to overflow), while a 96px-tall thumbnail strip unfolds under the row. Filter click: '[ ]' flips to '[x]', non-matching rows collapse to zero height in 120ms linear and the ledger restacks. Signature moment: the overflow marquee on hover. Reduced motion: no marquee, the title wraps on focus instead.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Halde Verein, a Zurich collective that runs an archive and shop in one list. IA: filter line (Statement, Product, Catalogue, Campaign, Press, Event, Research, .jpg, .mp4, .pdf) -> ledger of about 40 mixed entries (products with category, price and Add to cart; press with outlet and year; events with location) -> inline expanded entry (image strip plus two paragraphs) -> colophon rows (About, Stockists, Imprint) in the same ledger format.
directions.whyWorldClass: It turns a database into a poster without styling anything: the hierarchy is carried entirely by one 8:1 scale jump and a syntax, and the overflow says 'this archive is bigger than your screen' more convincingly than any hero image.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: editorial-index, swiss-international-typographic, stdout, mass-changelog-scroll-map. Differs by the intentional right-edge overflow at display size, the micro bracketed-link rail, and filters written as text checkboxes; no grid of columns, no terminal pastiche.
directions.buildRisk: Falls flat if rows wrap, get an ellipsis, or the rail grows above 13px: then it is a generic big list. Clip overflow on a wrapper (not the root) so the document never scrolls sideways at 390px; on mobile keep titles around 40px still overflowing with a 4-image strip above each. Resist adding images at scroll=0.

directions.name: Stretched Slab Navigation
directions.signature: The viewport is a margin-less 2-column grid in which two navigation words are each fitted to their cell by independent horizontal and vertical scaling, so the letters become grotesquely tall or wide black slabs touching all four edges; a single 16:9 media tile with a 12px radius occupies the one remaining cell (top-left). Nothing else is on screen.
directions.grammar: Grid: 2 columns, the left split into two rows; 8px outer padding, 0 gutters. Type: one extended bold grotesk, black on white, scaled per cell (aspect distortion from roughly 0.4x to 2.5x); secondary text is 11-12px and sparse. Colour: white, black, plus whatever the media tile brings. Navigation is the composition: there is no header, logo or menu. Below the fold each section title repeats the trick at a different column ratio. Absent: margins, body copy at scroll=0, icons, buttons.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Akzidenz-Grotesk BQ Extended Bold; Franklin-style condensed gothic plus Helvetica Neue Bold (Special Offer); custom slab logotype (PIN-UP). Free stand-ins: Archivo (Google, width axis 62-125) at wdth 125 weight 800-900 for the slabs; Antonio or Archivo Narrow for the letter-spaced variant; Inter for 12px labels.
directions.motion: Entrance: each word grows from its baseline (scaleY 0 to fit) over 500ms ease-out, 60ms stagger per letter. Pointer X continuously redistributes the two column widths (lerp 0.12) so the letters stretch and squeeze live. Click a word: its cell expands to full width in 400ms cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1) while the other compresses to a 40px sliver that stays clickable; content appears inside the expanded cell. Scroll: section title slabs squash vertically into 48px sticky strips. Signature moment: the live stretch-and-squeeze under the cursor. Reduced motion: fixed 50/50 split, instant swaps.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Okapi Grade, a Berlin colourist and finishing studio. IA: slab nav (WORK / ABOUT) with the showreel tile -> WORK expanded: 12 films as squashed word-rows with director and year -> ABOUT: three short paragraphs at 20px, client list in 12px -> a final stretched word CALL as the contact link.
directions.whyWorldClass: It breaks the oldest rule in typography (never distort letterforms) with total commitment and makes it functional: the distortion is literally the layout system, and the navigation is the only image the page needs.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: variable-font-pressure, kinetic-broken-grid, poster-crop, inflatable-balloon-type-hero. None uses non-uniform scaling bound to grid tracks where the stretched words are the navigation and the whole page.
directions.buildRisk: Fit-to-cell must be exact or it looks like a bug: use inline SVG text with preserveAspectRatio none (or measure after document.fonts.ready and apply transforms), and re-fit on resize. The scroll=0 thumbnail must be taken after fitting. One factory video loop is enough for the tile. At 390px stack the two words vertically at 50vh each with the tile inset between them.

directions.name: Roster Woven Paragraph
directions.signature: A single fully justified paragraph set at 3.5vw (50px at 1440) fills the viewport edge to edge, about 15 lines, in which a manifesto in light weight and the alphabetical roster of names in medium weight are woven sentence by sentence. Above it, the only chrome: a 39px table row of five bordered cells.
directions.grammar: One text block, 10px side margins, leading 1.15, justified with real hyphenation so word gaps vary visibly. Two weights of one grotesk (300 and 500), no size change anywhere in the block. Background a flat light grey (#f0f0f0), text black. Nav as a literal table: 1px borders, cells at 1/6, 1/6, 1/3, 1/6, 1/6, 16px labels, brand bold. Imagery is absent until hover. Absent: headings, lists, columns, buttons, footer.
directions.typeStack: Observed: ABC Monument Grotesk Light and Medium. Free stand-ins: Host Grotesk 300/500 (Google) or Switzer 300/500 (Fontshare); a variable face is preferable so the bleed-in can animate weight.
directions.motion: Entrance: lines set in from top with variable weight rising from 100 to 300 and a 6px blur clearing, 900ms total, 45ms per line. Hover a name: all prose drops to 15% opacity within 150ms while every name stays black, so the roster appears as a constellation, and a muted full-bleed still or loop of that person's film fades in behind. Click: the paragraph parts at that name and the project list is inserted as further sentences. Scroll: native, the nav row sticky. Signature moment: prose dimming to leave only names. Reduced motion: no blur or weight animation, opacity changes are instant.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Halloran and Vey, a film production company representing 28 directors. IA: table nav (Projects, Directors, brand, Film and TV, Contact) -> woven paragraph (manifesto plus roster) -> second paragraph listing selected projects with years in tabular figures -> contact details as the closing sentence at the same size.
directions.whyWorldClass: It collapses two pages (about and roster) into one piece of writing and trusts copy as the interface; the craft is in the weights, the justification and the edit, which is exactly what templates cannot fake.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: manifesto-essay, readme-manifesto, has-relational-reveal, text-clip-reveal. Differs: the index and the manifesto are the same justified text at one size; navigation happens inside prose, not beside it.
directions.buildRisk: Justified display text produces rivers and stretched last lines: set hyphens auto with a lang attribute, add soft hyphens by hand, and tune text-align-last. The static thumbnail depends on weight contrast, so use 300 vs 500 or 600. Copy quality is the design: write a real, strange, edited manifesto. At 390px keep it justified at about 26px.

directions.name: Browser Default Couture
directions.signature: Top centre: a 13 to 16px Times bio typeset by hand into a figure (a stepped diagonal that forks into two legs), built with indents and gaps, not an image. Under it a contact line with pipes, two rows of native grey-bordered buttons, then a centred column of thirty default-blue underlined links with a year column pinned hard left at the viewport edge. White page, no logo, no header.
directions.grammar: No grid: one centre axis plus a left-edge year rail at 16px. Type at browser scale (13 to 16px Times, 1.1 leading); the largest thing on the page is whitespace. Colours are the user-agent defaults used on purpose: #0000ee links, #551a8b visited, black text, white ground; a variant sets everything in one odd colour (BLESS beige). Controls are unstyled native buttons and selects. Exactly one authored glyph (the arrow). Absent: web fonts as display, images, cards, hover styling, footer.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Times New Roman, Arial Narrow, Helvetica Neue, plus custom remixes of system fonts (Werkplaats). Free stand-ins: Tinos (Google, metric-compatible Times) to pin metrics across OS; Archivo Narrow for the Arial Narrow variant; Arimo for Helvetica.
directions.motion: Stillness is the luxury; motion is typesetting, not animation. Entrance: the shaped bio sets line by line (30ms per line, no easing), then links appear in document order. Filter change: the bio re-indents into a different silhouette in six discrete steps over 250ms (ch-unit indents), list rows that do not match are removed instantly. Hover a link: a 120px image appears at the cursor with no transition; clicked links stay visited-purple (persisted locally). Scroll: year rail sticks per year group. Signature moment: the paragraph re-shaping itself. Reduced motion: everything static, changes instant.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Maren Oyelaran, fashion historian, editor and writer. IA: shaped bio -> contact line (email, two links) -> native filter buttons by format (Essay, Speaking, Editing, Journalism) and subject (Fashion, Art, Culture, Design, History) -> chronological list of about 60 writings with year rail and outbound arrows -> closing line 'Last edited by hand' with date.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is the web equivalent of an unlined, hand-finished garment: refusing styling is the styling, and the one concrete-poetry gesture proves every default was chosen. It also loads instantly and will never date.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: manpage, readme-manifesto, stdout, mono-ink-restraint. Those are terminal or developer pastiches or polished minimalism; this uses real browser defaults (Times, link blue, native controls) with a hand-shaped paragraph as the single signature.
directions.buildRisk: A judge may read the thumbnail as an unstyled or broken page. The shape must be unmistakably deliberate and elegant, the centre axis exact, the year rail crisp. Build the shape with non-breaking spaces or per-line ch indents and re-author it for 390px instead of letting it wrap. Load Tinos so metrics do not shift between macOS and Linux capture.

directions.name: Spreadsheet Cell Exhibition
directions.signature: The whole viewport is a live spreadsheet: pale grey cells with hairline gridlines, numbered rows, a names column, italic section rows with a pastel swatch cell, and 40-odd tiny images each squashed to exactly one 80x19px cell and scattered horizontally across the sheet like a scatter plot. Title and dates sit in row 1 and 2 as ordinary cell text; links are default blue.
directions.grammar: Grid is literal: 18 columns of 80px, rows of 19px, 1px #c8c8c8 lines, first column 40px for row numbers. One size of Helvetica-style text (15px on 19px), italic for section rows, blue for links. Colour: #ededed, black, link blue, two pastel swatches. Images are data: distorted to cell aspect at rest, true aspect when opened. Chrome borrowed from spreadsheets (frozen header rows, cell cursor, sheet tabs) but drawn flat with no skeuomorphism. Absent: hero, cards, margins, headings.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Helvetica Neue / Helvetica system stack. Free stand-in: Arimo (Google) or the system sans stack; no display face at all.
directions.motion: Entrance: gridlines draw, then cells fill row by row at 15ms per row. A 2px cell cursor follows pointer and arrow keys. Hover a name row: the row gets a selection outline and its squashed thumbnail expands in place to a merged 6x12-cell image at true aspect (160ms ease-out), overlaying neighbours. Click: rows are inserted beneath with the project text typed into cells. A formula bar at the top echoes the hovered cell. Scroll: rows 1 and 2 and columns A and B stay frozen. Signature moment: a one-cell smear of colour un-squashing into a picture. Reduced motion: no fill sequence, expansions instant.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Lindhagen School of Craft, Degree Show 2026. IA: frozen header (show title, dates, venue, Info, Press, Sponsors, language) -> row groups Form (11 students), Visual Communication (16), Fashion (22) -> expanded row as student project (statement, three images, contact) -> sheet tabs at the bottom as page nav (Students, Programme, Visit).
directions.whyWorldClass: It takes the most boring software surface there is and makes it the exhibition design, with one perverse, memorable move (pictures as squashed cell data). Fully systematic, instantly legible, and funny without a single joke element.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: spec-table-hero, conference-schedule-grid, notion-blocks and bloomberg-data (admin styles). None uses the spreadsheet itself as the gallery surface with images stored as cells; this is a public showcase page, not a dashboard.
directions.buildRisk: Without the scattered squashed thumbnails it reads as a plain data table. Thumbnails can be small procedural compositions (CSS gradients, SVG shapes) but need real variety; a small stock pack of craft objects would lift it. Keep horizontal panning inside a wrapper so the root does not overflow at 390px; show columns A and B frozen plus about three data columns on mobile.

directions.name: Sticky Mega-Nav with Dashed Feed
directions.signature: The left half of the viewport is permanently the menu: five words stacked at 11.4vw (164px), tracked -0.09em on 0.76 leading so they fuse into one black mass. The right half is a scrolling stack of dashed-outline rounded boxes, each starting with a headline at the same giant size and continuing in 11px monospace. A scrawled, hand-drawn outline logo sits top-left as the only non-typographic mark.
directions.grammar: 50/50 split, 16px outer margin, 12px between boxes, box padding 12px. Type ratio 15:1 (164px display vs 11px mono) with nothing in between. Display: medium-weight neo-grotesk, extreme negative tracking, sentence case. Body: mono, underlined links, italics for titles of works. Colour: black on white only. Borders: 1px dashed, small radius: the only 'UI' feeling element. Absent: images at scroll=0, colour, icons, a header bar, any mid-size heading.
directions.typeStack: Observed: custom display grotesk (Neue Haas-like, medium) and a custom mono with rounded parentheses. Free stand-ins: Inter Tight 500 at -0.09em (Google) or Switzer 500 (Fontshare) for display; Sometype Mono or JetBrains Mono 400 with true italics for body.
directions.motion: Left nav is sticky; the right column scrolls natively. Entrance: nav words arrive one per 80ms from the left edge with a hard stop (no overshoot); boxes draw their dashed outline (stroke-dashoffset) then fill with text. Scroll-linked: each box headline relaxes tracking from -0.14em to -0.09em as it enters; boxes stick and stack with 12px offsets like index cards. Hover a nav word: the other four switch to outline (text-stroke) and the feed filters. Signature moment: the card stack accumulating against the immovable giant menu. Reduced motion: no tracking animation, no outline draw.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Compagnie Mistral, a national choreographic centre. IA: giant nav (News, Works, Artists, Agenda, Search) -> feed boxes: directors' statement, current creation, associate artist, studio residency, tour dates as a mono table, newsletter -> final box with partners and legal in mono.
directions.whyWorldClass: An institution site with zero imagery above the fold that still feels physical and loud: two materials only (fused display type, typewriter text) and one border style, held with complete discipline across desktop and mobile.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: soft-brutalism, kinetic-broken-grid, split-master-detail. Differs: the navigation permanently occupies half the page at display size, the content lives in dashed boxes set in 11px mono, and the scale ratio is 15:1 with no intermediate sizes.
directions.buildRisk: The five words must be tuned so the longest fits the half width at 1440 and at 390 (stacked at about 20vw). Tracking this tight needs kerning checks pair by pair. Without the dashed boxes, mono body and scrawled logo it becomes generic big-type brutalism. Draw the logo as an inline SVG path with a hand wobble.

directions.name: Parenthesis Numeral Bands

exemplars.observed: Episodes stacked as full-bleed flat colour bands (yellow, ochre, cobalt, grey-sage, vermilion), each about 335px tall with a 260px hairline-weight numeral inside giant parentheses dead centre; left column holds date, caps title and synopsis in a 16px expanded Century serif, right column a right-aligned list of speakers, duration centred above the numeral. On mobile the numeral becomes a play triangle inside the parentheses and the header parentheses hold a word.

Entire viewport is one flat blue (rgb 0,70,241) divided into 15 equal ruled lanes by 2px white lines; nav items in OCR-B caps with 0.1em tracking occupy the first seven lanes, the rest stay empty; wordmark on a white tab top left.

exemplars.site: HKW Haus der Kulturen der Welt
exemplars.observed: Flat fuchsia-on-pale-cyan colour pair for all text (84px bold title, 34px light subtitle), event tiles as two-colour vector shapes with rounded corners, nav docked at the BOTTOM of the viewport as four large words.

directions.signature: At scroll 0: a white top band about 330px tall holding only four small caps serif nav words in the corners and one pair of giant thin parentheses (about 260px, stroke-thin) centred, empty or holding a single lowercase word; immediately below, the first two full-bleed colour bands (signal yellow #FFD900, then ochre #C0965C), each exactly the same height, each with '(10)' and '(9)' in the same 260px hairline sans centred, a 16px serif text block flush left (date indented, CAPS title, 10 lines of synopsis, underlined 'more'), duration centred at the top edge, and a right-aligned run-in list of names. Dark maroon-black text (#200000) on every band. On 390px: each band is one column, parentheses hold a solid play triangle, date left and duration right at the numeral's midline.
directions.grammar: Grid: three columns per band (33 / 34 / 33), text top-aligned to the band edge with 16px padding, numeral optically centred; bands are equal-height and butt together with no gap or rule. Type: two faces in maximum contrast: a hairline geometric sans used ONLY for the 260px numerals and parentheses, and a wide old-fashioned text serif at 16px/1.2 for everything else; ratio 16:1. Caps for titles and nav, same size as body. Colour: one flat ink per band from a deliberately awkward palette (yellow, ochre/cardboard, cobalt, warm grey, vermilion, lilac), text always the same near-black maroon; body background lavender (#D3D5FC) shows between states. Imagery: none. Chrome: four corner words; no logo, the parentheses are the logo. Absent: images, buttons, cards, icons other than the play triangle, any second weight.
directions.typeStack: Observed: AUTHENTIC Sans (numerals, 259px, weight 400 but hairline in appearance) + 'Century Abspanded' (a Century Expanded cut, 16px/19.2px). Free stand-ins: Google 'Jost' 200 or 'Outfit' 200 for the numerals and parentheses (test that '(' has a deep, thin curve; Jost works); Google 'Old Standard TT' or 'Libre Caslon Text' for the text serif, tracked +0.01em to get the expanded Century colour.
directions.motion: Entrance: the header parentheses open from closed '()' to '(      )' in 500ms ease-out, then a word types in between them. Scroll: each band is sticky for a beat so the next band slides over it like a card deck (pure CSS position:sticky, no JS needed); the numeral inside the header parentheses updates to the band currently under the header, counting down 10 to 1. Micro: hovering a band swaps the numeral for a solid play triangle inside the parentheses and the parentheses breathe apart 12px; clicking starts a fake audio progress drawn as the left parenthesis filling. Signature moment: the countdown numeral locking into the header parentheses as bands stack. Reduced motion: no sticky stacking, plain flow, parentheses static.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Nachtdienst, a ten-part listening series on labour in the arts produced by a performing-arts house. IA: 1) header (About, Sources, Speakers, Subscribe) + parentheses; 2) ten episode bands, newest first: date, duration in minutes, CAPS episode title, 8-10 line synopsis, 'with:' list of 8-14 names; 3) Sources band (bibliography as a long centred serif list); 4) Speakers index (all names alphabetical, run-in, with episode numbers in parentheses); 5) Subscribe band with one text input drawn as an underline between parentheses.
directions.whyWorldClass: Two typefaces, six flat inks and one glyph pair do everything: structure, identity, navigation and player. The parentheses as both logo and container is a genuinely ownable idea, and the awkward ochre-next-to-cobalt palette is the kind of confident colour choice templates never make.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: scrollytelling-chapter, interactive-timeline, music-release-hub, swiss-international-typographic. Differs: no narrative scroll effects or timeline; equal-height flat colour bands carrying a hairline 260px numeral in parentheses with 16px expanded serif text, a podcast/series programme as pure typography.
directions.buildRisk: Dies if the numeral face is not thin enough or the bands vary in height; lock band height (min 335px desktop) and use weight 200. Palette must stay flat and slightly 'wrong' (include ochre and grey-sage, not five brights). The synopsis copy needs real length (8+ lines) or the left column looks empty next to the numeral.

directions.name: Perimeter Pile, Clean Index
directions.signature: A chaotic pile of 60-plus rotated, shadowed thumbnails is confined to the viewport perimeter as a ragged picture frame, and inside it sits the most austere possible index: four columns of 14px system sans with dotted hairlines, name blurred until hovered. Maximalism and minimalism on one screen with a hard boundary between them.
directions.grammar: Frame: fixed, 60 to 90px deep on each edge, cards 80 to 220px, rotations within about 15 degrees, soft 8px shadows, overlapping. Centre: 80px inner padding; columns of about 240px with 16px gaps starting at one third of the width; row height 29px; 1px dotted rules; headers in grey with a 2px blur; one size, one weight. Colour: white centre, all colour comes from the pile. One figurative oddity allowed (a small mascot object). Absent: display type, buttons, descriptions, dates.
directions.typeStack: Observed: ui-sans-serif / system-ui 14px (tiger.exposed); Affairs Mono and Italic (Villarejo). Free stand-ins: Inter 400 at 14px on 20px; Sometype Mono for tag-style labels if used.
directions.motion: Entrance: cards are dealt from the centre out to the edges in 600ms (ease-out, random 0-200ms delays) leaving the index behind. Toggle (mascot click or key): cards fly inward and sort into the index as 20px thumbnails beside their titles (FLIP, 700ms, staggered by distance) and back. Hover an index row: its card in the pile lifts, un-rotates and scales 1.15; blurred headers sharpen on hover. Idle: the pile breathes by half a degree. Scroll: frame fixed, index scrolls inside it. Signature moment: pile-to-list sort. Reduced motion: frame static, toggle is an instant swap.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Ines Okafor-Brandt, independent designer, writer and type designer. IA: blurred name plus (About) -> four-column index: Web (28), Graphic Design (20), Writing (10), Type Design (3) -> row click opens an inline project note with two images -> About as a plain text overlay.
directions.whyWorldClass: It solves the portfolio paradox (show everything, stay calm) with a single spatial rule, and the blur on the author's own name is the kind of small perverse decision that signals an author rather than a template.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: draggable-scatter, collage-scrapbook, zine-collage, infinite-canvas. Differs: the collage is restricted to the perimeter as a frame, the centre is a severe text index, and the two states morph into each other.
directions.buildRisk: Needs 60 to 70 convincing, varied thumbnails: generate CSS and SVG mini posters, screenshots and book covers with different palettes and type, or it looks procedurally uniform. Many shadows cost paint: flatten the idle frame into few layers. At 390px keep only top and bottom strips of about 44px.

directions.name: Weathered Type, Focus on Approach
directions.signature: A calm, centred Times-style editorial page on a single flat peach ground where every glyph, from the 16.5vw masthead down to the 24px body, is eroded into stippled dust as if sandblasted or photocopied ten times; the text sharpens to crisp ink only where the reader's pointer or focus is. One crisp black pill button floats bottom-right as the control sample.
directions.grammar: Classic centred layout: 120px side margins, masthead full width, centred nav in uppercase, one featured post full width, then three columns with 48px gaps. One serif throughout (display 239px, tracking -0.03em; body 24px on 1.6 leading). Colour: one flat warm ground, black ink, no accent except a single emoji-scale red dot. The degradation is the art direction: threshold noise at the glyph edge with stray particles within about 6px. Absent: images, rules, cards, sans (except the one pill).
directions.typeStack: Observed: Times Seven (Soft Labor); a custom 'Wind Variable' display with Marfa Semi Mono (Three Zero Five); billInflate (Sandberg). Free stand-ins: Tinos or system Times for the serif; Archivo Black italic with an SVG hatch pattern fill for a wind variant; Sometype Mono for meta.
directions.motion: Idle: the dust re-seeds at about 8fps in steps, like photocopier noise, never smooth. Entrance: masthead condenses from scattered particles into letters over 1.2s. Pointer proximity (220px radius) and keyboard focus sharpen text by easing the filter scale to zero in 250ms; leaving lets it erode again over 600ms. Scroll velocity briefly increases erosion. A small live-data line (wind or time) sets the displacement direction. Signature moment: a paragraph coming into focus under the cursor. Reduced motion: static dither, sharpening on hover and focus without animation.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Slow Counsel, a research newsletter run by a small strategy consultancy. IA: masthead -> centred nav (About, Services, Collaborators, Approach, Archive, Contact) -> latest issue with date, read time, excerpt -> three-column archive of numbered issues -> fixed crisp Subscribe pill.
directions.whyWorldClass: It makes legibility itself the interaction and gives a text-only consultancy site an unmistakable material presence; the restraint elsewhere (one serif, one colour, centred classic layout) is what lets one radical surface treatment read as taste rather than gimmick.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: feturbulence-organic-hero, generative-svg-filter, dithered-lo-fi, liquid-ink-title. Differs: the degradation applies to all reading text as a state tied to attention (and optionally live weather) on a conservative serif editorial layout, not a hero effect or an image filter.
directions.buildRisk: Full-page SVG turbulence and displacement is expensive, especially on mobile Safari: filter a few large containers, animate the seed in steps, and avoid per-frame filter updates on scroll. Keep body text readable in the eroded state and offer a crisp toggle. Verify the filter renders in the headless capture at device scale factor 1 (dust must be visible, not anti-aliased away).

directions.name: Mismatched Widget Noticeboard
directions.signature: A scholarly centre column (small-caps serif title, 18px old-style serif paragraph, blue links, text-only slideshow controls) is flanked on the right by a rail of loud, over-scaled live widgets that refuse to align: a calendar with a red header, a weather strip with a sky photo, grey notice panels in letterspaced blue sans at 24px, each nudged a few pixels off the others. A red 'Menu' sits alone top-left.
directions.grammar: Three zones: 140px left gutter holding only the Menu word, a 600 to 680px text column starting at x=170, and a 500px widget rail hard against the right edge. Two unrelated type voices: old-style serif (18px on 24px; letterspaced small caps for the name) vs a wide-spaced grotesk at 24px on 32px in widgets. Colour logic is strict despite the mess: red for Menu and calendar header, link blue for all widget text, #eee panels, white page. Widgets vary in radius (24px, 0px) and offset by up to about 12px. Absent: grid alignment across zones, cards with shadows, hero, brand lockup.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Yale New (serif) and Univers (letterspaced). Free stand-ins: EB Garamond 400 with small caps for the serif voice; Hanken Grotesk or Arimo at 24px with 0.02em tracking and wide word spacing for widgets.
directions.motion: Widgets are live (today highlighted, weather line, next lecture). On each load every widget takes a new seeded offset (within 12px and 0.6 degrees). Entrance: widgets pop in one at a time at 90ms intervals with no easing. Scroll: the rail moves at 0.85x so widgets drift against the text and the fixed title slides over the paragraph. Hover a widget: it snaps square and lifts 4px. Slideshow is plain text Previous / Next with an instant swap. Signature moment: the rail drifting out of register with the text. Reduced motion: fixed offsets, no parallax.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Calder Graduate School of Art. IA: Menu word plus centred small-caps name -> introduction paragraph with programme links (Graphic Design, Painting and Printmaking, Photography, Sculpture) -> text-controlled slideshow -> widget rail: Calendar, Weather, Artist Lectures (next event), A Look Back (archive item), Open Studios, Notices -> plain footer list.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is the current reference for institutional anti-design: knowingly awkward, wiki-like and alive, yet held together by a rigorous colour code and a classical text column. It breaks the 'design system' convention while being more usable than most systems.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: interface-nostalgia-os, bento, notion-blocks. Differs: not an OS pastiche and not a tidy bento; a serious institutional page with deliberately clashing, slightly misregistered live widgets and two unrelated type voices.
directions.buildRisk: Highest risk in this set of reading as simply ugly or as a layout bug. Control comes from the calm serif column, the three-colour code and keeping every misalignment small and consistent. One or two real photographs (an interior, a sky) help; the factory interior image can serve. At 390px the widgets become a staggered stack above the text.

directions.name: Hairline Cell Ledger with Live Dither

exemplars.site: Aspen Search (Edoardo Lunardi, Awwwards SOTD 15 Sep 2026, SOTM nominee)

directions.signature: The viewport IS a ruled table. A 60px header row of cells (60x60 black logo tile, live city clock, nav cell, theme toggle, black Contact cell with arrow), then a 2x2 of half-width cells: top-left white cell with the one-word wordmark at 180px sitting bottom-left; top-right and bottom-left cells filled with a live 1-bit Bayer-dither canvas of a slow rotating blade form; bottom-right split into a charcoal statement cell and a mint cell with a logo row. On 390px it restacks to a 2-column checkerboard with the wordmark split across two cells.
directions.grammar: Grid: 1px #232323 hairlines edge to edge, zero outer margin, 20px cell padding, columns on halves and quarters of the viewport. Type: one grotesk at weight 450, tracking -0.04em, three sizes only (180 / 26-32 / 16) plus 12px mono caps labels led by an 8px square bullet; display to body 11:1; leading 1.0 display, 1.3 body. Colour: white, #232323, #D5D5D5 and a single mint (#A0FBCB); no shadows, no radii. Imagery: only procedural dither and flat colour tiles. Lists are 120px ruled rows (40px name plus mono category tag on a fixed column) with a sticky preview cell and '01 - 06' counter. Absent: cards, icons, gradients, photos, any centred hero.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Suisse Int'l (450) plus Suisse Int'l Mono. Free stand-ins: Fontshare Switzer 500 or Google Inter Tight 500 at -0.04em; mono Google Geist Mono or JetBrains Mono.
directions.motion: Entrance: hairlines draw from the top-left corner (scale 0 to 1, 600ms expo out, 40ms stagger), dither density sweeps from empty to target like an image developing, wordmark rises through its cell clip, clock starts ticking. Scroll: header cells stay sticky; each section enters as cells whose fill flips white to charcoal; long copy ramps line by line from 45 percent grey to full as it crosses mid-viewport. Hover: ledger row inverts, preview cell swaps to that client's colour tile. Signature moment: the pointer acts as a lens that locally raises dither density and tilts the blade form; the city in the clock cell rotates (LA, NYC) with a split-flap swap.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Halden Rye', an executive search firm for quantitative finance and AI. IA: header cells; hero cell quad; About (label cell left, 32px paragraph right); Clients ledger with category tags and preview cell; Testimonials as quote cells with role cells; Team roster table; one giant Contact cell.
directions.whyWorldClass: It makes a boring B2B category look like a designed object by turning the layout grid itself into the brand, with one accent and one moving texture. Total restraint, instantly recognisable thumbnail.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: swiss-international-typographic, swiss-grid-serif, dithered-lo-fi, bento. Differs: nav and content share one ruled cell table with no margins, the dither is confined inside cells as living imagery, and there is a single pastel accent cell; not a poster, not a card grid.
directions.buildRisk: Dither reads as noise if the underlying form is weak: render a high-contrast SDF blade or ribbon at low resolution, Bayer-threshold it, and scale with image-rendering pixelated at integer factors. Hairlines must stay exactly 1px (no subpixel blur); any radius or shadow kills it.

directions.name: Wordmark with an Inline Media Slot

exemplars.site: Paul Kalkbrenner (HOLOGRAPHIK, Awwwards SOTD 2 Sep 2026, SOTM nominee)
Colonia Zacamil (Adoratorio Studio, Awwwards SOTD 1 Oct 2026)

directions.signature: A white void with one line of bold grotesk at about 150px, dead centre: two words whose word space is replaced by a small live video chip (about 113x75px) sitting on the baseline at x-height. Nothing else in the centre. On first scroll the chip grows to full bleed and the next section arrives through a stepped pixel-block skyline wipe.
directions.grammar: Grid: 8px page margin, 12 columns, everything hugging the edges: evenly spaced 12px bold nav across the top right half, a three-zone bottom bar (left 'Now playing' plus 5-bar equaliser, centre a 3-line 12px bold blurb starting at column 6, right 'Sound OFF'). Type: display 150px weight 700 tracking -0.05em leading 0.8 versus 12px bold body: 12.5:1. Colour: pure white and pure black, then a mid grey (#C6C6C6) chapter; photos mostly monochrome. Sections use a black square bullet label ('RECORDINGS'), a stacked photo deck receding upward in 4 layers, Prev/Next as plain text at the edges, '01/08' counters. Absent: buttons, cards, colour, icons.
directions.typeStack: Observed: ABC Diatype Plus Variable 700 (Kalkbrenner); Heathergreen ultra-condensed plus Reckless Neue plus Roboto Mono (Zacamil). Free stand-ins: Google Inter Tight 700 or Fontshare General Sans 700 at -0.05em; condensed variant: Google Big Shoulders Display 800 or Anton, with Newsreader 300 and Roboto Mono.
directions.motion: Entrance: the two words rise from a baseline mask together as one word, then the word space opens (width 0 to chip width, 900ms expo) and the chip fades up already playing: the gap opening is the ritual. Scroll: the chip is the shared element; it scales to full bleed under a sticky clip, then a row of square blocks of uneven height wipes the next grey chapter over it. Deck cards shuffle forward on Next. Hover: nav underline wipes left to right; chip pauses and shows a tiny timecode. Sound: explicit text toggle, equaliser bars animate only when on.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Ilse Varga', a touring electronic composer. IA: wordmark hero with chip; Recordings (release rows with year and format); Tour table; Journey timeline; Gallery deck; News; Store strip; persistent player bar.
directions.photoBrief: One 6-10s loop for the chip (performer in motion, car or stage, reads at 113px wide) and 6-8 black and white portraits: candid, high contrast, plain backgrounds, 1:1 and 3:2, plus one saturated colour interior for the first full-bleed. The factory's existing AI video loops can carry the chip.
directions.whyWorldClass: The emptiest possible page that still has a hook: one typographic gesture that is also the navigation into the content. It proves confidence, and the chip growing into the page is a transition people remember.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: knockout-video-type, text-clip-reveal, sticky-iris-expansion, poster-crop. Differs: the media is a word-space sized object inside the line of type that becomes the page, not video clipped to letterforms or a generic iris; plus the persistent audio bar chrome.
directions.buildRisk: At scroll=0 the frame is 90 percent white, so it lives or dies on optical setting: kerning pairs, chip baseline and height matched to x-height, and a chip frame that is legible at thumbnail size. On 390px the name must stay on one line (about 44px) with the chip retained.

directions.name: Chamfered Frame, Script Ghost and Arch Aperture

exemplars.site: ERA Residence (The First The Last, Awwwards SOTM Aug 2026)

directions.signature: A deep aubergine field (#330D22) held by a 1px chamfered-corner frame inset 22px. Dead centre: a two-line lockup in a tall condensed didone (about 75px, leading 0.95) with a copperplate script word crossing its lower edge at about -8 degrees. Two wide-tracked serif labels sit left and right on the same horizontal axis, a floral monogram at top centre, a giant script word at 4 percent opacity behind everything, and an 80px vertical hairline above a two-line 10px extended-caps caption at the foot.
directions.grammar: Grid: strict centre axis plus a cross axis; the frame is persistent chrome. Type: three voices with strict roles: condensed didone caps for names and statements (48-75px, centred, max 800px measure), copperplate script only as overlap or ghost, extended grotesk 10-14px bold caps with leading 1.0 for all UI. Colour: one field colour per chapter with one ink: aubergine and cream, then powder blue (#B5CEDB) with navy (#17233B), accents from the botanical cut-outs only. Imagery: a single render inside an arch (530px wide, semicircular head) wrapped by two concentric hairline arches; circular hairline CTA of about 180px; rotating circular text badge as logo; left rail with scroll-percent numeral and vertical 'SCROLL'. Even the cookie notice is a designed card with script lettering. Absent: full-bleed photo hero, nav bar, buttons with fills.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Ambroise Francois (condensed Didot), Sloop Script Three, Maison Neue Extended. Free stand-ins: Fontshare Gambarino or Google Bodoni Moda (opsz max, light) for the didone; Google Pinyon Script or Monsieur La Doulaise for script; Google Archivo at wdth 125, wght 700 for the extended caps.
directions.motion: Entrance: frame draws clockwise from the top centre (1.2s), monogram blooms petal by petal, lockup lines rise 12px with a mask, script word writes on via stroke-dashoffset, flanking labels track out from 0.2em to 1.2em. Scroll: the arch rises from the bottom edge while the lockup fades, concentric arches trail with lag; at the chapter break the field colour cross-fades and cut-out botanicals grow in from a corner with slight parallax; the rail numeral counts scroll percent. Hover: circular CTA rotates its hairline dash and fills radially. Signature moment: the monogram morphs into the rotating circular badge as the palette flips.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Casa Lumen', 24 boutique residences on a southern coast. IA: framed lockup; arch reveal; place statement; residences range (sizes, layouts); amenities as numbered slides (1 / 2 with arrows); location axis; availability table; book a call.
directions.photoBrief: 3-4 architecture images that survive an arch crop with the subject centred: pool terrace in hard midday sun with saturated teal water and white stucco, one interior, one dusk exterior; plus 2 botanical cut-outs on transparency (bougainvillea, olive branch). The factory's interior image can serve the arch; botanicals can be drawn in SVG if no cut-outs are available.
directions.whyWorldClass: It reads like an engraved invitation rather than a property site: three typefaces with disciplined roles, a frame that never leaves, and chapter palettes instead of sections. It is luxurious through restraint and wit, not through gold gradients.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: sealed-invitation, property-developer-presales, art-deco-luxe, silent-luxury-restraint. Differs: persistent chamfered frame chrome, didone and script overlap lockup with a ghost script layer, arch aperture as the only image container, and full palette flips per chapter with scroll-percent rail.
directions.buildRisk: Falls flat if the condensed didone stand-in looks wide or clumsy or the script looks like a wedding template: test the free faces at size first, keep script to one or two words, and hold the ghost at 3-5 percent opacity. Do not add a nav bar.

directions.name: Stitch-Bar Rasterised Wordmark and Landscape

exemplars.site: Son Daven (The First The Last, Awwwards SOTM Jun 2026)

directions.signature: A dark espresso field left completely empty for the top 80 percent of the viewport; across the foot, edge to edge, a heavy extended wordmark in tan rendered as vertical stitch bars (about 6px columns with stepped, jagged top and bottom ends, like embroidery or a loom draft). The same bar rasteriser later draws mountain silhouettes and section dividers.
directions.grammar: Two colours only (#2C2824 and #A89474), swapped per section. Grid: 16px margins, 12 columns, big data-first blocks. Type: an inscriptional roman in caps for statements and numerals (56-90px, tracking -0.06em, leading 1.0) against an extended techno sans at 12-14px caps for labels, with key values set as inverted highlight boxes. Devices: double-rule bands holding a marquee, a vertical-bar landscape (bars of varying height and thickness forming ridgelines, denser toward the base), hairline circle CTA, bracketed [X] close on a designed cookie panel. Photography appears once, dark and warm, with type laid directly on it. Absent: any third colour, icons, cards.
directions.typeStack: Observed: KTF Metro Roman and KTF Metro Blueline. Free stand-ins: Google Marcellus or Cinzel for the roman caps; Google Michroma for the extended techno labels; wordmark drawn on canvas from a heavy extended face (Google Unbounded 900 or Archivo Black at wdth 125).
directions.motion: Entrance: wordmark assembles column by column left to right, each bar growing from its centre with slight overshoot (1.4s total), like a loom advancing. Scroll: the wordmark compresses and docks top-left; ridgelines of bars rise in a wave as their section enters and their heights respond subtly to scroll velocity; marquee band runs at constant speed and reverses on scroll direction. Hover: tag boxes invert; the circle CTA label rotates. Signature moment: section transitions are a bar wipe where the columns of one colour grow until they become the next section's field.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Olsa House', a mountain design hotel sold as an investment project. IA: wordmark gate; investment summary (two headline percentages); place and developer strip; financial indicators table; architecture and materials; amenities; construction timeline 2026-2029; invest CTA.
directions.whyWorldClass: A whole identity out of one rasterising rule applied to type, landscape and transitions, in two colours. It turns a financial prospectus into something with cultural texture, and the scroll=0 frame is a poster.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: mudmee-loom-resolve, generative-woven-textile-hero. Differs: no textile pattern is depicted; a vertical-bar rasteriser is the rendering system for wordmark, ridgelines and wipes inside a two-tone prospectus with inscriptional numerals. Proximity to mudmee-loom-resolve is real, so keep the content genre (investment prospectus, data tables) and the bottom-anchored empty hero to stay distinct.
directions.buildRisk: Bars that are too regular look like a barcode, too random look like a glitch: use a fixed column pitch with 2-3 widths and stepped end caps, sample a real glyph bitmap, and bottom-anchor it with tight margins. Must be crisp on DPR 1 screenshots (integer pixel columns).

directions.name: One-Size Contact Sheet Portfolio

exemplars.site: Gil Huybrecht (Awwwards SOTD 21 Sep 2026, SOTM nominee)
Jesper Landberg (Awwwards SOTD 29 Sep 2026, SOTM nominee)

directions.signature: A black page with no headline at all: every piece of text is the same 16px medium white grotesk. Top: a six-column facts row (name, availability, services with three indented items, recognition with seven indented counted items, Profile, Email). Then 300px of black, then a seven-column contact sheet of small page thumbnails at native aspect ratios, top-aligned, each run labelled once with the project name and numbered 1..n above the frames. Two segmented toggles pinned to the bottom corners switch layout mode and projection mode.
directions.grammar: Grid: 14px margins and gutters, 7 equal columns; thumbnails share width, vary in height, rows top-aligned with about 90px between rows. Type: one size, one weight, white on black; hierarchy only by position and indentation (sub-items indented 14px). Colour comes only from the thumbnails. Chrome: two pill toggles with the inactive option at 50 percent. Absent: display type, section titles, dividers, hover cards, descriptions.
directions.typeStack: Observed: a single custom grotesk at 16.3px, weight 500. Free stand-ins: Fontshare Switzer 500 or Google Inter Tight 500, leading 1.1, tracking -0.01em.
directions.motion: Entrance: text row appears instantly; thumbnails fade in in reading order at 30ms stagger, like a sheet developing. Hover: all frames except the hovered project dim to 30 percent, its name underlines. Click: frame expands in place via a shared-element transition. Mode toggles use FLIP: Grid to Gallery (one large frame with filmstrip), Normal to a perspective crawl (sheet tilts to about 55 degrees and scrolls toward a vanishing point). Scroll: plain document scroll, no smoothing needed; the stillness is the point.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Ines Vallat', freelance designer and art director. IA: facts row; contact sheet of 8 projects with 3-6 frames each; profile paragraph; recognition list; email. Each frame is a miniature of a fictional site.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is the logical end of the index-portfolio trend: the work is the only visual, typography is reduced to one size, and the single playful control (crawl mode) proves interaction craft without decoration. Minimal and confident in a way judges rewarded in Sep 2026.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: editorial-index, cmd-k-portfolio, anchor-annotated-index, end-crawl. Differs: strictly one type size, a dense contact sheet of live miniature pages as the entire composition, and view-mode toggles (grid, gallery, crawl) as the signature interaction.
directions.buildRisk: The thumbnails carry everything: grey placeholder boxes will kill it. Build 30+ miniatures as real scaled-down DOM (transform scale about 0.14) from 6-8 parametrised mini layouts with distinct palettes, type and one image-like block each, so they read as varied, tasteful sites. Keep text contrast AA at 16px on black.

directions.name: Swatch-Stack Navigation with Colour-Coded Scroll Rail
directions.signature: Inside a 10px white margin: a large rounded (12px) media card of a calm dusk scene with a two-line soft semi-serif headline at about 124px centred near the top in white, and to its right a 200px full-height rounded column that is the entire site map as stacked colour swatches (blush block with Home and two numbered children, sage block with Products and four numbered children, then single rows stepping through olive greys to a near-black green Contact). A mono CTA pill with a dark square arrow tile sits bottom centre of the card.
directions.grammar: Grid: two columns (media about 84 percent, nav about 14 percent) with a 10px gap; later full-bleed. Type: headline 124px light semi-serif tracking -0.01em leading 0.9 against 16px sans nav and 13px mono caps tags: about 8:1. Colour: a six-step earthy scale used as wayfinding, each chapter owning a swatch; the scrollbar repeats the scale as segments sized to chapter length. Imagery: one atmospheric subject with mirror reflection, then small floating media cards with mono tab labels attached top-right. Statement lists use opacity (active 100, others 55) instead of bullets. Absent: top nav bar, hamburger, icons.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Season Mix (display), Season Sans (text), Supply Mono (labels). Free stand-ins: Google Fraunces at opsz 144, wght 300, SOFT 100 or Fontshare Sentient Light for display; Google Instrument Sans for text; Google DM Mono for labels.
directions.motion: Entrance: swatches stack in from the bottom one by one (60ms stagger, 700ms expo), headline lines rise with a mask, the scene drifts slowly. Scroll: the nav column squeezes horizontally into a 6px colour-segmented rail with a thumb; the media card's radius relaxes to full bleed; statement lines hand over the 100 percent opacity as you scroll; media cards float in on different parallax rates. Hover: a swatch widens 8px and its children slide out; rail segments show a label tooltip. Signature moment: the swatch column becoming the scrollbar, colour for colour.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Tidewright', maker of autonomous survey vessels. IA: hero; what the ocean hides (statement list with media cards); capabilities; past missions; products with a comparison table and three models; leadership; careers; press; contact.
directions.photoBrief: One wide dusk or dawn seascape with a small dark vessel and mirror reflection, low contrast pink to slate sky; 5-6 small documentary frames (cargo ship, storm wave, harbour, deck detail). Fallback without photos: a canvas dusk gradient with slow ripple lines and SVG vessel silhouettes with reflected copies.
directions.whyWorldClass: Navigation, palette and progress indicator are one idea. It is a genuinely new chrome pattern that is calm, legible and brand-owning, wrapped around a quiet cinematic hero rather than fighting it.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: scroll-timeline-chapter-nav, vertical-elevator-floors, luxury-resort-cinematic-stillness. Differs: the site map is a visible stack of chapter-coloured swatches that collapses into a colour-coded scroll rail; the palette scale is the wayfinding system.
directions.buildRisk: With a weak hero image it reads as a dashboard sidebar: the swatch scale must be beautiful on its own (hand-tuned OKLCH steps) and the hero must be atmospheric and low contrast. On 390px the column should become a horizontal swatch strip under the hero, not a hidden menu.

directions.name: Object Monograph with Occluded Split Type

exemplars.site: FS 60P The Watch (60fps, Awwwards SOTD 17 Aug 2026)
Oryzo AI (Lusion, Awwwards SOTM Apr 2026, CSSDA score 9.43)

directions.signature: A pale fog-grey field (#EAEAEA with one large soft dark radial at top right). The model code is split into two halves set at about 300px in wide geometric caps, one each side, and a single rendered object sits dead centre physically occluding the inner edges of both halves. Around it a 700px hairline circle with eight sector lines and a short black progress arc; bottom-left a two-tone 60px 'MODEL / code' and a 12px spec label.
directions.grammar: Grid: centre axis for the object, 12-column margin text at 12px (leading 1.0) in the lower right, about 150px side margins for copy blocks. Type: display 300px light-regular wide geometric versus 12px body: 25:1, the most extreme ratio seen; secondary words at 180px in white, 40 percent and 70 percent grey layered in z. Colour: greys only, the object supplies the only material colour. Chrome: registration '+' marks at the four corners, crosshair on the object, left chapter rail with numbered labels and a growing line, small dial pictogram as section icon. Absent: buttons, cards, photography, any colour accent.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Nekst plus Inter (The Watch); ABC Repro caps tracked +0.07em (Lightweight); Halyard Display, Literata, DM Mono (Oryzo). Free stand-ins: Google Unbounded 300 or Michroma for the wide display; Inter or Geist for text; DM Mono for specs.
directions.motion: Entrance: fog radial drifts in, sector lines draw outward from the centre, the two type halves slide apart from behind the object (1.2s expo), progress arc sweeps to its first tick. Scroll: the object turns (turntable) and scales while three display words travel vertically, one layer in front of the object and two behind (z-sandwich); chapter rail line grows; palette inverts between chapters; headings roll in per letter along an arc. Hover: crosshair follows the pointer over the object and prints a part name in mono. Signature moment: the object rotating through the words so that type is alternately hidden and revealed by its silhouette.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Aerel', maker of carbon bicycle wheels, model 'AR 46C'. IA: model hero; philosophy; craft (layer exploded view); innovation numbers; full spec table; colourways; dealer and service CTA.
directions.whyWorldClass: The whole page is one object treated like a museum piece, with typography physically interacting with it. This is where the heavy-WebGL studios have landed in 2026: fewer effects, one believable thing, engineering chrome.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: luxury-watch-callouts, spec-sheet-instrument, supplement-3d-product-stage, celestial-complication. Differs: no callout leaders or dark vitrine; a light fog field, a split code-name that the object occludes, z-sandwiched scroll type, registration-mark chrome, and a non-watch object (a wheel) so it does not repeat the library's horology templates.
directions.buildRisk: Exemplars are real-time 3D; a flat SVG object will look like clip art unless it has convincing material: build the wheel from layered SVG (rim with conic and linear gradients, 20 spokes, hub, soft contact shadow, specular sweep that moves with scroll) and rotate in-plane, with the z-sandwich done by two text layers and an object-shaped mask. If WebGL is allowed, a single three.js torus-rim wheel with one HDR-like light is enough. Do not attempt the Oryzo desk scene without real 3D.

directions.name: Mixed-Voice Persona Site with Notched Collectible Grid

exemplars.site: Lando Norris (OFF+BRAND, Awwwards Site of the Year 2025 and Users' Choice)

directions.signature: An off-white field threaded with faint organic contour lines. Top-left a two-line name logo that mixes a hairline display serif (line 1) with a heavy grotesk (line 2); top centre a monogram; top right an acid lime (#D2FF00) pill-square button beside an outlined menu square. Centre: one large hero object (a race helmet with a procedural livery) under a white wireframe shell. Bottom-left: a small 'NEXT RACE' card with a notched top-right corner holding a circuit outline, event name and a laurel badge.
directions.grammar: Type: two voices alternated word by word inside the same headline (heavy grotesk caps in cream, display serif caps in lime), centred, about 95px, leading 1.0, measure about 1050px; UI at 12-14px. Colour: chapters step off-white, dark olive (#282C20), near black (#111112) with lime as the only accent in two strengths (#D2FF00 for UI, a muted #B4C736 for serif words). Shape language: 1px outlined cards with 6px radius and a notched tab corner carrying label plus year; grid of four columns with alternate columns offset by half a card. Texture: contour-line field that continues across chapters. Absent: photos in boxes, gradients, drop shadows.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Mona Sans Variable (free, on Google Fonts) plus Brier display serif; Die Grotesk on the sibling site. Free stand-ins: Google Mona Sans 700-800 for the grotesk; Google Gloock or Instrument Serif for the serif voice.
directions.motion: Entrance: contour lines draw with stroke-dashoffset in a slow drift, wireframe shell scans down over the object, logo lines slide in from opposite sides, the tab card flips up from its notch. Scroll: field colour steps between chapters, the mixed-voice headline reveals word by word with the block cursor travelling, a signature scribble draws itself in lime; collectible cards rise with a half-row stagger. Hover: a card's object rotates 20 degrees and its tab fills lime; contour lines bend toward the pointer. Signature moment: the wireframe shell resolving into the painted object as the first chapter flips to olive.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Kaito Arden #47', a rally driver. IA: hero with next-event card; manifesto headline; on-track and off-track split; season timeline; helmet hall of fame (12 liveries with year tabs); partners; store teaser; footer signature.
directions.whyWorldClass: Site of the Year 2025 for a reason: a personal brand built from a two-typeface voice, one accent colour and a custom shape language, with collectibles turned into the content. The mixed-voice headline is the most copied move of the year, but here it is done with real typographic judgment.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: esports-team-roster, music-release-hub. Differs: word-level serif and grotesk alternation as the brand voice, notched-tab card system, contour-line field, and a generative collectible grid; not a roster or stat page.
directions.buildRisk: The exemplar leans on a photographed portrait and 3D helmets. Without them the hero must be a strong drawn object: build the helmet in SVG (shell, visor, vents) and generate 12 liveries from pattern rules (maze lines, checker, mirror tiles) so the grid looks rich. If the serif stand-in is weak the mixed headline looks like a font bug: test Gloock vs Instrument Serif at 95px caps.

directions.name: Swash Serif Private Society with Object on a Curved Horizon

exemplars.site: Miu Miu: A House That We Shaped (Merci Michel, SOTD 25 Aug 2026)

directions.signature: A grainy vertical gradient from umber to sand. Three short lines of hairline high-contrast serif at about 150px, ragged and offset about 120px from each other, with swash ligatures that loop between letters. A dark faceted mineral object rises from the bottom centre and overlaps the third line. Tiny sans labels are scattered like map annotations, a hairline orbit ellipse crosses the frame, and two tilted photo cards stand at the lower corners on a curved black horizon. Below the object: a three-line staggered serif motto and a white input-like CTA with a single dot.
directions.grammar: Grid: centre-weighted but deliberately off-axis, with each headline line indented differently; labels float on a loose 12-column grid. Type: display 150px weight 300-400 leading 0.9 versus 13px sans labels: 11:1; a second serif at 20px for mottos; mono 10px tag at the foot. Colour: umber, sand, cream and black only; the object supplies iridescent darks. Chrome: stacked three-line serif logo, two wide ghost pills divided by a vertical rule, a cream MENU pill with a triple-line glyph. Second chapter: charcoal field, rounded 8px images in an uneven masonry around a featured slide, 88px black circular arrows, serif fraction counter. Absent: prices, feature lists, any urgency.
directions.typeStack: Observed: OT Jubilee Platinum (display), Voyage (secondary serif), Switzer (text, free on Fontshare). Free stand-ins: Google Cormorant 300 with swash and discretionary ligature features on, or Google Italiana, for display; Google Gilda Display for mottos; Fontshare Switzer for text.
directions.motion: Entrance: grain fades up, the horizon arc rises from below, headline lines write in with a soft blur-to-sharp per line (1.4s), swash loops draw last, the object ascends with a slow rotation and settles, cards tilt into place. Scroll: horizon climbs to take the whole viewport into charcoal, object sinks behind it, images arrive at different speeds; the orbit ellipse rotates slightly with scroll. Hover: pills fill from the divider outward; arrow circles nudge 6px; images de-blur. Signature moment: the mineral object eclipsing the last headline word and catching a specular sweep.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'The Halcyon Table', a private membership for furniture makers and collectors. IA: withheld hero; creed; Places (6 rooms carousel); Objects (catalogue of 8 pieces with lot-like captions); admission steps; request form.
directions.photoBrief: Optional: 6 interiors in soft daylight (timber, stone, linen, winter window, no people) for the Places chapter; the factory's interior image plus procedural variants can cover a reduced set.
directions.whyWorldClass: Luxury through withholding: the copy says less than the type, the type is half hidden by the object, and the palette never raises its voice. The swash serif gives it a 2026 signature that is not the usual Canela or Editorial New look.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: silent-luxury-restraint, jeweled-vitrine, material-cabinet, sealed-invitation. Differs: swash-ligature display serif set ragged and off-axis, an object physically overlapping the headline, curved-horizon stage with tilted cards, and the admission-request genre.
directions.buildRisk: The swashes are the point and free faces have few: use Cormorant's swash alternates or draw 2-3 custom SVG ligature loops for the hero words. The mineral must not look like a grey polygon: build it from 25-40 SVG facets with dark gradients, a turbulence sparkle layer and one moving specular facet.

directions.name: Anachronism Collage with a Framed Index

exemplars.site: The Renaissance Edition, Shopify Editions Winter 26 (Shopify Design, Awwwards SOTM Feb 2026)
Tracing Art, Getty (Resn, Awwwards SOTM Jul 2025)
The Tuscan Journey Begins (MONOGRID, Awwwards SOTD 13 Sep 2026)

directions.signature: A full-bleed classical painted landscape with two cut-out old-master figures in mid leap, each carrying one neon magenta contemporary object. Dead centre, a 340x465px 1px outlined box: three-line title in bold tight grotesk with one syllable swapped into script, a two-line serif subtitle, then a 12-row index in bold 16px at leading 1.0 with roman numerals right-aligned in a serif. Hairline guides run past the box edges across the painting.
directions.grammar: Grid: the centred index box plus its extended guide lines; everything else is free collage. Type: bold grotesk at tracking -0.03em in two sizes (26px title, 16px index) on the cover, exploding to 180px chapter words inside; serif for numerals and captions; one script syllable. Colour: the painting's muted greens, creams and umbers with exactly one synthetic accent (magenta #FF2DA6) reserved for the anachronistic props. Chrome: a plain top bar, the index re-docking bottom-left as persistent TOC with numerals. Chapters: one cropped painting detail each, one prop, one giant word. Absent: UI cards, gradients, stock photos.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Neue Montreal 700, Imperial Script, HW Cigars. Free stand-ins: Google Inter Tight 700 or Host Grotesk 700 at -0.03em; Google Imperial Script (the same face is on Google Fonts); Google Instrument Serif for numerals and captions.
directions.motion: Entrance: painting fades from sepia to colour, figures drift in on opposing arcs and hang with slow float, props arrive last with a small bounce, box outline draws and index rows tick in at 40ms. Scroll: figures parallax apart, the box collapses into the bottom-left TOC, each chapter wipes via a mask shaped like the previous prop; chapter words scale from 0.8 to 1 with the portrait behind. Hover: index row shifts 8px and its numeral turns magenta; props wobble. Signature moment: the two figures' fingers almost touching across the index box, held for a beat before scroll releases them.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: a commerce platform's seasonal release, 'The Baroque Release: 140 updates'. IA: cover with framed index; 12 numbered chapters each with a giant word, 3-5 feature rows and one prop; search; persistent TOC; footer credits listing the public-domain artworks.
directions.photoBrief: Public-domain old-master sources from open-access museum collections: one wide Arcadian landscape, two full figures with clear silhouettes for clean cut-outs, 3-4 half-length portraits for chapters. Props (cup, bag, board, laptop) drawn as flat-shaded SVG in the single neon accent. The factory's one painting can serve as landscape; figures need sourcing.
directions.whyWorldClass: A product changelog turned into a cultural object: one loud conceptual joke (classical painting plus neon commerce props) held in check by a tiny, disciplined index box. It shows how a big brand can be funny and still typographically strict.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: digital-rococo-baroque, collage-scrapbook, mass-changelog-scroll-map, magazine-takeover. Differs: restrained modern grotesk index box as the cover, single neon accent on anachronistic props, and release-notes IA; not ornament revival and not a scrapbook.
directions.buildRisk: Bad cut-outs read as clip art: needs 2 figures with clean alpha masks and consistent painterly grain, or the collage collapses. Keep the accent to one hue and the box small; resist adding more type on the cover. Licence notes for artworks must be in the footer.

directions.name: Spiral stair table of contents
directions.signature: At scroll=0 a CSS 3D spiral staircase of pale paper slabs climbs from lower centre to upper left on a pure white page. Each tread front face is one contents row: two-digit number in 11px grotesque, bold serif title, italic genre, author right-aligned. The nearest four treads are fully legible, the further ones foreshorten into illegibility. The only other element is the masthead, right-aligned top right: about 79px regular serif in lower case with a 22px grotesque issue line beneath. No nav, no logo, no colour.
