directions.grammar: No column grid: one 3D object owns the left-centre two thirds; 40px page margins. Display 79px regular serif, leading 1.0, tracking 0; row text 16-18px (display to row about 4.5:1); numbers 11px sans. Slab front faces #ffffff, top and side faces #ededed to #f4f4f4, 1px #e6e6e6 edges, no drop shadows, depth only from face tone. Colour is white, black and two greys. No imagery. No chrome at all; the stair is the navigation. Absent: header bar, buttons, cards, images, footer in first view. Mobile: stair rotates to near-frontal, tread about 86vw, row cells wrap.
directions.typeStack: Observed: system Times New Roman for everything, Helvetica/Arial for numerals and the issue line; no webfonts loaded. Free stand-ins: use the system stack as-is, or Tinos (Google, Times metric match) plus Arimo (Google) if a webfont is required for consistency.
directions.motion: Entrance: treads unfold one by one from a flat stack into the spiral (rotateY + translateZ, 60ms stagger, 500ms ease-out each). Scroll: document scroll drives rotation around the newel and upward travel so each tread reaches the reading position in turn (scroll-timeline or rAF), with the masthead fixed. Hover: a tread slides 24px out along its own axis and its top face darkens one step; focus ring is a plain 2px black outline. Click: the tread extends into a full-width sheet (view transition). Signature moment: the first scroll tick, when the whole stair turns as one rigid object. Reduced motion: a flat list with stepped left indents, same rows.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'The Slow Quarterly', a journal of writing made for the browser, issue 07. IA natural to the genre: masthead and issue line; stair contents of 10-12 pieces (poem, essay, love letter, conversation, artifact of memory); editors letter; contributors as a plain list; colophon (how the issue was built, typefaces, page weight); past issues, each as a small different 3D stack; submissions window with dates.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is the rare case where a single structural idea carries a whole site: the table of contents is an architectural object, set in the plainest possible type, and it is still perfectly usable. It reads as literature, not as tech demo, and it survives on a phone.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: fold-origami, css-cube-rotator, scroll-3d-rotation (and the sibling scout's browser-default-couture). Those rotate decorative objects or stay flat; here the navigation itself is the 3D structure, in default browser typography with zero imagery and zero colour.
directions.buildRisk: 3D text goes soft or illegible when foreshortened, and a timid stair reads as a skewed list. Dodge: keep the nearest four treads under 12deg rotateY so they rasterise crisply, use transform-style preserve-3d with real side and top faces, exaggerate tread depth, and make sure scroll=0 already shows four legible rows plus the receding flight. On 390px switch to the near-frontal stair that was observed.

directions.name: Battery-gauge background, duotone-dither magazine
directions.signature: The page background is a live battery gauge: the top 58% of the viewport is pale sky blue (#eaf4ff), the bottom 42% cream (#fff5d1), with a 1px boundary line crossing the full width and a tiny battery icon plus '42%' at the right edge. Over it sits a Times-set magazine front page: 50px caps masthead with an arrow glyph, a one-line 'this is a solar-powered website, it sometimes goes offline' statement, pipe-separated nav with three coloured section links, a 2px black rule, and a hero image rendered as a coarse one-colour ordered dither that shifts tint where the gauge line crosses it. Mono 'Page size: 511 KiB' pinned bottom-left.
directions.grammar: 20px outer margin, 4-column grid with 20px gutters; hero spans columns 2-4, its headline and dek sit in column 1 at the same top edge. Masthead 50px, headline 28px, body 20px/28px, dates 13px mono grey: a deliberately flat scale (2.5:1 max). Section colours: blue #1a3ccf, red #d0121b, green #0a6b4d, used for nav links and as the dither ink of each article image. Images are 4-level Bayer dithers at 2x pixel size on a pale tint, no borders, no radius. One 2px rule under the header; no cards, no shadows, no icons except globe, mail, RSS and battery glyphs. Optional header strip (from Branch): bordered mono control group Default / Low / Moderate / High. Absent: webfonts, logo image, hero type bigger than 50px, any decoration.
directions.typeStack: Observed: system Times at 20px body and 50px masthead, system monospace for dates and page size (Low-tech); Inter 300 at 68px with mono controls (Branch). Free stand-ins: ship no webfont (system Times, Courier) to keep the page weight honest; if needed Tinos plus Courier Prime (Google).
directions.motion: Ambient: the gauge line drifts a few pixels per minute along a simulated solar day and the two tints re-register through the hero image. Entrance: images arrive as 1-bit silhouettes and refine to 4-level dither in three steps (120ms each, steps easing), text is instant. Interaction: a weather/intensity control (sunny, overcast, night or Low/Moderate/High) immediately re-renders images as dither, outline only, or alt text only, and updates the printed page weight; hovering an image floods it to full section ink. Signature moment: drag the gauge line down past 10% and the page swaps to an 'offline, back at sunrise' postcard with forecast. No easing curves beyond steps; reduced motion: fixed gauge, final dither state.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Slow Current', a solar-powered journal of repair and appropriate technology run from a balcony server. IA: masthead plus power statement; lead story; 8-story grid with section-tinted dithers; 'about this server' panel (battery, uptime, panel output, 3-day forecast at the server location as icons); printed editions; archive by year as a plain list; offline reading; donate; page-weight and energy colophon in the footer.
directions.whyWorldClass: The constraint is the art direction: the layout tells the truth about its own infrastructure, and the duotone dithers give every story a cover at a fraction of the bytes. It has been the reference for sustainable web design for years and still looks fresher than most 2026 award sites.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: dithered-lo-fi, weather-reactive-scene, broadsheet-newspaper. dithered-lo-fi is a generative texture and weather-reactive-scene is a hero scene; this is a working magazine front page whose background, images and footer are energy instruments (gauge split, per-section dither ink, printed page weight, intensity modes).
directions.buildRisk: Without commitment it reads as an unstyled blog. Dodge: make the two-tone gauge split unmissable and let it cross the hero image; dither in canvas with a coarse Bayer 4x4 matrix at 2x pixels and a single ink per section (the factory car, interior and painting assets dither well, plus SVG line drawings of tools); keep the real transfer size small and print the true number. Mobile: single column, gauge still visible behind the masthead as observed.

directions.name: Watercolour shopfront, hairline shop, sentence finder
directions.signature: On warm paper (#f8f3ea) an unframed ink-and-watercolour portrait of the shops own corner premises (fascia lettering, lamp post, railings, two passers-by, three loose washes of terracotta, teal-grey and olive) sits top right, about 680px wide. Left of it the wordmark runs as letterspaced serif small caps with the district and postcode. A 90px hairline tool rail on the far left stacks four tiny line icons with labels, and directly under the drawing a horizontal strip of cut-out objects, each with an 11px tracked-caps label, the first underlined as active. Below it a 4-column grid of single objects divided by 1px hairlines.
directions.grammar: Left rail 90px with a 1px #e5ddd0 divider, content full-bleed to its right. Product grid: 4 columns, no gaps, 1px hairlines between cells, object centred with a soft contact shadow on the same paper colour, title 21px/29px serif centred (two lines max, ellipsis), price in italic old-style figures in a lighter ink. Wordmark 22px caps tracked 0.2em; labels 12px light geometric sans tracked 0.15em; announcement bar 13px on #ece8dc. Colour: paper #f8f3ea, ink #3c4539 (a green-black, never pure black), hairline #e5ddd0, pale olive pill #e9e8d6. Sentence finder: 30px serif sentence with three pill dropdowns, two small buttons (one outlined, one filled pale) and a watercolour object to the right. Mobile: rail becomes a bottom tab bar with the bird mark in a centre circle, grid goes 2-up, the drawing stays on top. Absent: lifestyle photography, banners, badges, colour blocks.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Trinite (roman and italic, body 21px/29.4px, colour rgb(60,69,57)), plus a light rounded geometric sans for chrome. Free stand-ins: Crimson Pro 300/400 or Newsreader (Google) for Trinite, with italic old-style figures; Jost 300/400 (Google) tracked for the chrome.
directions.motion: Entrance: the shopfront inks itself (stroke-dashoffset on the line layer, 1.2s, ease-out), then the washes bloom under it through a turbulence mask (600ms each, slightly late and misregistered). Ambient: two or three 6fps cut-paper loops in the drawing (a figure walks past, the lamp flickers, the door opens). Category strip: drag to scroll with inertia, objects bob 4px on hover, strip becomes sticky under the header on scroll (observed). Grid: hairlines draw first, objects fade up 60ms apart. Signature moment: the sentence finder, where each pill word rolls vertically like a counter and the grid below re-deals. Easing gentle, 300-600ms; reduced motion shows the finished drawing and instant swaps.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Marlowe and Quill, stationers, 9 Lambs Passage'. IA: shopfront header; departments strip (inks, pencils, papers, desk, ornaments, seasonal); new arrivals hairline grid; sentence finder; a note from the shop floor; printed catalogue request; visit us (hours, hand-drawn street map); newsletter; small-print footer with delivery times.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is e-commerce with the manners of a real shop: the illustration is a portrait of the premises, the grid is drawn with hairlines rather than cards, the type is a bookish Dutch serif, and the search is a sentence. Nothing in it could be mistaken for a theme.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: la-carta-restaurant-character, material-cabinet, jeweled-vitrine, collage-scrapbook. Those are showcases; this is a working shop flow (rail, departments strip, hairline product grid, sentence filter) led by an architectural illustration rather than a mascot or collage.
directions.buildRisk: An SVG 'watercolour' that looks like clip-art sinks it, and so do weak object drawings. Dodge: confident single-weight ink linework with overshoots and unclosed corners, three flat pigment washes offset from the lines with feTurbulence plus feDisplacementMap edges and multiply blend, grain overlay; draw 12-16 simple flat SVG objects (ink bottle, pencils, notebooks, scissors, paper ornaments) with contact shadows and no attempt at photorealism. Thumbnail check: drawing, wordmark, rail and strip must all be inside 1440x900.

directions.name: Linocut facade and boxed notice cells
directions.signature: A page printed in one black ink on white: a scalloped linocut border runs along the top edge, the name sits centred in lower-case serif, a cluster of thin-ruled boxes with italic links hangs top right, the address is one letterspaced serif line, and across the full width a hand-cut linocut street scene of the restaurant facade (striped awnings, sash windows, a hanging sign, a row of figures) fills the lower 60% of the viewport inside a 2px frame. Below, the page continues as a notice board of ruled cells.
directions.grammar: 12px outer gutter; everything lives in 2px black-bordered cells with 10px gaps; three unequal columns (220px / fluid / 220px) for the notice rows. Serif 16px/20px with 0.06em tracking; caps headings 34px with 2px tracking; small caps kickers 16px ('TODAYS'); every link italic; buttons are boxes with italic text and no fill. Lists use hairline dividers at 46px row height. Strict 1-bit palette; the only permitted variant is a cream panel #f4e8d6 with a 4px frame and one hot pink #ec2f95 action. Illustration: linocut with visible gouge marks and white-line hatching, used as the hero and as spot cells; photography only inside cells and sparingly. Chrome: a hamburger at top left, nothing fixed. Absent: gradients, radius, hero video, food-photo carousels.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Georgia for all text with a custom logo face (Quo Vadis); Futura PT plus Century Expanded (Noble Rot); Cheltenham plus Gill Sans Nova (Dishoom). Free stand-ins: Gelasio (Google, Georgia metric match) or Libre Caslon Text; Jost for Futura; Old Standard TT for Century Expanded.
directions.motion: Entrance: cells print in sequence like a proof being pulled (opacity plus blur 2px to 0, 80ms stagger, 240ms each), the scallop border first. Ambient: three or four cut-paper loops inside the facade at 6fps with steps easing (awning flutter, a diner raises a glass, a swallow crosses). Live cells: weather line and todays date; menu list rows invert to black on hover; boxed links fill black with white italic. Scroll: plain document scroll with the scallop border staying as a fixed top frame; optional bottom-docked nav that moves to the top after the first screen (as observed on Noble Rot). Signature moment: the facade loops, discovered a second after load. Reduced motion: still print.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'The Swallow Rooms', dining rooms and members club in an old Soho townhouse. IA: facade print; notice board (todays bill of fare, todays weather, private rooms, the club, a short history essay); menus as typeset lists (a la carte, pudding, wine, set lunch); events as dated notices; bookings and enquiries boxes; gift vouchers; address, telephone and hours colophon.
directions.whyWorldClass: A commissioned print language applied with total discipline: one ink, one rule weight, italic for every action. It feels like the restaurant, not like a booking widget, and the small live cells give a reason to come back.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: la-carta-restaurant-character, broadsheet-newspaper, evening-service, ukiyo-e-woodblock. This differs by being a 1-bit linocut notice board of boxed cells with living cells (weather, todays menu) and an animated facade; it is neither a newspaper column layout nor a colour woodblock pastiche.
directions.buildRisk: The linocut must be convincing; clean vector shapes will read as an icon set. Dodge: assemble the facade from modules (sash windows, awning stripes, brick courses, sign bracket, simple cut-shape figures), render white-line hatching with SVG patterns, roughen all edges with a feTurbulence displacement of about 1.5px, and keep it strictly 1-bit. Avoid any modal on load so the scroll=0 thumbnail shows the print.

directions.name: Gouache mark overprinted by the wordmark
directions.signature: An almost empty warm-white page (#fdfaf6). At its centre a single loose gouache shape (a flat process-yellow lemon about 230px wide with two dark green leaf strokes, dry-brush edges visible) is overprinted by a two-line wordmark in wide-tracked monoline grotesque caps roughly 96px tall, the letters running across paint and paper alike. Top left: eight destinations as a plain vertical list in 24px book serif, no underlines. Bottom left: one 13px italic line. Nothing else.
directions.grammar: 50px margins; no header bar, no grid visible. Nav list 24px with 30.7px leading (ratio wordmark to nav 4:1); wordmark tracking about 0.12em, weight regular, line gap equal to cap height. Second screen: a pale grey paper panel (#eeeeee) carrying the menu as an actual typeset sheet (italic serif notes, centred courses) with two pager dots, while the nav list stays fixed and swaps its active item to italic with indented sub-items; a small pen-drawn monogram replaces the wordmark top left. Info is prose: address, telephone and service hours in 24px serif starting at a 34% left offset, hours in italic. Palette: paper, black, one yellow (#f5e800), one green (#1f7a5c). Absent: buttons, cards, food photography, icons, footer blocks.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Bembo at 16-24px with 0.16px tracking for all text; a light monoline geometric grotesque for the wordmark. Free stand-ins: Cardo or EB Garamond (Google) for Bembo; Jost 400 (Google) or Satoshi (Fontshare) tracked 0.12em for the wordmark.
directions.motion: Entrance: the paint goes down first, as a brush-path mask reveal (lemon 900ms, each leaf 500ms, ease-out, slightly overlapping), then the wordmark fades through at 300ms as if printed on top. Ambient: on pointer move the paint layer drifts 6-10px against the type like a misregistered print; the mark changes fruit with the month. Nav hover: roman to italic swap, no colour. Menu sheet: pages turn with a short paper flip between services. Scroll is unadorned. Signature moment: the brush reveal on load. Reduced motion: finished mark, static.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Cafe Odile', a canal-side cafe and bakery. IA as the genre really works: the mark; menus (breakfast, lunch, a dated sample menu, each a typeset sheet); info (address, telephone, service hours written as sentences); about (one paragraph); reservations; private hire; press as a plain dated list; a three-object shop; one Instagram line.
directions.whyWorldClass: It has the nerve to show one painted shape and a list. Every remaining decision (Bembo at one size, hours written as prose, the menu as paper) is exactly right, and it scales to a phone without losing anything. This is minimalism with a pulse.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: mono-ink-restraint, silent-luxury-restraint, liquid-ink-title, la-carta-restaurant-character. Those are typographic restraint or ink effects; this hinges on one hand-painted mark physically overprinted by type, a list-as-navigation, and paper-sheet menus.
directions.buildRisk: If the paint is small or flat the page looks unfinished and the thumbnail looks blank. Dodge: make the mark large (about 40% of viewport height), fully saturated, with a believable dry-brush edge (SVG path plus feTurbulence and feDisplacementMap, a grain mask, slight opacity variation inside the fill) and real overlap with the letters; keep the wordmark at a weight that survives at thumbnail size. Give the second screen real typeset menu content so depth exists below the fold.

directions.name: Typewriter chronology under a fluoro slab
directions.signature: Under a header made of black-ruled boxes (name in bold condensed grotesque inside a 4px box, an equally boxed empty search field, a round rotated OPEN stamp, three bold lines of address and todays closing time) a full-bleed cream band is filled edge to edge with a 10px typewriter chronology: a year column and one-line events on the left, repeated date and venue columns on the right. Across it, overprinted in fluorescent magenta with multiply so the typewriter text shows through, runs a two-line fat slab-serif headline about 150px tall spanning the full 1440px, with a smaller slab date and venue at the lower corners.
directions.grammar: Content column 992px centred, closed by a 4px black rule; the band alone is full-bleed. Nav: 30px bold grotesque words, each with a 3px black underline; utility row: 13px bold with tiny pictograms and magenta underlines. Catalogue: 6 text-only columns, AUTHOR 11px caps, title 14px bold, category 11px caps, price 11px, a yellow highlighter tag; no thumbnails. Section heads 30px bold centred over paired blocks; event type words in purple, orange and magenta. Palette: white, black, cream #fdf8ec, magenta #ec008c, highlighter #fff200. Images rare and greyscale. Scale jump is extreme: 10px chronology against 150px slab (15:1). Absent: product photos in lists, cards, shadows, radius, hero imagery.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Arial/Helvetica bold 14px body and 30px nav (no webfonts loaded), a bold condensed grotesque logo, Courier-style chronology, a Rockwell/Stymie-weight fat slab for the overprint. Free stand-ins: Barlow Condensed 700 (logo), Arimo 700 (body and nav), Courier Prime (chronology), Alfa Slab One or Bevan (slab), all Google.
directions.motion: Entrance: the chronology types in at teletype speed (a 600ms burst that fills the band, then a blinking caret on the last line), then the slab headline stamps on in two hits (120ms each, steps easing) landing 2px off-register before settling. Live: the OPEN stamp rotates slowly and flips to CLOSED by local time, 'Today until 7 pm' updates. Hover: catalogue rows get a left-to-right highlighter sweep (150ms), nav underlines thicken. Scroll: the header condenses to the boxed name plus search and stays sticky while catalogue rows pass beneath (observed). Signature moment: the overprint stamp. Reduced motion: printed state.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Paper Assembly, Inc.', a non-profit artists book shop and annual book fair. IA: boxed header with open status; fair announcement band over the organisations own chronology; recent arrivals as a text catalogue; events and exhibitions; editions; membership programme; submit a book; locations and hours; donate.
directions.whyWorldClass: Institutional history used as texture, a fluoro slab used as a stamp, and a shop that trusts titles over thumbnails. It is loud and completely functional at once, and every element comes from the print culture it serves.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: festival-lineup-poster, svg-paint-order-poster, stdout (and the sibling scout's overflow-ledger-index). This differs through its two-layer print logic (dense typewriter data as ground, fluoro slab overprint with multiply) attached to a working shop header with live status and a text-only catalogue.
directions.buildRisk: Needs a lot of believable chronology copy, and the overprint can become illegible mush on 390px. Dodge: write 40-plus specific dated lines for the fictional organisation; on mobile set the slab at about 64px over four lines with the band height auto and the chronology at 8px; use mix-blend-mode multiply with a solid magenta fallback; keep the boxed header intact on mobile as two stacked boxes.

directions.name: Daily puzzle page in three live columns
directions.signature: Under a slim navy bar (bubble wordmark with a 'by ... and friends' line, a 'Your dailies' tab underlined in pink) the page is a newspaper games page in three equal columns on pale grey. Each column stacks live boards under a header row built from a 28px pictogram, a bold serif game name, a hairline leader and an italic 'Unplayed' at the right. At scroll=0: a 9x13 crossword grid with an italic serif title and bylined avatar chips, a colour-block tiling puzzle in peach, sage, sky and pink over diagonal hatching, and a word-chain diagram of grey and white tiles joined by arrows.
directions.grammar: Three equal columns with 24px inner padding, separated by 8px lighter gutters; dashed 1px separators between games; boards drawn with 2-3px strokes in near-black navy. Header row: name 15px bold serif, status 12px italic, sub-items as bullets with dashed leaders and 'Bonus' tags. Body 16px geometric sans. Palette: navy #1b1d29, paper #f2f2f2, white, peach #f9c06a, sage #9bb38a, sky #5db8ff, pink #ffa9b0; pink also for small buttons. A 'Yesterdays news' block lists records in plain sentences with bold numbers. Absent: hero, marketing headline, photography, cards with shadows.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Poppins (UI and body), Zodiak bold and extrabold italic (game names and titles), Dongle and Rubik in boards. Free stand-ins are the real faces: Poppins (Google) and Zodiak (Fontshare); Fraunces 900 with soft axis stands in for the Pudding-style fat serif.
directions.motion: Entrance: boards deal in like cards (translateY 12px, rotate 1deg, settle; 40ms stagger, 260ms spring). Interaction: tiles squash on press (scale 0.94 to 1.04 to 1 in 180ms), pieces snap with a hard 2px offset shadow, wrong moves shake 6px twice. Completion: the status flips from 'Unplayed' to a rubber-stamped 'Played' with a short burst of board-coloured squares, the leader line fills. Live: countdown to the next daily, streak dots. Scroll is plain; the navy bar stays. Signature moment: a mini puzzle in the hero that can be solved in ten seconds. Reduced motion: no deal or squash, state changes instant.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'The Morning Fold', six small puzzles, new every day at 06:00. IA: dailies page (mini crossword, tiling, letter-shift, nine-box, word chain, colour match); yesterdays news and records; streak calendar; the makers with bylines; membership; archive by date; how each game works as one-paragraph rules.
directions.whyWorldClass: It treats play with newspaper seriousness: column rules, bylines, leaders and status, with boards as the only imagery. Dense, legible, cheerful, and every pixel is interactive content rather than marketing.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: playable-terminal-game, broadsheet-newspaper, bento. This differs by using newspaper column grammar where every cell is a live toy, a pastel-on-navy puzzle palette, and status leaders; it is neither terminal-themed nor a bento of feature cards.
directions.buildRisk: Static fake boards would be hollow, and six real games in one file invites bugs. Dodge: make exactly two boards genuinely playable with keyboard support (the tiling puzzle and the letter-column shift), render the others as animated previews labelled 'opens at 06:00', and keep all boards as CSS grid or SVG. Mobile: one column, crossword first, header row intact.

directions.name: Two labels on four-way kraft stripes
directions.signature: The whole viewport is brown kraft divided into four quadrants of two-tone stripes (about 14px, #b89968 and #a6885c), each quadrant running a different way: horizontal, diagonal down, diagonal up, vertical. On it, slightly above centre, sit two white rectangles like bottle labels, each about 367x518px with a 20px gap. The left label carries only the hand-stamped name with uneven inking and one small one-colour ink drawing. The right label repeats the name and lists four centred entries, each a 15px sentence followed by a 34px condensed caps destination word. No nav bar, no footer, nothing else.
directions.grammar: The labels are the entire interface. All type centred; small text 15px regular, destinations 32-34px condensed caps (ratio about 2.2:1), name stamp about 30px with a two-line small suffix. Colours: kraft, white, black. Below the fold the label proportion persists as content columns and beers are listed as label strips (name, style, ABV, hops, bottled-on date). Variant chrome from Labour and Wait for inner pages: one pale tray (#ebebe9) with 28px corners on umber #474442, wide-tracked humanist sans caps lists, a 4px rule under the wordmark. Absent: photography, icons, buttons, colour accents.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Share (Google) for all text plus a hand-stamped logotype (The Kernel); Gill Sans MT Medium, Bold and Display Bold with 0.06 to 0.21em tracking (Labour and Wait). Free stand-ins: Share itself (Google); Cabin or Lato tracked wide for Gill Sans; draw the stamped name as SVG text with a roughen filter.
directions.motion: Ambient: each quadrants stripes drift very slowly along their own direction (60s loop), like wrapping paper being unrolled. Entrance: the two labels are slapped down one after the other (translateY -12px, rotate 0.6deg, settle in 260ms) and the name inks in with uneven opacity. Hover: a destination word debosses (1px down, inverted text-shadow). Click: the label flips on its vertical axis and its back becomes the page. Scroll: beer label strips peel in from the left edge. Signature moment: the label flip. Reduced motion: static labels, still stripes.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Arch Seven Brewery', a railway-arch brewery with a taproom. IA: two labels (identity; four doors: online shop, bottle shop hours, taproom, the brewery); beer list as label strips with bottled-on dates; taproom hours and booking; wholesale enquiries; a short note on why the labels are plain; address and opening times.
directions.whyWorldClass: Packaging and website are one object. It is wabi-sabi without styling: stamped ink, wrapping paper and two rectangles, with a hierarchy so clear it needs no navigation. Nobody else looks like this.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: monogram-card, soft-brutalism, e-receipt-invoice, living-note-flavor-kraft (admin). This differs as packaging-as-interface: two physical labels on a four-direction striped kraft ground, no chrome at all, and a product list built from the same label logic.
directions.buildRisk: Can read as an under-construction splash, and repeating gradients can moire or shimmer. Dodge: craft the labels (paper fibre noise, ink-stamp roughness via SVG filter, a real small drawing), use repeating-linear-gradient at whole-pixel sizes with no fractional scaling, animate stripes with background-position only, and give the page a rich lower half (label-strip beer list) so it is clearly a complete site.

directions.name: Season ledger rail with live release countdown
directions.signature: A fixed left rail (26% of the width) on warm stone holds only a serif wordmark and a three-row ledger, each row a plain label and an inset field cell in small tracked caps: 'Current season: [AUTUMN 26]', 'Next release: [80D 3H 40M 58S]' ticking every second, 'Waiting list: [OPEN]'. A hairline, then empty space down to language and country selectors. To the right, a tall botanical still life on a slate ground with a rounded frosted card that states the model in three numbered steps, a red status sentence ('Currently full.') and a wide JOIN button with a small status dot. A round menu button floats top right.
directions.grammar: Rail about 380px with 48px padding and a 1px divider; the right column scrolls, each section opening with a 60px label bar in terracotta 14px text. Body 15-16px semi-mono humanist with 0.25px tracking and 24px leading; display only 28px light serif with -0.5px tracking (a deliberately small display, about 1.8:1 over body). Field cells roughly 140x30px, 4px radius, one tone darker than the rail, 11px tracked caps. Numbered steps use hanging two-digit numerals. Colours are approximate because the capture was dimmed: stone #e6e0d6, bone #f4f0e8, ink #382b1f, terracotta #b55d2e, status red #a3271f, slate #5a5651. Imagery: botanical still lifes and seasonal artefacts; quotes from press in a quiet carousel. Absent: product grid, prices in the hero, basket, promo colour.
directions.typeStack: Observed: FfernType and FfernTypeMono (custom, body and labels) with Spectral light for headings. Free stand-ins: Spectral 300 (Google, the real face) for display; Karla (Google) at 15px with 0.25px tracking for body; DM Mono caps for field values.
directions.motion: Entrance: the ledger fills itself like a clerk completing a form (caret, about 30ms per character, rows in order), then the right column image fades up over 900ms. Live: the countdown ticks each second with a soft digit roll; the status dot pulses on a 2.4s cycle. Scroll: only the right column moves, sections slide under sticky label bars; the rail never moves. Interaction: 'check availability' runs a three-step concierge flow in place and appends your number to the ledger as a fourth row. Easing slow ease-in-out, 600-900ms, nothing bouncy. Signature moment: the ledger typing itself in. Reduced motion: ledger present at load, countdown still live.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Thistle and Rime', four seasonal bitters a year, each batch made to a ledger of 2,000 members. IA: rail ledger (season, next release, list status); how the model works in three steps; this seasons story (ingredients, where they were gathered, the weather of the season); artefacts made alongside the release; press quotes; the join flow; questions; a line about the makers.
directions.photoBrief: Three or four free-licence botanical still lifes: sprigs of heather, lavender, thistle or dried grasses standing behind or on a rough stone, against a dark slate or grey plaster wall; soft north-window light from the left, matte and low saturation with fine grain; portrait 4:5 and one 16:9 crop. One overhead of a hand-painted slipware plate with dark plums. Treatment: slight warm grade, no props, no hands. Fallback if no stock fits: an SVG botanical plate in two inks on slate.
directions.whyWorldClass: The business model is the interface: a ledger, a season and a countdown replace the shop grid, and the restraint (28px display, form-like fields, one status sentence in red) makes scarcity feel administrative and true rather than hyped.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: countdown-rsvp-launch, private-bank-ledger, engraved-ledger, auction-lot. Those are launch pages or ledger skins; this is a commerce flow in which a fixed form-like status rail is the brands main voice and the product is sold by season and membership, not by catalogue.
directions.buildRisk: Without a strong still life the right column is flat, and the rail can look like a generic sidebar. Dodge: build the field cells as real inset form fields with mono caps and a live ticking value; source one excellent botanical image or paint an SVG plate; never open a modal on load (the real site hides its own hero this way). Mobile: collapse the rail into a three-row ledger strip pinned under the wordmark so the signature survives at 390px.

directions.name: Dashed-territory map of hyperlinks
directions.signature: A black viewport filled edge to edge with about ninety white underlined 16px serif links, positioned as places on a map and enclosed by a dozen loose dashed outlines in different hues (green, violet, cyan, amber, coral, grey) that overlap like a hand-drawn Venn diagram. Each territory is named once in bold 18px sans in its own colour. A row of tiny native-looking buttons sits bottom left: random, evening, a labels checkbox, info, submit, view index, and one in yellow.
directions.grammar: No grid; position carries meaning (a link inside three outlines belongs to three communities). Links: system serif 16px, underlined, about one per 150x45px. Territory labels: bold sans 18px. Outlines: 2px dashed (6 on, 5 off), closed organic blobs, no fills. Canvas larger than the viewport in both directions. Palette: #000 ground, #fff links, eight outline hues of similar lightness, one yellow button. Controls look like default form buttons at 12px. Absent: header, logo, hero copy, images, cards, hover cards.
directions.typeStack: Observed: default Times for links and Arial bold for labels, no webfonts loaded. Free stand-ins: system stack, or Tinos plus Arimo (Google).
directions.motion: Entrance: outlines draw themselves one territory at a time (stroke-dashoffset, 900ms each, overlapping by half), each followed by its links fading in. Hover: every outline that contains the link brightens and its dashes march, all other territories drop to 25% opacity. Controls: 'random' flies the view to one link (700ms ease-in-out); 'evening' inverts to a paper-coloured day mode; 'labels' toggles territory names; 'view index' collapses the map into an alphabetical list with a FLIP transition. Panning: drag with inertia; keep vertical document scroll as the primary pan so the page still scrolls on the root. Signature moment: the outlines drawing on load. Reduced motion: static map plus the index list.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'A Field Guide to the Small Web, 2026 edition', a directory of 120 independent sites grouped by overlapping communities. IA: the map; index view (alphabetical and by territory); info (what this is, who keeps it); submit a site; legend of territories with one-line definitions; changelog of additions by date.
directions.whyWorldClass: Pure information design with no styling to hide behind: overlapping membership is shown spatially, the typography is the browsers own, and it is still beautiful and endlessly explorable. A jury would not expect it and could not dismiss it.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: infinite-canvas, game-map-room-nav, svgmap-journey, chord-diagram-hero (and the sibling scout's walkable-line-atlas). This differs as a Venn-territory diagram of live hyperlinks in default type where overlap is the data; there is no illustration, route or chart metaphor.
directions.buildRisk: Hand-placing 100-plus links and drawing convincing loose blobs is laborious, and density collapses on 390px. Dodge: generate link positions with a seeded force relaxation per territory, build outlines from padded convex hulls smoothed with Catmull-Rom and slight noise, then bake to static SVG; on mobile open centred on the densest overlap with 13px links and two-axis pan, and expose the index list as the accessible alternative.

directions.name: Ruled Ticker Programme

exemplars.site: Museum of Modern Art in Warsaw

directions.signature: At scroll 0: a regular-weight grotesk wordmark set to fill the full content width (fit with JS or vw units, cap height near 200px at 1440) with one hand-drawn sticker shape rotated -8deg overlapping its last three letters; a one-line caps descriptor at 40px under it; then a 6px black rule and at least three programme rows visible, each about 155px tall, each a single inline run: two-line date tag (40px caps) + small 3:2 thumbnail at row height + TITLE in 104px uppercase + an arrow drawn at cap height + a secondary label, the run wider than the viewport and clipped at the right edge. On 390px the same rows shrink to about 70px tall with 50px type and still overflow.
directions.grammar: Grid: none in the column sense; the page is a stack of full-bleed horizontal bands separated by 6px solid black rules (3px on mobile), left margin 36px, no right margin because rows bleed off. Type: one neo-grotesk at weight 400 only, uppercase for rows; three sizes total (about 200px wordmark, 104px rows with line-height 0.95, 22px nav/body), so display:body is roughly 5:1 and wordmark:body 9:1; tracking normal, not tightened. Spacing: rows are tight (text nearly touches the rules, about 25px padding), generous only above the wordmark. Colour: pure white ground, #0A0A0A text, one neon green (#1CFF1C) button, one yellow sticker, one red round badge; all other colour comes from the thumbnails. Imagery: thumbnails are tiny (195x130) and inline with the text baseline like emoji, never hero-sized. Chrome: text nav left (Visit, What's on, icons), underlined membership link, green ticket button, 'Menu' word plus icon at 28px. Absent: hero image, cards, columns, bold weight, any grey.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Union Regular (Radim Pesko) for everything, plus a hand-lettered sticker face. Free stand-ins: Arimo 400 or Fontshare Switzer 400 for the Helvetica/Arial-hybrid voice (keep it at regular weight, do not go bold); sticker lettering can be an inline SVG path or Google 'Rubik Bubbles'/'Climate Crisis' rotated on a yellow parallelogram. For the Warsaw-style serif variant use Google 'Bodoni Moda' caps or Fontshare 'Boska' tracked +0.03em.
directions.motion: Entrance: wordmark letters are already in place; the 6px rules draw left to right in 300ms each, staggered 60ms, then rows unmask. Scroll: the wordmark scrubs from full-width into a 30px-high copy centred in a sticky white header (sticker travels with it and stays overlapped); rows translate on X at different slow constant speeds (alternating direction optional), pausing on hover. Micro: hover on a row inverts it (black band, white type) in under 100ms and the thumbnail scales from row height to 1.6x, overlapping neighbours; the arrow nudges 12px. Signature moment: the masthead collapse into the header with the sticker still stuck on it. Reduced motion: rows static, left-aligned and clipped; header swaps without scrub.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Museum Halvemaan, a municipal museum of modern art and design in a port city. IA natural to the genre: 1) wordmark + descriptor; 2) WHAT'S ON ticker rows (8-10: new exhibition, kids festival with date range, opening soon, design retrospective, guided tour with round badge, late opening); 3) a membership row ('BECOME A FRIEND' + two-line perk text at 40px); 4) Visit band (hours, address, ticket prices as one giant row each); 5) Collection row linking to 'ONLINE COLLECTION 90,000 WORKS'; 6) colophon rows (newsletter input as a row, partners, languages).
directions.whyWorldClass: It makes the listing itself the monument: no hero, no cards, the programme is readable from across a room and the whole identity is carried by one typeface at one weight plus a thick rule. The sticker and inline thumbnails add wit without a second layout system, and it scales to mobile without changing the idea.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: festival-lineup-poster, nested-marquee-matrix, conference-schedule-grid, swiss-poster. Differs: those treat type as poster or marquee decoration; this is an operational listing where each ticker row is a record (date + inline thumbnail + title + arrow) under heavy rules, with a collapsing sticker wordmark. Museum register, regular weight, no grid.
directions.buildRisk: Falls flat if the type goes bold or the rows get padding and become 'cards'; keep weight 400, row padding under 28px and rules at 6px. Thumbnails need to look like real artworks: generate 8-10 small SVG/CSS abstract compositions (dot fields, concentric rings, colour planes) rather than grey placeholders. Rows must be visibly cut off at the right edge at scroll 0 so the ticker idea reads in a still. Fit-to-width wordmark needs a resize handler or it will under-fill on some viewports.

directions.name: Bracket Metadata Megalist
directions.signature: At scroll 0: a 48px-high header whose left 25 percent is a white tab holding the archive name in 14px bold caps and whose remaining 75 percent is a flat pure-blue bar (#1F00FF) carrying six filters written as '[ ] Label' in white 11px text, the active one shown as '[x]' on the white tab; a second line of file-type filters in black ('[ ] .jpg [ ] .pdf [ ] .mp4'); then nine or ten archive rows filling the viewport, each row = a 250px left column with four 12px label/value pairs (values in blue inside square brackets) and, to its right, the item title on ONE line at 95px/0.83 medium grotesk that is deliberately longer than the viewport and clipped at the right edge. On 390px the title drops to 44px and stays one clipped line with the bracket metadata stacked under it.
directions.grammar: Grid: two columns only, 250px fixed metadata rail + fluid title lane; left margin 16px, zero right margin (titles bleed). Type: one neo-grotesk at weight 500; two sizes only, 95px titles and 12px metadata, a ratio of 8:1 with nothing in between; title line-height 0.83 so descenders nearly touch the next row; metadata leading 1.25. Spacing: rows are exactly one title line tall (about 87px), no gaps, no rules; rhythm comes from the repeating metadata blocks. Colour: white, black, one web-default blue for anything clickable; no greys. Imagery: none in the list; on hover or expand an image strip of 4 portrait thumbnails slides in ABOVE the title (seen on mobile where thumbnails are always shown). Chrome: bracket checkboxes as the entire filter UI, '[0] Cart' counter in the same syntax. Absent: cards, thumbnails by default, icons, pagination, hero, section headings.
directions.typeStack: Observed: SBM (custom neo-grotesk close to Suisse Int'l / ABC Diatype Medium) at Visual Society; Arial at Roma Publications and Buchholz; Archivo + Crimson Pro at Triple Canopy. Free stand-ins: Inter 500 with letter-spacing -0.02em or Geist 500 for the megalist; Arimo for a Roma-style ledger variant; keep brackets and the slashed-zero/empty-set glyph for null values.
directions.motion: Entrance: rows print top to bottom one line every 40ms like a query result returning (no fades, opacity jumps 0 to 1). Scroll: plain document scroll; the blue filter bar is sticky; a live result counter in the bar ticks as rows enter. Micro: hovering a row slides its title left along X so the clipped tail becomes readable (a per-row marquee driven by hover, 600ms linear) and turns bracket values from blue to black-on-blue; clicking a '[ ]' filter fills it with 'x' and non-matching rows collapse to 0 height in 180ms steps. Signature moment: ticking a filter and watching the giant list re-flow instantly, row heights snapping shut. Reduced motion: filters apply with no collapse animation, titles do not slide (wrap to two lines on hover instead).
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Office for Loose Pages (OLP), an artist-book publisher and exhibition space publishing its complete archive since 2009. IA: 1) filter bar (Content type, Year, Place, Collaborator, Search, About, Cart) with counts; 2) megalist of about 40 records across types (Book, Edition, Exhibition, Lecture, Press, Object) with type-specific metadata (Pages/Size/Price/Buy for books; Location/Collaborators/Year for events); 3) one expanded record state showing an image strip and a 3-line description; 4) About as a single 34px paragraph; 5) colophon in bracket syntax ([Typeface], [Code], [Last updated]).
directions.whyWorldClass: An archive that reads as both database and poster: the 8:1 scale jump with nothing in between is a real typographic decision, and the bracket syntax turns filtering, pricing and metadata into one consistent written language. It is what curators and publishers actually ship in 2025-2026 instead of card grids.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: editorial-index, anchor-annotated-index, museum-collection-explorer, minimal-mono-type. Differs: those are tidy indexes or thumbnail explorers; this is a clipped one-line megalist at 95px with a bracketed metadata rail and typographic checkbox filters, no images by default and no mono face.
directions.buildRisk: Reads as a plain list if titles are short enough to fit; write long, specific titles (type + quoted name + publication + place) so every row is cut by the right edge. Do not add row dividers or thumbnails to 'help'. Needs 35+ believable records, so the content writing is the real work. Filter logic must actually work (data attributes + a small script) or the bracket UI is a prop.

directions.name: Sticky Megatype, Dashed Dossier
directions.signature: At scroll 0: the left half of the viewport is filled top to bottom by five stacked nav words (for example News, Season, Artists, Agenda, Search) in a medium grotesk at 164px with letter-spacing -0.09em and line-height 0.76, so characters collide and each line overlaps the next; the right half shows two 1px DASHED rounded boxes (radius 6px), each starting with a heading in the same 164px collided type and continuing in 11px monospace paragraphs with underlined links. Pure black on pure white; a hand-scribbled outline monogram top left, a language code in a 34px circle top right. On 390px: the nav words stack at about 88px above the first dashed box, which becomes full width.
directions.grammar: Grid: strict 50/50 split, 16px outer margin, 16px gutter; left column position:sticky, right column a vertical stack of boxes with 18px gaps. Type: two voices at the extremes: display grotesk 164px/0.76, tracking -0.09em, weight 500, sentence case; monospace 11px/1.5 for all prose; ratio 15:1 and nothing in between. Italic + underline inside the mono text for work titles. Spacing: boxes have 12px padding, headings sit hard against the top of the box; the page is dense on the right and empty under the nav on the left. Colour: #000 and #FFF only. Imagery: none on the landing view (deeper pages may place one uncropped image inside a dashed box). Chrome: the nav IS the left column; no header bar. Absent: images, colour, icons, buttons, rules other than the dashes.
directions.typeStack: Observed: a custom/licensed display grotesk (Next font var '__display', Helvetica-like, weight 400-500) + a monospace ('__mono', Diatype-Mono-like) at 11.1px. Free stand-ins: Inter Tight 500 at letter-spacing -0.09em (or Fontshare 'Switzer' Medium) for display; Google 'DM Mono' 400 or 'JetBrains Mono' 400 for text. PIN-UP variant: Arimo Bold caps.
directions.motion: Entrance: nav words drop in line by line from above with a hard stop (each 220ms, cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.2,1), 50ms stagger), then dashed borders 'march' once around each box (stroke-dashoffset) and settle. Scroll: left nav stays pinned; the word matching the box in view compresses its tracking a further -0.02em and the others drop to 25 percent black; boxes enter from below with no fade. Micro: hovering a nav word slides the others apart vertically by 10px (squeeze-and-stretch, as Hoverstat.es notes for similar sites); hovering a dashed box makes its dashes march continuously; links invert to white-on-black. Signature moment: the nav word tightening as its section arrives, like a pressed stamp. Reduced motion: no marching dashes, no drop-in, active nav word shown by underline only.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Compagnie Mistral, a national choreographic centre and touring dance company. IA: left nav (News, Season, Artists, Agenda, Search); right dossier boxes: 1) the artistic direction (collective bio with dated works in italics); 2) the company (who, where, since when); 3) Associated artist; 4) Studio residencies; 5) Agenda box: tour dates as a monospace table (date, city, venue, piece, ticket link); 6) Transmission/school; 7) contact and partners as a mono colophon.
directions.whyWorldClass: The 15:1 jump between collided megatype and 11px mono is the whole design, and it works because nothing sits in between: no subheads, no lead paragraphs. Dashed boxes give a provisional, working-document feel that suits a living institution and is rarely seen at this level of polish.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: split-master-detail, swiss-poster, minimal-mono-type, soft-brutalism. Differs: not a master-detail app shell or poster; a pinned megatype nav with -0.09em collided letterforms against dashed dossier boxes of 11px mono, black and white only.
directions.buildRisk: Timid tracking kills it: letters must actually touch (test -0.085em to -0.1em per font) and line-height must be under 0.8 with overflow visible so descenders are not clipped. The right column needs long, real institutional prose in mono (names, years, italic titles) or the boxes look like placeholders. Keep the nav words short and of different lengths so the left block has a ragged silhouette.

directions.name: Stepped-Crop Name, Ink Flood Reader
directions.signature: At scroll 0: one name in lowercase medium grotesk sized to span the full width (about 150px x-height at 1440) repeated in six rows; each row is a clipped window onto the same word, with window heights stepping roughly 40, 85, 105, 125, 140 and 165px, so the top row shows only the tips of the ascenders and dots and the bottom row the complete word: the name appears to rise out of the page in slices. Off-white paper ground with a faint texture, near-black ink, two initials top left and four 14px nav words top right. On 390px: the same six stepped slices with the name broken onto two lines per slice or scaled to width.
directions.grammar: Grid: single full-bleed column, 16px margins; hero slices separated by about 12px of paper. Type: one grotesk, weight 500, lowercase for the name; reading text at 34px/1.27 on a measure of about 75 characters (very large for body: display:body only 4:1, the reading size itself is the luxury); nav 14px. Spacing: paragraphs separated by a full blank line; text starts at the very top edge after the hero. Colour: two states: paper (#FAFAF8) with black, then a total flood of one process ink (cyan about #0099D8) with the same black text; images are monochrome and multiplied into the flood colour so they read as darker cyan rectangles BEHIND the text. Chrome: four words, underlined when active. Absent: headings inside the text, captions, cards, colour other than the one ink.
directions.typeStack: Observed: ABC Monument Grotesk Medium throughout (name, 34px text, 14px nav). Free stand-ins: Google 'Schibsted Grotesk' 600 or Fontshare 'General Sans' Semibold for the name; same family at 500 for the reading text. System-style variant: Google 'Tinos' Bold (Times metric) in cyan.
directions.motion: Entrance: the six slices open from 0 height to their stepped heights top to bottom (each 350ms ease-out, 70ms stagger), like blinds. Scroll: as the hero leaves, slice heights equalise and the rows merge into one full name that shrinks into the 'H S' initials; simultaneously the background floods from paper to ink (a hard linear 300ms change triggered at one scroll position, or a clip-path wipe rising from the bottom). Tinted photographs drift slower than the text beneath it. Micro: hovering a paragraph de-tints the photo behind it to full greyscale; nav words underline instantly. Signature moment: the ink flood taking over the whole page while the text stays put. Reduced motion: slices static at final heights, background changes with no transition, photos fixed.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: the estate of Ines Calloway (1931-2009), poet, editor and translator; an official archive site. IA natural to an author estate: 1) stepped name hero; 2) Biography in flood colour (12-15 short paragraphs with years, magazines founded, scandals, prizes); 3) Index: every publication as a year-ordered ruled list; 4) Poems: five or six poems set one per screen at 34px, each on its own ink colour; 5) Archive: a contact-sheet strip of tinted documents and photographs with dates; 6) colophon (estate contact, rights).
directions.whyWorldClass: It turns a name into architecture with a single clipping trick and then commits to a reading experience at 34px on a flooded ink ground, which is far braver than a 18px article column. Photographs as tinted ghosts under the text keep the page typographic while still carrying the archive.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: text-clip-reveal, blind-mask-wipe, variable-font-pressure, manifesto-essay. Differs: the stepped crop is a static scroll-0 composition (six graded slices of one word), not a transition effect, and it hands over to a whole-page process-ink reading mode with images multiplied behind 34px text.
directions.buildRisk: The slices must be cut through the letterforms at the right places (top rows showing only ascender tips); implement as six overflow:hidden boxes with the same text anchored to the bottom, and tune heights against the chosen font's ascender/x-height. If the name has no ascenders or dots in the first rows the top slices look empty, so pick a fictional name with b/d/h/k/l/t/i letters. Tinted images: any greyscale image with mix-blend-mode multiply over the ink works, so the factory's painting/interior can be reused; do not show them in full colour.

directions.name: Alphabet Wheel Slab Index
directions.signature: At scroll 0: a slab-serif masthead in caps tracked out so its first and last letters touch the 22px margins (cap height about 110px), with the full current date in 17px slab above its left end and the word 'Menu' above its right end; below, a single portrait image 525px wide centred with white on both sides; bottom left a three-line caption beginning with a small arrow glyph (name, issue number and year, photographer). To make the index signature visible in the thumbnail, dock the alphabet ring (a 280px circle of 27 slab glyphs, '#' then A-Z, with a fixed arrow at 12 o'clock) in the white space right of the cover. On 390px: masthead on one line at about 30px cap height, cover full width, ring at 180px under it.
directions.grammar: Grid: masthead full-bleed; cover on a centred 525px column; index on a 2-column block occupying the left half (columns 316px apart) with the wheel centred in the right half and vertically sticky. Type: ONE slab face at one weight; sizes 17px (date, captions), 26px (index entries, line-height 1.15), about 150px (masthead); the index is set solid with 1.5px black rules between letter groups and a dash + letter label above each group. Spacing: margins 22px; cover has about 20px air under the masthead; index groups 22px padding. Colour: white, black, and the photograph. Chrome: date, masthead, Menu; nothing else. Absent: sans-serif, grey, cards, thumbnails in the index, section navigation.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Diplomat (beta; a wide Clarendon/Egyptian slab) for all text; masthead drawn in the same family. Free stand-ins: Google 'Besley' 500 (closest Clarendon), or 'Hepta Slab' 500; widen with font-stretch if using a variable cut, track masthead with JS to fit. Gentlewoman variant: Google 'Jost' 500 for the Futura voice.
directions.motion: Entrance: masthead letters start bunched in the centre and track outward to the margins in 700ms ease-out; date types on. Scroll: the wheel's rotation is bound to the scroll progress of the A-Z list (rotate so the current letter sits under the fixed arrow), moving in 13.3deg detents with a slight overshoot; the active letter group's rule thickens from 1.5px to 4px. Micro: dragging or clicking the wheel scrolls the list to that letter; hovering a name shows a 120px portrait chip beside the wheel; '(Spin the wheel)' caption nudges. Signature moment: spinning the ring and the index snapping to the letter. Reduced motion: wheel jumps without rotation animation, masthead static.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: CORRESPONDENT, a biannual journal of men, manners and clothes. IA natural to a personality-led magazine: 1) dated masthead; 2) cover story (one portrait + three-line credit); 3) The Index: A-Z of every person and subject ever featured (about 90 entries, two columns) with the wheel; 4) Current issue contents as a ruled list with page numbers; 5) three 'Recommendations' short texts set as letters; 6) subscribe + stockists list by city; 7) colophon/masthead of staff.
directions.photoBrief: One editorial portrait, 3:4 portrait crop, subject in tailoring or knitwear, direct or three-quarter gaze, hard flash or studio light against a flat or screen-like coloured background (the observed cover used a magenta/blue video-wall backdrop); saturated but not retouched-glossy; no text in frame. Optionally 6-8 small square head shots for index hover chips.
directions.whyWorldClass: A single slab typeface doing masthead, index and captions is the most disciplined magazine identity on the web right now, and the alphabet wheel is a genuinely delightful, mechanical alternative to search that suits a title built on people. It is editorial confidence without a single trend effect.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: radial-hub-menu, text-on-path-poster, editorial-index, magazine-takeover. Differs: the ring is a scroll-bound A-Z dial for a ruled two-column name index (not a menu or poster ornament), in a one-typeface slab system with a fit-to-width dated masthead and a single centred cover.
directions.buildRisk: Needs one strong portrait-format photograph; without it the page is a masthead over a void. The factory's painting can stand in (crop to 3:4, treat as the 'cover story' on an artist) but a stock portrait is better. The ring must be visible at scroll 0 for the thumbnail (place it beside the cover), and glyphs on the ring need correct per-letter rotation (27 absolutely positioned spans or SVG textPath). Slab must be a true Clarendon; a geometric slab (Roboto Slab) breaks the tone.

directions.name: Monument Serif Noir Museum

exemplars.site: Museum of Modern Art in Warsaw

directions.signature: At scroll 0: pure black page; the institution's three-word name set as three stacked lines of flared display-serif caps (about 125px, line-height 0.95, weight 500), ranged left on a column that starts 176px in from the left edge so the stack steps outward like a stoop; 100px of black; then the top edge of a single wide installation photograph on the same column. In the outer gutters, two tiny marginal items (48px thumbnail, 13px grey caps caption, an action word 'Watch' or 'Read'). Top right: 'PLAN YOUR VISIT' in 15px sans, search glyph, two-line burger. On 390px: name at 60px three lines, photo full column, then the first exhibition title in white caps with its date in grey at the same size.
directions.grammar: Grid: a 1088px centre column (two 532px halves with a 24px gutter) flanked by 160px margins that hold marginalia; images are never full-bleed. Type: display flared serif caps for names and exhibition titles; a humanist sans for dates and types. The key rule: title and date are the SAME size (64px/1.0), differentiated only by case and colour (white caps serif vs mid-grey #8A8A8A sentence-case sans), then a 26px white sans type line ('Exhibition', 'Artist-in-Residence'). Marginalia 13px caps grey. Spacing: 100px+ voids between blocks, text set tight to images (8px). Colour: #000 ground, #FFF, one grey; colour only inside photographs. Imagery: un-styled installation views with visible floor and ceiling. Chrome: minimal top-right cluster. Absent: buttons, cards, rules, overlays on images, any accent colour.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Studio Museum Black Glare (display, customised from Pangram Pangram's Fragment) + Studio Museum Black Sans; MSN Qwerty + MSN Next (Warsaw); Suisse Works + Suisse Int'l (Kronborg). Free stand-ins: Google 'Fraunces' (opsz 144, SOFT 0, WONK 0, wght 500) or Fontshare 'Gambetta' Medium for the flared display caps; Google 'Hanken Grotesk' 400-500 for the sans. Warsaw variant: 'Bodoni Moda' caps +0.03em with 'Jost' caps.
directions.motion: Entrance: the three name lines rise from behind a mask one after another (500ms, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), 90ms stagger); the photo fades from black over 800ms. Scroll: the name stack collapses to a single 20px line in the header; images do not parallax; marginalia items are sticky within their section so they ride alongside the main column for a moment before releasing. Micro: hovering an exhibition block swaps the grey date to white and the white title to grey (a two-tone flip, 120ms); marginal thumbnails enlarge to 160px in place. Signature moment: the title/date colour flip on hover across a same-size pair. Reduced motion: no mask rise, no sticky marginalia, instant colour flip.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Meridian House Museum, a collecting museum of contemporary art in a harbour district, newly reopened. IA: 1) stacked name; 2) lead installation image + current headline exhibition (title, 'Through' date, type); 3) two-up exhibitions grid (4-6 pairs); 4) gutter marginalia: Watch (building film), Read (staff pick with accession caption), Listen (podcast); 5) Plan your visit as three giant same-size lines (hours white, address grey, admission white); 6) collection teaser: one object with a full tombstone caption; 7) membership + newsletter as plain text links; footer credits.
directions.photoBrief: 6-8 installation views of contemporary art in white-cube rooms: wide, eye-level, straight verticals, polished concrete or grey floor visible, even daylight-balanced light, one or two coloured walls (ochre, deep blue) for variety, works small in frame, no visitors; landscape 4:3 and 3:2; no grading. Plus 3 tiny thumbnails (building exterior, archival black-and-white photo, a drawing) for marginalia.
directions.whyWorldClass: The same-size white-title/grey-date pairing is a subtle, learned typographic move that makes a programme scannable without a single rule or label, and the gutter marginalia give the page a second, quieter voice the way footnotes do in a well-made catalogue. Black ground with un-styled documentation feels like an institution, not a brand campaign.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: silent-luxury-restraint, museum-collection-explorer, gallery-corridor, gothic-horror-editorial. Differs: not luxury-product restraint or a 3D corridor; a black institutional page built on monumental flared-serif caps with same-size two-tone title/date pairs and footnote-like marginalia in the gutters around a narrow centre column.
directions.buildRisk: Entirely dependent on credible installation photography: generic stock 'gallery interior' images or AI images with warped frames will sink it. Source a consistent free-licence set (same white-cube room type) or render simple gallery rooms in CSS/SVG (white walls in perspective, grey floor, coloured rectangles as works) and accept an object-render classification. The serif must be flared and weighty; a thin Didone turns it into fashion.

directions.name: Corner-Numeral Issue Shelf
directions.signature: At scroll 0: a flat pastel ground (pink #FBE6F0) with exactly five things on it: a centred serif caps wordmark at 22px; three text links top left and one top right at 20px; ONE magazine cover, about 485x585px, centred with a 12px spine strip in a contrasting mint and a soft contact shadow; and in the bottom corners two old-style-figure numerals at 56px (year left, volume.issue right) with 'All (148)' underlined between them. On 390px: cover at 300px wide, numerals at 40px pinned to the bottom corners.
directions.grammar: Grid: everything on the centre axis or in the four corners; 20px margins; the cover occupies roughly 65 percent of viewport height. Type: a Garamond-class serif with old-style figures for numerals and wordmark; nav in the same serif at 20px; display numerals 56px; ratio under 3:1, hierarchy comes from position and emptiness, not size. Spacing: at least 100px of clear ground on every side of the cover. Colour: one flat pastel per issue (the ground changes with the cover: pink, pale blue, butter, sage), black text, the cover supplies saturated colour. Imagery: the cover as a physical object (spine, shadow), nothing else. Chrome: text links with a 1px underline for the active one. Absent: grids of covers on first view, buttons, cards, prices, any sans-serif.
directions.typeStack: Observed: 'Practice' (Garamond-like display serif with old-style figures) + 'Plain' sans at Surfer's Journal Archives; Kinfolk Serif Deck/Display + Kinfolk Sans; Futura TGW at The Gentlewoman; Times bold at System. Free stand-ins: Google 'Cormorant Garamond' 500-600 or 'EB Garamond' 500 with font-feature-settings 'onum' for the numerals; optional sans 'Instrument Sans'. Real Review variant: 'Hanken Grotesk' with a giant geometric initial drawn in SVG.
directions.motion: Entrance: the cover drops 16px onto the page and its shadow resolves (500ms); corner numerals count up to their values. Scroll: the first 600vh is a sticky shelf: each scroll step slides the current cover out left as the next arrives from the right with a slight rotation settle (like pulling issues off a shelf), the ground cross-fades to the next pastel, and the corner numerals roll like an odometer (year left, issue right). After the shelf releases, the selected issue's contents appear as a ruled list. Micro: hovering the cover tilts it 3deg in 3D and reveals the spine text; 'All (148)' expands into a dense grid of 40px thumbnails. Signature moment: the odometer roll of the corner numerals in sync with the cover swap and colour change. Reduced motion: covers cross-fade in place, numerals change without rolling.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: TIDEWATER QUARTERLY, the complete digital archive of an independent coastal culture journal (148 issues since 1989). IA natural to a magazine archive: 1) issue shelf (8-10 CSS-built covers, newest first) with year and volume.issue numerals; 2) contents of the selected issue: ruled list with page numbers, author, section; 3) Collections: curated reading sets as short titled lists; 4) a pull-quote spread from one feature at 40px serif; 5) Library/subscribe panel (print + archive access) in plain text; 6) colophon.
directions.whyWorldClass: It treats the issue as a collectable object and gives it a whole coloured room to itself; the old-style numerals in the corners are the only navigation feedback and they are beautiful. This is the calm, luxurious end of the lens, with nothing to hide behind.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: coverflow-3d, bibliophile-spread, magazine-takeover, silent-luxury-restraint. Differs: no carousel of many items or spread simulation; one cover alone on a per-issue pastel ground with corner old-style numerals acting as the index readout, scrubbed as a shelf.
directions.buildRisk: The covers carry it, and they must be designed, not placeholder rectangles: build 8-10 covers in CSS/SVG as strong typographic or two-ink illustrated designs (the Real Review face/letter system is the model: flat shapes, big letterform, barcode, issue line) or use the factory's painting and cinematic stills cropped as cover art under a serif title. Cheap-looking covers make the whole page look like a template shop. Keep the ground truly flat; a gradient ruins it.

directions.name: Interlocked Outline Wordmark Kunsthalle
directions.signature: At scroll 0: white page, top half empty except for a two or three-word institution name in thin geometric capitals about 200px tall, letter-spaced so tightly (about -0.18em, tuned per pair) that neighbouring letters overlap and interlock; every glyph is filled with one flat pastel (turquoise #00BFA5 on first view) and outlined with a 1.5px black stroke, with stroke painted above fill so overlapping shapes stay readable as line drawing. Below it, at the vertical centre, a full-width 1px black boxed nav bar 56px high (logo glyph + italic underlined current page left, three links centre, language pair and a boxed burger right). On 390px: name on two or three lines at 84px, nav box under it.
directions.grammar: Grid: 40px margins; the wordmark is centred and occupies about 75 percent of the width; content below hangs in a simple 12-column grid. Type: the interlocked outline caps are reserved for the name and for one headline per section (each section re-uses the device with a different pastel fill: lilac #EEDAFB, pale yellow #F0ECA0, turquoise); all other text is plain Helvetica-class sans at 16px/1.5; italic + underline marks the active nav item. Spacing: huge white voids (300px+) around each interlocked headline. Colour: white, black hairlines, three pastels used one at a time. Shapes: parallelogram tags (skewX about -20deg) with 1px black outline and pastel fill as the only buttons. Imagery: optional, small, below the fold. Absent: bold type, photography in the hero, drop shadows, solid dark blocks.
directions.typeStack: Observed: 'HDK Variable Fragment' (a custom variable cut of Pangram Pangram Fragment used as overlapping monoline caps) + Helvetica for text. Nieuwe Instituut: 'Cerial' (custom, dotted-to-slab) + 'Social'. Free stand-ins: Google 'Poiret One' or 'Julius Sans One' (monoline deco caps) with -webkit-text-stroke 1.5px #000, paint-order stroke fill, pastel color, letter-spacing -0.16em to -0.2em and per-letter spans for manual kerning; text in 'Arimo' or 'Inter' 400. Best fidelity: draw the 2-3 word lockup as inline SVG outlines.
directions.motion: Entrance: letters start at normal tracking, un-overlapped, then slide together into the interlocked state over 900ms (ease-in-out), the black outlines drawing just before the pastel fills in. Scroll: at each section the fixed wordmark's letters shuffle apart and re-interlock to spell that section's headline with a new pastel fill (letter-spacing and content swap at the section boundary); the boxed nav sticks to the top after it is passed. Micro: hovering a letter lifts it above its neighbours (z-index swap) and deepens its fill; parallelogram tags shear a further 6deg on hover. Signature moment: the letters pulling together into the lock on load. Reduced motion: wordmark renders interlocked immediately; section headlines swap without shuffle.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: HALLE NORD, a non-collecting kunsthalle in a former customs hall. IA: 1) interlocked name; 2) boxed nav (What's on, Plan your visit, Arts and Ideas, DE/EN); 3) What's on: 3-4 exhibitions, each announced by an interlocked outline headline in its own pastel with dates and a 3-line text; 4) parallelogram tags for Club and Tickets; 5) Plan your visit: hours table, access, admission; 6) Arts and Ideas: three essays/talks as plain text teasers; 7) footer with funders as text.
directions.whyWorldClass: A wordmark that behaves like a variable ligature system is the most distinctive identity idea seen in the survey, and outlining the overlaps turns a legibility problem into the visual signature. It is mostly empty white space and still unmistakable, which is the definition of high-taste minimalism with character.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: svg-paint-order-poster, variable-font-axis-playground, kinetic-broken-grid, art-deco-luxe. Differs: not a font-axis demo or deco pastiche; an institutional system where thin caps physically overlap with outline-over-pastel-fill, re-set per section, paired with a hairline boxed nav and parallelogram tags on an otherwise empty white page.
directions.buildRisk: Highest typographic risk in the set: with a generic thin font and uniform negative tracking the overlaps look like a bug. Kern every pair by hand (per-letter spans with individual margins) or draw the lockups in SVG, and make sure paint-order puts the stroke on top so intersections read. Choose words whose letters nest well (A, H, U, O, K, N, T, S). Keep the stroke at 1.5px; thicker reads as cartoon.

directions.name: Outline Shapes Over Poster Type

exemplars.site: HKW Haus der Kulturen der Welt

directions.signature: At scroll 0: a two-line title in condensed regular-weight grotesk at 200px/0.82 (for example a prize name and year) starting 44px from the left and running past the right edge, where the beginning of the same title in the second language is visible, cut off; over the type, three outline shapes with 5px strokes and no fill, each a different process colour and a different geometry (cyan arch 490x850, teal parallelogram skewed -17deg, pink rectangle 580x850), overlapping each other and the letters; each shape carries one lowercase label at 30px in its own colour, sitting where the shape is empty; small 22px condensed text begins at the bottom edge inside the shapes. On 390px: title at 84px on three lines, shapes scaled to overlap as a cluster below it.
directions.grammar: Grid: none; a poster composition. The title fixes the top-left, the three shapes form a horizontal chain across the viewport, body text is anchored bottom-left in two columns of about 780px. Type: one condensed sans at regular weight in three sizes: 200px title, 30px labels, 22px text (line-height 1.2), plus 12px captions; ratio 9:1. Colour: white, black type, three stroke colours (cyan #12B5F5, teal #0DB89E, pink #F56CB4) used only as lines and their labels. Shapes are the navigation: the entire outlined area is the hit target. Bilingual by duplication: the second language is a full copy of the page sitting to the right, reached by a horizontal shift. Absent: filled blocks, images, buttons, header bar, footer.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Zurich Condensed BT (Bitstream's Univers Condensed) for everything, 201.6px/165.6px, tracking -1.6px, body 22.4px/26.9px. Free stand-ins: Google 'Roboto Condensed' 400 or 'Archivo Narrow' 400 (closest in width and neutrality); avoid extra-condensed display faces. HKW variant: 'Fira Sans' Bold with text on an SVG circle path.
directions.motion: Entrance: title is static; the three shapes draw themselves stroke-first (stroke-dashoffset, 900ms each, staggered 150ms) in the order cyan, teal, pink, then labels pop in. Scroll: shapes are position:fixed while text scrolls beneath them, so they act as coloured viewfinders framing different passages; each shape drifts a few pixels at its own rate. Micro: hovering a shape fills it with its colour at 12 percent and thickens the stroke to 9px, label underlines; the parallelogram shears 4deg further. Pressing Shift (or a visible 'DE / EN' toggle on touch) slides the whole page one viewport left to the other language (500ms ease-in-out). Signature moment: the page shift between languages with the shapes staying fixed. Reduced motion: shapes drawn instantly and static, language switch is an instant swap.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Prix Garamont 2026, an annual prize for the most beautiful books, run by an independent book-design society. IA natural to a prize microsite: 1) title + year; 2) three shape-links (archive, jury, submit); 3) awardees statement in two languages (main prize + ten honourable mentions as a run-in list of designer and title); 4) the awarded books as a typographic list with format, pages, printer, binder; 5) jury of five with one-line bios; 6) call for entries with deadline and fee; 7) past years as a row of year numerals.
directions.whyWorldClass: It collapses poster and interface: the navigation is three drawn shapes thrown across the headline, with colour used only as line. The bilingual side-by-side structure is an honest, clever answer to a real cultural-site problem and makes the cut-off right edge part of the composition.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: swiss-poster, swiss-international-typographic, text-on-path-poster, bilingual-epigraph. Differs: the Swiss templates are grid-and-block compositions; here large unfilled outline shapes overlap the condensed headline and each other as the actual link targets, and the two languages exist as side-by-side page copies reached by a lateral shift.
directions.buildRisk: Looks like a wireframe if the strokes are thin or the shapes are tidy and non-overlapping: keep 5px strokes, three different geometries, and make them cross the letterforms and one another. Horizontal language shift must not create page-level horizontal scroll (factory rule: document scrolls on root, no overflow on mobile): wrap both language panels in an overflow:hidden track and translate it; at scroll 0 let the second panel peek 140px at the right edge on desktop only, and drop the peek on 390px.

directions.name: Riviera arch portal: saturated field, condensed didone, copperplate script

exemplars.site: ERA Residence (The First The Last) - Awwwards Site of the Month Aug 2026
Sobha Privy Collection (Vide Infra) - Awwwards SOTD 23 Sep 2026

directions.signature: At scroll=0 a deep saturated field (aubergine, not black) framed by a 1px chamfered-corner border; dead centre a tall arch portal (33vw wide, rising from the bottom edge to 20vh from the top, two concentric hairline arcs around it) already open onto a sunlit scene; the condensed didone caps wordmark sits across the arch crown with one copperplate script word overlapping its last line; two letter-spaced caps words (0.6em tracking) sit left and right of the arch on the horizontal centre line; a ghost script word at 4-6 percent contrast fills the whole background. On 390px the arch takes 78vw and the two side words stack above and below.
directions.grammar: Grid: strictly centred axis; everything hangs off one vertical centre line that is literally drawn as a hairline between sections. Margins 22-24px to the frame, content column about 800px for statements. Type scale: display condensed didone caps 56-72px set tight (leading 0.92) for 3-line centred statements, script 2.5x the caps size used for one word only, UI in extended grotesque bold caps at 11-14px with 0.08em tracking; ratio display to UI about 5:1, no body paragraphs longer than 3 lines.
