Colour: three flat saturated fields used as whole sections (aubergine, sky blue rgb 181,206,221, ivory rgb 242,240,232) with navy rgb 23,35,59 and ivory ink; one hot accent arrives only as imagery (bougainvillea magenta). Imagery: one scene behind the arch, plus cut-out botanical elements that overlap section edges. Chrome: no nav bar; a rotating circular text badge top left, a two-line didone text link top right (SELECT / AN APARTMENT underlined), a vertical progress line with a numeral on the left edge, a 1 - line - 2 pager. Absent: cards, shadows, gradients, icons, rounded corners, gold.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Ambroise Francois (condensed didone), Sloop Script Three, Maison Neue Extended. Free stand-ins: Gambarino (Fontshare) or Bodoni Moda (Google, opsz max) compressed with scaleX 0.74 for the caps; Pinyon Script or Imperial Script (Google) for the copperplate; Archivo at wdth 125 wght 600-700 (Google variable) for the extended UI caps.
directions.motion: Entrance: frame border draws corner to corner (0.9s), centre hairline grows downward, wordmark fades up letter group by letter group, then the arch mask opens from a 2px slit to full width (1.2s ease-out) revealing the scene; ghost script drifts 2 percent laterally forever. Scroll: the arch scales to full bleed as a pinned transition into the next colour field (the field colour floods from the arch outward); statements reveal line by line with a 12px rise; the side numeral counts with scroll progress; cut-out botanicals parallax at 1.15x. Micro: links underline from left, badge rotates 20s per turn and speeds up on hover, pager line fills. Signature motion moment: the arch becoming the next section. Reduced motion: arch rendered open, no flood, sections simply change colour.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Cala Verano, 42 residences on a Balearic headland. IA natural to prime property: gate with monogram and arch; one-line promise; the range statement (interior areas in square metres set in didone numerals); residence selector table (type, bedrooms, interior, terrace, orientation, status); amenities as a 1-2-3 pager of colour fields; location by minutes (airport, marina, old town); architect's note with signature in script; private viewing request with a single field row.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is the clearest 2026 example of luxury signalled through colour and letterform confidence instead of darkness: three saturated fields, one ornamental device (the arch) used as navigation, layout and transition at once, and a type trio where every face has exactly one job. It won Site of the Month on that restraint, not on WebGL.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: property-developer-presales (page purpose), art-deco-luxe and sealed-invitation (ornamental frame). Differs by the Mediterranean saturated palette, the condensed didone plus copperplate couplet, and the arch portal as the single structural device and scroll transition; none of the listed slugs is built on a portal mask or on colour-field flooding.
directions.buildRisk: Wordmark-only hero is the trap (the real site rests on it for 2 seconds): keep the arch open at rest so the thumbnail shows the device. The scene behind the arch needs to be good: use the factory interior or painting asset, or paint a pool-and-white-volumes scene in layered CSS gradients; a weak image kills it. Free didones are wider than Ambroise, so compress with scaleX and tighten tracking, and test Pinyon hairlines at 390px (keep script above 64px).

directions.name: Ultra-black grotesque wordmark spliced by hairline script, then a script colour flood

exemplars.site: House of Honey (Edoardo Lunardi, Eva Landaluce) - Awwwards SOTD 14 Jul 2026, Siteinspire Sep 2026
Tengile MalaMala Collection (DashDigital) - Awwwards HM Jul 2026

directions.signature: At scroll=0 a warm blush field; a two-word wordmark in ultra-black expanded grotesque caps fills the viewport width edge to edge (8px margins, cap height about 120px at 1440) and a hairline copperplate script connector word, 1.8x the cap height, slices diagonally through the gap between the words; directly under it two serif caps descriptors pinned to opposite margins; the top edge of one full-bleed interior photograph begins at 42vh. On 390px the wordmark still runs one line edge to edge and the descriptors merge into one three-line serif caps statement.
directions.grammar: Grid: full-bleed with 8px outer margins, no column grid visible; text blocks pin to the extreme left and right margins, centre is reserved for the script. Type: three voices with violent contrast: ultra-black grotesque (weight 900, expanded) only for the wordmark; copperplate script only for one connector word and one section-wide phrase; a sharp text serif in caps at 28-32px for all statements; nav in 16px neo-grotesque with tight tracking. Display to nav ratio about 9:1. Spacing: sections are tall single ideas, 55-70vh each, with one centred serif caps line and a lot of empty field. Colour: two-colour world (blush and oxblood) that inverts per section, plus one shocking accent (hot pink) used once at giant scale. Imagery: one large interior per section, square crop edges, no rounded corners. Chrome: tiny geometric monogram, five nav words, one contact chip with an arrow square; nav becomes a blush chip when over dark. Absent: gold, gradients, shadows, cards, icons, body copy longer than two lines.
directions.typeStack: Observed: canora (ultra-heavy grotesque), a custom or licensed copperplate script, Noe Text, Neue Haas Grotesk. Free stand-ins: Archivo at wdth 125 wght 900 (Google variable) or Unbounded 900 for the wordmark; Pinyon Script or Imperial Script (Google) for the script; Newsreader 500 or Sentient (Fontshare) in caps for the serif; Switzer (Fontshare) or Inter Tight for nav.
directions.motion: Entrance: wordmark letters rise from a baseline clip in two groups (0.7s, 40ms stagger), then the script connector draws itself as an SVG stroke left to right (1.1s) and settles; photo wipes up from the bottom edge. Scroll: the photo scales from inset to full bleed; on entering the dark section the giant script phrase translates horizontally with scroll (about 0.6x speed) so it is always cropped by both edges; colour inversion happens as a hard cut at the section edge, not a fade. Micro: nav words dim siblings to 50 percent, the contact arrow square nudges 3px, project images crossfade to a second view on hover. Signature moment: the hot-pink script sliding across oxblood. Reduced motion: script rendered static and centred, no horizontal travel.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Salon Fauve, an interiors, objects and atmospheres studio. IA natural to a design atelier: wordmark and descriptor couplet; one hero interior; manifesto on dark with the script phrase; Spaces index as a plain list (place, typology, year) with one image each; Objects (editions with dimensions and material); Dear Fauve (letters or journal); press room as a text list of mastheads; commission enquiry with three questions.
directions.whyWorldClass: It proves that playful can read expensive when the craft is typographic: extreme weight contrast, a script used as a structural stroke rather than decoration, and a two-colour system with one accent used exactly once. Nothing on the page is a component; it is all composition.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: variable-font-pressure and poster-crop (type-led heroes), silent-luxury-restraint (luxury register). Differs by the heavy-grotesque-versus-hairline-script splice and the script colour flood on an inverted field; the library has no copperplate-script-at-architectural-scale template and its luxury entries are quiet rather than exuberant.
directions.buildRisk: The free heavy grotesque must be genuinely black and wide or the splice loses its contrast; set Archivo at max width and weight and tighten tracking to -0.02em. Script hairlines alias below about 90px and Pinyon is lower contrast than the original, so draw the connector as an inline SVG path with a 1.5px stroke if the font looks soft. Needs one strong interior photo (the factory has exactly one); without a second image keep later sections typographic.

directions.name: Expedition ledger: visible column rules, cropped place name, bracketed coordinates
directions.signature: At scroll=0 a full-bleed remote landscape; a single place name in condensed gothic caps, 17.8vw tall, stands on the bottom edge spanning the content width; seven hairline column rules (white at 18 percent) run top to bottom through image and type and continue unbroken into the next section; nav is a row of small frosted rectangles; a two-line italic serif caption sits alone at left centre. On 390px the place name runs vertically up the left column rule or breaks into two stacked lines, rules reduce to three.
directions.grammar: Grid: a real 6-column grid whose rules are part of the design (x about 60, 248, 484, 720, 956, 1192, 1380 at 1440); every block starts on a rule and statements deliberately start on rule 3 or 4, leaving the left third empty. Type: condensed gothic caps for one word only; light classical serif caps at 40-46px with leading 0.95 for statements; italic old-style serif at 16-18px for captions; grotesque 15px for UI; bracketed coordinates in condensed caps at 13px. Ratio place name to statement about 6:1. Spacing: 60-70vh of pure white between hero and first statement. Colour: white, slate rgb 31,42,68, ice blues from imagery, one signal orange side tab. Imagery: aerial and wide landscape, cards floating on texture. Chrome: frosted rectangles with 2-4px radius, one vertical side tab. Absent: icons, cards with shadows, serif italics in headlines, dark overlays on video.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Oswald (place name), Cardinal Classic Long (serif caps statements), Inter Tight (UI), an italic old-style serif for captions. Free stand-ins: Oswald and Inter Tight are the actual Google fonts; Cormorant Garamond 400 caps or Boska (Fontshare) for the statements; Cormorant Garamond Italic or EB Garamond Italic for captions.
directions.motion: Entrance: column rules draw downward staggered left to right (60ms apart, 1s each), then the place name rises from below the fold line as if surfacing, caption fades last. Scroll: the image fades to white while the rules persist (the rules are the continuity); statements reveal word by word from 12 percent grey to full slate tied to scroll position; a pen loop SVG draws around the italic label when it enters; camp cards translate horizontally in a pinned band over a slowly panning texture. Micro: chips brighten their frost on hover, coordinates tick digits when a card becomes active. Signature moment: the place name staying cropped at the fold while the landscape drifts behind the rules. Reduced motion: rules static, text fully inked.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Ultima Camp, private expeditions to a polar interior. IA natural to expedition travel: place-name hero; the last continent statement; three camps as coordinate-stamped cards; the itinerary as a day ledger (Day 1 to Day 8 with aircraft, altitude, temperature); the operation (runway, fleet, guides, medical) as numbered facts on the rules; season calendar and rates table; how it works side tab; enquiry.
directions.photoBrief: Six to eight frames, all remote cold or high landscape: one aerial hero with a strong vertical rock or ice feature and clear sky in the top third (leave the bottom third calm for the place name); one cracked-ice or snow texture, top-down, for the card band; three camp or shelter exteriors at blue hour with warm window light; one aircraft or sled on ice, small in frame; one human-scale figure walking away. Light: low polar sun, pale blue shadows, no HDR. Crop 16:9 for hero and texture, 4:3 for cards. Treatment: untouched colour, slight desaturation toward slate, no vignette, no dark overlay.
directions.whyWorldClass: It makes the grid itself the luxury signal: the rules read as cartographic meridians, so layout, data voice and subject agree. The single enormous word cropped at the fold is confident in the way hotel sites rarely are, and the long white pause before the first statement is the stillness move executed with nerve.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: luxury-resort-cinematic-stillness (hospitality) and svgmap-journey or observatory-log (data voice). Differs by the persistent visible column rules as a through-line across image and white sections, the fold-cropped condensed place name, and the day-ledger IA; the resort template is a calm cinematic sequence without a structural grid or data voice.
directions.buildRisk: Entirely dependent on landscape imagery of real quality; with AI loops or a weak still it becomes a travel template. Source a free-licence polar or alpine pack first and use a still (not autoplay video) for the thumbnail frame. Keep the rules on integer pixels so they do not blur at DPR 1, and make sure the place name is fully legible at scroll=0 (crop at most the bottom 4 percent).

directions.name: Macro fume dial: the dial is the viewport, hands longer than the screen, hairline type
directions.signature: At scroll=0 a procedurally drawn fume dial is cropped so hard that the viewport sits inside it: the centre pinion is at about 50 percent x, 45 percent y, the minute hand runs off the top right corner, only five or six applied indices are in frame, and the lacquer falls from a saturated core (oxblood, petrol or moss) to black at the edges with a fine sunburst grain. The hands show the visitor's real local time and the seconds hand sweeps. Bottom left: a two-line headline in weight 100-200 sans at 60px, a two-line light paragraph, and two bold 11px caps links with short underline stubs. On 390px the crop moves so pinion sits upper right and the hands cross the screen diagonally.
directions.grammar: Grid: 40px margins, text block pinned bottom left with a max width of 520px; nav is four small bold caps words left, script or engraved logo centre, three line icons right. Type: one sans family at extreme lightness for display (weight 100-200, 56-60px, leading 1.0), 18-20px light for body, 11px bold caps tracked 0.08em for links; optionally one italic serif caps line inside the headline. Display to link ratio about 5.5:1 with the weight contrast doing the work. Spacing: full-viewport macro sections alternate with pure black bands holding a single ruled spec table. Colour: black, white, and exactly one dial colour per section; later sections may each take a different saturated studio colour. Imagery: macro only, never a whole watch until the specification section. Chrome: hairlines, no boxes except one ruled label. Absent: gold, crests in the hero, feature icons, carousels with dots, whole-product hero shots.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Inter Variable at weight 150 (H. Moser), Helvetica Neue Web weight 100 with Times Now italic (Audemars Piguet), ITC Blair with Aventa (De Bethune), Exat Wide Light with Work Sans Light (Urwerk), Prelo with Sohne (Vacheron Constantin). Free stand-ins: Inter 100-200 (Google) is literally the Moser face; Instrument Serif Italic or Newsreader Italic for the italic caps line; Syncopate or Archivo wdth 125 wght 200 for the wide gothic variant.
directions.motion: Entrance: black, then the dial exposes like a slow aperture (radial reveal from the pinion, 1.4s), hands settle to the real time with one damped correction, a specular sweep crosses the lacquer once; text fades up last. Scroll: the camera pulls back on scrub so the macro becomes the whole watch by the specification section (scale 4.5 to 1 with slight rotation); sunburst highlight rotates with scroll so the lacquer appears to catch light; paragraph lines ink in one by one. Micro: seconds hand sweeps continuously (not ticking), indices glint when the pointer passes, link stubs extend to full width. Signature moment: realising the hands tell your own time. Reduced motion: hands set once, no sweep, no pull-back (static crop then a static full view).
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Maison Arcelin, an independent manufacture making 28 watches a year. IA natural to haute horology: macro dial with live time; the reference (case, diameter, thickness, calibre, reserve) as a hairline two-column table; dial making in three chapters (lacquer, sunburst, hand-bevelled hands); calibre view with numbered components; the year's allocation ledger (serial, metal, status); atelier visit and waiting list.
directions.whyWorldClass: The macro crop is how the best independent and big-house horology sites assert confidence in finishing: no logo, no whole product, just lacquer and steel at a scale where flaws would show. Paired with type at weight 100-150 it is the most technically restrained dark luxury on the web right now.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: luxury-watch-callouts, celestial-complication, silvered-complication, terminator-clock. Differs by never showing the whole watch at rest (extreme inside-the-dial crop), by the fume lacquer as the colour system, by live local time on oversized hands, and by the hairline-weight type; the existing watch templates present a complete dial or watch with annotations.
directions.buildRisk: A procedural dial can look like clip art. Dodge with layered construction: repeating-conic sunburst at 0.3 degree steps under a radial fume gradient, SVG noise grain, hands as bevelled polygons with two-tone faces and a soft offset shadow, applied indices with a top highlight and contact shadow, and a moving specular band. Keep the crop extreme (fewer elements means fewer tells). Canvas 2D or SVG is enough; avoid WebGL so capture stays deterministic.

directions.name: Engraver's wide gothic monograph: stationery capitals, white field, one sculptural jewel
directions.signature: At scroll=0 a white page with two hairline nav rows; a monograph title in thin wide gothic capitals (60px, tracking 0.06em) and a subtitle one third its size, ranged left; one sentence of 15px text; then, already in view from 47vh down, a wide inset plate (64px margins) in which a single high-jewellery piece is drawn as a continuous line of pave stones describing an open curve across a pale stone surface under a hard spotlight, casting one soft shadow. On 390px the plate becomes a 4:5 portrait and the title wraps to three lines at 34px.
directions.grammar: Grid: 64px margins, 12 columns, text ranged left in columns 1-7; image plates span all 12 or sit as 5-column portraits against 6-column text with a tall empty gap between. Type: thin wide gothic caps for every title (60 / 22 / 14px steps, all same face), neutral grotesque 15px for text with 1.65 leading, underlined text links, no buttons. Title to body ratio 4:1 but equal visual weight because the caps are so light. Spacing: 280-320px of white between plates; text blocks are short (one heading, one sentence, one link) and bottom-aligned to their image. Colour: white, black, one deep green bar; all colour comes from stones. Imagery: one object per plate, hard spot lighting, marble or paper ground. Chrome: text-plus-icon utilities, ruled rows. Absent: serif display type, gold, gradients, product grids on the home, overlay text on images.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Sackers Gothic Std Light with Moderat (Boucheron), Novecento Wide with Cormorant (Buccellati), ITC Blair (De Bethune), Termina (Akrivia), Janson Text with Maison Neue (Van Cleef and Arpels). Free stand-ins: Julius Sans One (Google) is the closest thin wide engraver's gothic; Syncopate 400 as the heavier alternative; DM Sans or General Sans (Fontshare) for text; EB Garamond for an optional notice line.
directions.motion: Entrance: title letters fade in with tracking easing from 0.14em to 0.06em (1s), rules draw from left, the plate lights up as if a spot is switched on (radial brightness from the jewel outward, 1.2s). Scroll: stones along the path glint in sequence as the plate crosses the viewport (a travelling highlight tied to scroll); on a pinned moment the finished jewel crossfades to its gouache drawing on grey paper (painted dots and pencil construction lines), then back; text blocks rise 16px and fade. Micro: underlines redraw left to right, the pointer acts as a second small light on the plate (highlight follows within 40px). Signature moment: jewel to gouache and back. Reduced motion: static plate, gouache shown as a second plate below.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Maison Oriel, high jewellers. IA natural to a high-jewellery collection: monograph title and exhibition notice; the suite's hero piece; the three chapters of the collection, each one plate and one sentence; the gouache; the stones ledger (stone, carat, origin, cut) as a ruled table; hours of work and number of artisans as two numerals; salons by city; private appointment.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is the visual language of engraved stationery and museum monographs applied to a web page: one typeface, one weight, enormous white intervals and a single object treated as sculpture. It is the opposite of the sparkle-on-black jewellery cliche and it is what the Place Vendome houses actually publish.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: jeweled-vitrine, monogram-card, auction-lot, museum-collection-explorer. Differs by the engraver's wide gothic as the only voice, the white monograph layout with left-ranged titles and tall intervals, and the pave-line jewel drawn procedurally with a gouache alternate; jeweled-vitrine is a dark display-case register.
directions.buildRisk: A procedural jewel and marble can look cheap. Dodge by committing to the gouache idiom even for the finished state: each stone an SVG symbol with four facet polygons and a white table highlight, sized along a bezier with slight graduation, on a paper or very subtle veined ground built from two blurred turbulence layers; one large soft shadow sells the object. Julius Sans One has a single weight, so hierarchy must come from size only (which matches the source).

directions.name: One-size catalogue: a single 13px voice, one tall photograph, bare captions
directions.signature: At scroll=0 one line of 13px grotesque across the top (nav words left at a 20px margin, a thin wide-tracked caps wordmark centred, utilities right) laid directly over a single full-bleed photograph that is three viewports tall: the subject occupies the right 45 percent, the left 55 percent is soft empty wall. There is no headline, no button and no overlay; the nav is the only typography on screen. On 390px the same single line collapses to a two-bar icon, the wordmark and a count, and the tall plate continues.
directions.grammar: Grid: 20-24px outer margins; plates either full-bleed, centred at 68 percent width, or two-up with a 24px gutter; captions hang 12px below the plate's left edge. Type: exactly one size (12-13px) and one weight for everything including prices and footer; the wordmark is the only variation (same size range, light, tracking 0.35em). Hierarchy is produced by position and white space alone. Spacing: 36px between plate and next plate row; text never sits on an image except the nav. Colour: white or warm off-white, near-black text, no accent. Imagery: full-length looks shot in daylight interiors, or monochrome hard-shadow still lifes; grain visible. Chrome: none beyond the line of words; brackets around counts, Bag (0). Absent: display type, buttons, icons, borders, hover cards, colour, any marketing sentence.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Basic Commercial (The Row), Univers LT Pro 55 (Sophie Buhai), Brown Std with Garamond Premier (Lemaire), Jil-Futura (Jil Sander), Fakt Pro with ITC Galliard (Khaite). Free stand-ins: Switzer (Fontshare) or Hanken Grotesk 400 (Google) at 13px for the Akzidenz or Univers voice; Jost 300 tracked 0.35em for the light caps wordmark; Jost 500 caps for a Futura variant.
directions.motion: Entrance: nothing moves except the plate fading from white (0.6s) and the nav appearing 200ms later; the restraint is the entrance. Scroll: native scroll down the tall plate with the nav fixed; when the plate ends, the wordmark fades out and returns in black over white; plates below fade in without translation. Micro: nav words switch to 45 percent opacity siblings on hover; two-up plates swap to an alternate frame with a 300ms crossfade; captions underline. Signature moment: discovering that the page is a single photograph you walk down. Reduced motion: identical, crossfades become instant.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Orme, a ready-to-wear and objects label with no logo beyond its name. IA natural to quiet fashion: tall look plate; two-up category plates with bare one-word captions; Galerie (objects and furniture) as a centred plate; Collections as a plain text index (season, year, number of looks); Special Projects list; stores as address lines; footer in the same 13px voice.
directions.photoBrief: Seven to nine frames. One very tall portrait-orientation look (aspect about 1:1.9, so it survives a three-viewport crop) of a single figure in daylight interior, subject in the right half, pale blurred wall on the left, visible film grain, no eye-contact drama. Four still lifes of objects (bracelet stack, bag, shoe, vessel) on plain paper with one hard raking light and long shadows, black and white, slight grain. Two details (hand holding a book or bag, fabric at the waist). Treatment: untouched skin and fabric, no retouched gloss, neutral colour or true monochrome, never both in one row.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is the hardest thing to do on the web: remove every device that signals design and still be unmistakable. The houses with the highest price points per item use the smallest type on the internet, and the single tall plate turns scrolling into looking at clothes from collar to hem.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: silent-luxury-restraint and mono-ink-restraint. Differs by having no display typography at all (one 13px size for the entire page), by the single three-viewport photograph as the whole hero, and by plate-and-bare-caption rhythm; the existing restraint templates still use a large serif headline and whitespace as the statement.
directions.buildRisk: With nothing but 13px text the template is only as good as its photographs; a stock-looking image makes it read as an empty page. Do not build until the tall look frame is sourced. The thumbnail will look sparse by design, so the photograph must carry it; make sure the nav line and wordmark are crisp at DPR 1 (use 13px, weight 400, no letter-spacing on nav).

directions.name: Folk-stitch two-tone: embroidered wordmark, bar-rendered landscape, ruled marquee

exemplars.site: Son Daven (The First The Last) - Awwwards Site of the Month Jun 2026

directions.signature: At scroll=0 a two-colour composition, tan paper and near-black brown only: the upper 55 percent is a mountain ridge rendered as about 220 vertical stitch bars of varying height and thickness (dense at the base, thinning to single threads at the crest); across the ridge line sits the wordmark in wide capitals whose outlines are stepped like cross-stitch; below, a marquee band between two double hairlines carries a flare-serif caps phrase separated by four-point stars; bottom left a three-line flare-serif caps descriptor, bottom right an outline circle CTA. On 390px the ridge keeps about 90 bars and the wordmark stacks to two lines.
directions.grammar: Grid: 16px margins, full-width bands stacked like a woven strip; double hairline rules (two 1px lines 4px apart) separate every band. Type: a flare or glyphic serif in caps, tight tracking, for headlines and numerals (48-64px); a wide techno sans in caps at 11-13px for all labels; no lowercase anywhere. Headline to label ratio 5:1. Spacing: bands of 30-45vh; data pairs (label above value) stacked in a right-hand column. Colour: exactly two, used as figure and ground and inverted per band; photography appears only inside the hero and is toned warm so it does not break the pair. Imagery: architecture render or photo once, everything else is bar-rendered pattern. Chrome: outline circle CTAs, bracketed [X] close, small bar-code progress mark bottom left. Absent: gradients, a third colour, lowercase, rounded cards, icons.
directions.typeStack: Observed: KTF Metro Roman (flare serif caps) and KTF Metro Blueline (wide techno sans). Free stand-ins: Marcellus or Forum (Google) in caps with tracking -0.04em for the flare serif, or Boska (Fontshare) for more weight; Michroma (Google) for the wide techno sans labels.
directions.motion: Entrance: bars grow upward from the baseline with random 0-600ms delays until the ridge resolves (1.4s), the wordmark assembles from stitch columns left to right, the marquee starts at 40px per second. Scroll: ridge bars shear slightly with scroll velocity and settle; bands invert colour with a horizontal stitch-wipe (columns flip in sequence); numerals count up in steps that match the stitch grid; a second pattern (a peak, a tree) weaves itself in a pinned band. Micro: circle CTA fills with bars on hover, labels flicker one stitch. Signature moment: the mountain weaving itself from threads. Reduced motion: bars drawn at final height, marquee paused, hard colour cuts.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Varda, a mountain design hotel and residences rooted in a regional weaving tradition, selling both stays and investment units. IA natural to that genre: stitched gate; aerial hero with location chips and construction dates; the concept (culture meets architecture) in one band; the woven landscape divider; rooms and residences as ruled rows; indicators band (yield, instalment plan, handover quarter) with marquee title; construction timeline; consultation CTA.
directions.whyWorldClass: It finds luxury in local craft translated into a rendering rule: one stitch logic draws the wordmark, the landscape and the transitions, in two colours. It is heritage without nostalgia styling, and it is why the site took Site of the Month over heavier 3D work.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: mudmee-loom-resolve and generative-woven-textile-hero (same woven mechanic family), slit-scan-temporal, benjarong-atelier. Differs by the strict two-colour tan and brown register, the flare-serif plus techno-sans pairing, the stitched wordmark and the hospitality-investment IA with ruled marquee bands. The mechanic overlap is real: build only if the result is clearly bar-rendered landscape plus ledger, not another loom hero.
directions.buildRisk: Overlap with the two existing woven templates is the main risk; differentiate through landscape subject, two-tone discipline and the data bands. Thin vertical bars moire and blur at DPR 1: snap bar x and width to integer pixels and render on canvas 2D at device resolution. The stepped wordmark needs a real construction (rasterise the text to a coarse grid and redraw as columns), not a filter.

directions.name: Maison letterhead: linen page, hand-inked wordmark, courier small caps, rotated seal

exemplars.site: Les Grands Chenes (Studio Krabb) - Siteinspire 29 Sep 2026

directions.signature: At scroll=0 the top 32 percent of the viewport is a sheet of letterhead on linen: a centred row of three typewriter small-caps links over a full-width hairline, a two-line wordmark in imperfect hand-inked capitals centred beneath it, a two-line typewriter descriptor at the far left, and at the far right a solid circular seal (120px, tobacco brown) carrying one italic serif word rotated -18 degrees. Below the sheet one full-bleed photograph of the house begins, and the first line of a 40px Garamond sentence overlaps its bottom edge. On 390px the seal drops to a fixed bottom-right position at 84px and the wordmark keeps two lines.
directions.grammar: Grid: 40px margins; text lives in a narrow left column (about 400px, columns 1-4 of 12) while images sit as an offset pair in columns 6-12 at different heights; one small figure drawing floats alone in the gap. Type: old-style serif for all reading text at generous sizes (24px body, 40px headings, leading 1.25), typewriter mono caps at 11px for labels, descriptors and figure captions, hand-inked caps for the wordmark only. Body is unusually large relative to headings (ratio 1.6:1), which reads as a letter rather than a web page. Spacing: slow, 160-200px between blocks, images never aligned to each other. Colour: linen, soft black, one tobacco brown for seal and text links. Imagery: natural-light architecture and woodland, plus ink line drawings as numbered figures. Chrome: the seal is the only button; links are sentences ending in a long arrow. Absent: sans-serif, cards, icons, sliders, overlays, any second accent.
directions.typeStack: Observed: EB Garamond (via Adobe, the same design as the Google release), a Courier-like mono for labels, a custom hand-inked sans wordmark; Aman uses Lyon Display and Lyon Text with Whitney; Vacheron uses Prelo with Sohne. Free stand-ins: EB Garamond (Google) is literal; Courier Prime (Google) for the mono caps; for the wordmark set Jost or Barlow 500 caps and roughen with an SVG feTurbulence plus feDisplacementMap filter (scale 2-3) and a slight blur-threshold ink spread; Newsreader or Sentient (Fontshare) if a Lyon-like text face is preferred.
directions.motion: Entrance: the header rule draws from centre outward, the wordmark appears as if blotted (opacity with a brief blur 3px to 0), the seal stamps in (scale 1.12 to 1 with rotation -26 to -18 degrees, 0.5s, one small settle). Scroll: the seal stays fixed top right and rotates a few degrees with scroll; photographs reveal by a slow vertical unmask at different speeds so the offset pair never moves in sync; figure drawings stroke themselves in when they enter; paragraphs fade without movement. Micro: the seal turns to face horizontal on hover, sentence links extend their arrow, FR / EN crossfades the copy. Signature moment: the seal stamp. Reduced motion: seal static at -18 degrees, drawings pre-drawn.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: Maison des Sources, a five-room family guesthouse on a wooded plateau. IA natural to a maison d'hote: letterhead; the house in one sentence over its photograph; La Maison (text plus offset image pair); the five rooms as named entries (exposure, bed, bath, from-price) in serif with mono labels; figures (FIG.1 bark, FIG.2 floor plan, FIG.3 the spring); the table (breakfast, dinner on request); the surroundings with distances in kilometres; practical notes (season, access by train); the seal as the only call to action.
directions.photoBrief: Five to six frames in soft natural light: one wide exterior of a low timber or stone house seen through trees (16:9, calm lower third); two portrait-orientation frames for the offset pair (a stone wall corner in dappled light, tall woodland); one interior detail (bench, linen, wood) in warm side light; one local heritage object or landscape. Treatment: analogue feel, greens kept natural, no HDR, no people facing camera. Plus three ink line drawings (bark, plan, spring) which can be authored as SVG paths.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is hospitality stillness done with stationery craft instead of cinema: the page behaves like a letter from the owner, with a seal for a button and numbered figures for curiosities. The enormous reading size and the refusal of any sans-serif UI make it feel hosted rather than marketed.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: luxury-resort-cinematic-stillness, monogram-card, field-notes, sealed-invitation. Differs by the letterhead header as the scroll=0 signature, the rotated seal as sole CTA, large-serif letter typography with typewriter labels, and FIG. line drawings; the resort template is video-led stillness with conventional chrome.
directions.buildRisk: The hand-inked wordmark is the make-or-break detail: a clean font reads as a template, an over-distorted one reads as a horror title. Use low displacement and test at 390px. Needs three or four natural-light photos of one place; mixing unrelated stock breaks the letter illusion, so pick a single stock series. Keep the header to about a third of the viewport so the photograph is visible in the thumbnail.

directions.name: System-serif defiance: default Times, one pure primary, zero gutters, no persuasion

exemplars.site: Miu Miu - A House that we shaped (Merci Michel) - Awwwards SOTD 25 Aug 2026

directions.signature: At scroll=0 a full-bleed pale field (a cool grey studio backdrop or portrait) with a two-line wordmark in bold system Times capitals, pure #FF0000, 10.4vw tall, centred and overprinting whatever is beneath; two 12px Times caps words top left; one 16px white Times caps line centred at the bottom edge; nothing else. Scrolling arrives at flush two-up plates with no gutters or margins and centred white caps labels. On 390px the wordmark stays two lines at 19vw and the plates stack edge to edge.
directions.grammar: Grid: none visible; full-bleed and half-bleed blocks butt against each other with 0px gaps and 0px page margins; type is centred on its block or parked 24px from a corner. Type: one face, the system serif, in three states: bold caps giant (wordmark), regular caps 12-16px (everything else), no lowercase headlines, default letter-spacing. Ratio wordmark to label about 10:1 with nothing in between. Colour: black, white, and a single pure primary used once (red #FF0000, or a flat cobalt field for a campaign card). Imagery: blunt, unretouched, cropped mid-body; plates are allowed to be awkward. Chrome: a black rectangle with a native select and a white button; no icons. Archive section: a plain file-list table (name, modified, size) as the collections index. Absent: brand typeface, tracking, animation flourishes, margins, rounded corners, any copywriting.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Times New Roman served as the system default (no font files) at Phoebe Philo; Work Sans bold at Miu Miu; Atlas Grotesk and Sharp Grotesk in the Dropbox chrome of Margiela folders. Free stand-ins: use the system stack literally (font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif) with Tinos (Google) as the metric-compatible fallback so capture is deterministic; Work Sans 700 (Google) for the campaign card variant.
directions.motion: Entrance: none by design; the page is simply there (a 150ms opacity at most). Scroll: plain document scroll; plates do not parallax; the red wordmark is position sticky for the first viewport and is cut off hard by the first plate row. In the campaign-card variant the justified words slide apart from the centre to the edges of the measure (0.8s) and the last word tracks out letter by letter. Micro: labels invert to red on hover, plates swap to an alternate frame instantly (no fade), file-list rows highlight like an OS list. Signature moment: the absence of any animation next to a wordmark that loud. Reduced motion: identical.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: HOLLIS WARD, a womenswear label that sells by timed edits. IA natural to conceptual fashion: wordmark over the season image; LATEST ARRIVALS flush plates by category with centred labels; the edit as a numbered list of pieces with fabric and price in plain serif; the archive as a file list (A1_Coats, A2_Trousers, with dates); shipping region box; stores and contact as plain lines.
directions.whyWorldClass: Refusing a brand typeface and shipping the browser default in pure red is the most confident typographic act in luxury fashion right now; it reads as conceptual precisely because every other house spends six figures on a custom face. Zero gutters and zero copy complete the statement, and Margiela publishing a raw folder as its archive shows the attitude is a 2026 current, not a one-off.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: swiss-poster, mono-ink-restraint, soft-brutalism, manpage or commit-log (default-tooling registers). Differs by being a fashion house in system Times with a single pure primary overprint, zero-gutter plates and a file-list archive; it is neither Swiss grid nor developer nostalgia, and the library has no template whose point is the undesigned default.
directions.buildRisk: It can read as unfinished rather than defiant. The dodge is absolute consistency: one face, no tracking, exact 0px gaps, a perfectly centred wordmark, and at least two strong plates (flat colour fields with a single blunt object silhouette work if photographs are unavailable; the factory portrait-free asset set means the hero may be a pale studio field, which still carries the red). System Times renders differently per OS, so ship Tinos as the first family for stable capture.

directions.name: Grain abstraction: 16mm optical forms, stencil wordmark, docked product chip
directions.signature: At scroll=0 the whole viewport is a procedural 16mm film frame: two very large near-black discs (each about 60vw across, cropped by the left and right edges) with soft lens-edge falloff sit on a deep oxblood field, a thin vertical highlight glints inside one disc, and coarse animated grain plus slight gate weave covers everything. A white stencil-cut wordmark sits top centre; bottom right a docked product chip (white packshot tile with a drawn bottle, and a translucent grey panel with category, name, price and size in small tracked caps); a five-segment vertical pager at the right edge. On 390px one disc dominates and the chip spans the bottom width.
directions.grammar: Grid: 28px margins; three fixed anchors only (wordmark top centre, menu and cart in the top corners, chip bottom right); the field is otherwise empty. Type: stencil grotesque caps for the wordmark and chapter titles (56-72px, tracking 0.04em); a neutral sans in caps at 12-16px tracked 0.02em for chip and UI; one italic old-style serif line per chapter as the poetic caption. Ratio title to UI about 5:1. Spacing: each chapter is one full viewport with one abstraction; below the film, an off-white reading section sets body copy in a warm brown instead of black. Colour: per-scent duotone (oxblood and black; moss and umber; milk and slate), text white on film, brown on paper. Imagery: abstract optical forms standing for raw materials; the product appears only as a small packshot inside the chip. Chrome: translucent grey panels, no borders, a mute glyph and pause glyph bottom left. Absent: bottle hero shots, ingredient icon rows, gold caps, gradient-mesh blobs.
directions.typeStack: Observed: byredoSans (custom) with a stencil wordmark at Byredo; Lutz Headline with Eidetic and GT Standard at Perfumer H; Andale Mono with a custom wide caps face at Ormaie; Bell Gothic at Le Labo. Free stand-ins: Allerta Stencil or Saira Stencil One (Google) for the stencil caps; Hanken Grotesk or Figtree (Google) for UI caps; Newsreader Italic or Fraunces Italic (Google) for the caption line; Courier Prime if a lab-label variant is wanted.
directions.motion: Entrance: the frame starts overexposed and settles to exposure over 0.9s (like a projector lamp), grain is live from the first frame, discs drift apart by 3 percent, the chip slides up 24px and fades. Scroll: each chapter crossfades the duotone and morphs the optical forms (discs to a meniscus line to a single vertical slit) on scrub, with a 2-frame flash at each cut like a film splice; the chip content swaps per chapter (name and size tick over); the reading section rises as a paper sheet over the film. Micro: pause and mute glyphs, the pager segments fill, the chip packshot tilts 3 degrees on hover. Signature moment: the splice flash between two scent colours. Reduced motion: grain frozen, forms static per chapter, hard cuts without flash.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: OBLIQUE, a perfume house releasing extracts as numbered films. IA natural to niche fragrance: abstract film hero with the current extract in the chip; the composition as three colour fields (opening, heart, base) with one italic line each; the perfumer's note in brown text on paper; formats ledger (extract 70 ml, travel 15 ml, refill) with prices; the discovery set; boutiques by city; newsletter as a single underlined line.
directions.whyWorldClass: It sells a scent the only honest way a screen can: by abstraction and atmosphere, with the commerce reduced to one small docked chip. Grain, defocus and duotone are doing the work that bottle renders do on lesser sites, and the product is treated as a caption to a film.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: beauty-skincare-ritual-editorial (vertical), feturbulence-organic-hero and reaction-diffusion-canvas (procedural fields), liquid-ink-title. Differs by hard optical forms on a duotone under real film artefacts (grain, gate weave, splice flash) rather than organic noise, the stencil wordmark, and the docked product chip as the entire commerce surface.
directions.buildRisk: It can slide into the generic blurred-gradient-blob look. Dodge with hard geometry (true circles with lens falloff, a crisp meniscus line, one specular slit), coarse monochromatic grain rendered on a half-resolution canvas and scaled up, and sub-pixel gate weave; never use more than two colours per chapter. The chip needs a decent drawn bottle (simple SVG: rectangular flask, domed cap, label block). Animated grain is fine for capture but cap it at about 24 fps to keep measured FPS healthy.

directions.name: Opus-numbered plan index

exemplars.site: OFFICE Kersten Geers David Van Severen - projects index
OFFICE Kersten Geers David Van Severen - home

directions.signature: At scroll 0 the viewport is a black-ruled 4x2 grid (2 columns on phone) of square cells directly under a 60px header: each cell shows a large centred opus number, an inline-SVG architectural plan (thick black poche walls, hairline grey furniture, dotted site lines) and a one-line caption 'NAME - City'. A fixed bottom-centre text toggle 'Drawings / Images' crossfades every cell from plan to a flat tonal elevation or photo.
directions.grammar: Grid: 4 equal columns edge to edge, no outer margin, 1px #000 rules as the only structure, cells are exact squares (360px at 1440). Type: one neo-grotesque at 14.4px/1.3 for everything; the opus number is the only larger size (about 30px, regular weight, lining figures), so the ratio display:body is only 2:1. Captions centred, name in caps, city in sentence case after a spaced hyphen. Colour: pure white, pure black, drawings in black with 20 to 40 percent grey hairlines; zero accent. Imagery: drawings first, photographs secondary and only on demand; home variant is a 50/50 photo|plan diptych. Chrome: two-bar menu glyph left, office name centred with the first word underlined, FILTER right. Absent: thumbnails with rounded corners, hover cards, project descriptions, years, any colour.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Folio (KGDVS), Geometric mono + Gravity bold (H&dM), Aktiv Grotesk 500 (Kerez). Free stand-ins: Familjen Grotesk or Schibsted Grotesk (Google) for Folio's slightly awkward warmth; Hanken Grotesk as fallback; DM Mono or Geist Mono for filter labels.
directions.motion: Entrance: rules draw in from top-left over about 500ms (scaleX / scaleY on the borders), then numbers and plans appear cell by cell in reading order with a 30ms stagger, opacity only. Scroll: native; header stays fixed and overprints. Micro: hovering a cell inverts it (black cell, white drawing via CSS filter invert) and reveals year + status under the caption. Signature moment: the Drawings/Images toggle, which crossfades all cells at once (250ms) so the whole wall flips from line-drawing to image; FILTER collapses non-matching cells to empty ruled squares rather than removing them, so the grid never reflows.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'BUREAU Halden Arntz Verhoeven', an architecture office in Ghent with 400+ numbered works. IA natural to the genre: header (menu / office name / filter) -> index grid of numbered works with plans -> same works as a five-column text list (No., title, place, year, status) -> a 120-word office statement set in the same 14px -> competitions and publications list -> address block. No hero, no services.
directions.whyWorldClass: It turns the oeuvre itself into the interface: the numbering system, the plan drawing and the rule grid are the brand. Nothing is styled, everything is specified, and it communicates an intellectual position (drawing over image) in the first frame.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: blueprint-svg, isometric-atelier-plan, trace-diagram, museum-collection-explorer. Those style drawings as 'blueprint' decoration (blue, technical kitsch) or build one illustrative scene; this is a neutral black-on-white catalogue of many real-looking orthographic plans in ruled square cells with an opus-number system and a global drawing/image flip.
directions.buildRisk: The plans must look like real architecture, not icons: 8 to 12 distinct SVG plans with believable structure (column grids, thick walls with openings, stairs, a circular or blob outline, a courtyard) and three line weights. Weak, symmetric or clip-art plans will sink it. Dodge: author plans from a small set of parametric generators (grid of columns + wall segments + stair hatch) and hand-tune each; keep stroke widths in non-scaling-stroke so they stay crisp at 390px.

directions.name: Cropped wordmark over a sortable project ledger
directions.signature: A single word set so large (cap height about 85vh) that only its first two or three letters fit the viewport, flush to a 16px left margin, black on white; one tiny grey caps label top-centre; a row of small sort arrows at the bottom edge sitting exactly on the x positions of the table columns to come. Scrolling scrubs the word smaller so more letters enter while a bold eight-column sortable ledger rises under a double rule.
directions.grammar: Grid: 16px outer margins; the table uses 8 unequal columns (No 7 percent, Title 19, Place 15, Client 12, Year 12, Area 12, Status 12, Category 11) and the hero arrows pre-announce that grid. Type: one tight neo-grotesque in a single heavy weight (650); display about 800px with leading 1 and natural tracking, body 16px/26px; ratio 50:1 with nothing in between. Rows are #A0A0A0 and become black on hover; headers black with a small arrow, active sort arrow black, others grey. Two 2px black rules frame the header row. Colour: white, black, one grey. Imagery: none on the home view. Chrome: no logo other than the wordmark, tabs are two words. Absent: images, cards, descriptions, buttons, footer design.
directions.typeStack: Observed: TWK Lausanne 650 (Etablissement); Inter 500 (Benji Taylor). Free stand-ins: Switzer 600/700 (Fontshare) is the closest to Lausanne's proportions; Inter Tight 650 or Hanken Grotesk 700 as alternates. Tabular lining figures on (font-feature-settings 'tnum').
directions.motion: Entrance: the wordmark is simply there; the eight arrows tick in left to right (40ms stagger). Scroll: the word's font-size is bound to scroll progress over the first viewport (about 85vh down to about 55vh cap height) with transform-origin left top, while the table translates up beneath it; after one viewport the word pins as a 64px strip header. Micro: clicking a header re-sorts with rows sliding to their new positions (FLIP, 300ms ease-out); row hover turns the row black and shows a 1-line drawing or thumbnail inline at the far right; tab switch is a hard cut. Signature moment: the first re-sort, when 60 grey rows reorder under a wordmark that never moves.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Terrain', a landscape and public-space practice in Lyon. IA: wordmark hero -> tabs Projects / About -> ledger of 60 works (No, title, place, client, year, surface with m2 / ha units, status, category) -> clicking a row opens an inline drawer with 80 words and one site plan -> About as a two-column text in the same 16px -> a colophon line stating page weight and 'low-impact website'.
directions.whyWorldClass: Maximum contrast between two scales and nothing else: a logo as architecture and a database as content. It is honest about what a practice site is (a list of work) and makes the list itself the interaction, with real data density that rewards reading.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: spec-table-hero, editorial-index, poster-crop, private-bank-ledger. Those either style a table as a spec sheet or crop type as a poster; none bind a scroll-scrubbed 800px wordmark to a genuinely sortable, FLIP-animated multi-column ledger with column positions foreshadowed in the hero.
directions.buildRisk: Falls flat if the data is thin or fake-looking (needs 50+ plausible rows with varied units and statuses) or if the giant letters reveal poor glyph quality: pick a face with excellent curves at 800px and use real text, not SVG outlines. On 390px keep the crop (two letters) and collapse the ledger to three columns (No, Title, Year) with the rest in the row drawer; reduced-motion should show the pinned state without scrub.

directions.name: Justified book page with travelling margin notes
directions.signature: A warm-paper page set like a well-made book: a centred portrait plate with a 9px credit line, then a fully justified old-style serif paragraph whose first line is indented by exactly the image's left offset, with superscript note numbers answered by small justified notes in the right margin; top-left a tiny ruled table of four cells acts as the chapter navigator (I. to IV.), top-right a pen signature.
directions.grammar: Grid: 12 columns at 1440; text block spans columns 4 to 9 (690px), the plate spans columns 5 to 8 (454px, 3:4), margin notes occupy columns 11 to 12 (217px) with 20px page margins. Type: one old-style serif throughout; body 20px/24px (leading 1.2, tight like print) tracking -0.01em, justified with hyphenation; notes and captions 12px/14px; wordmark in spaced caps of a humanist sans at 26px centred. Display:body ratio is about 1.3:1; hierarchy comes from position and measure, not size. Colour: paper #F2ECDF, ink #47403C, rules at 25 percent ink; small colour only inside the plates. Imagery: 3:4 portrait photographs or painted plates, one small poster-like object in the margin. Chrome: table-cell navigator, 'About / Contact' as two stacked 12px words. Absent: headings, buttons, cards, dividers, sans-serif body, any centring of text.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Adobe Caslon Pro ('acp') 20/24 + a humanist display sans for the wordmark (Studio OL); Arnhem + Theinhardt (Caruso St John); Tesseract (Toogood). Free stand-ins: Libre Caslon Text (Google) for body with EB Garamond as fallback for italics and small caps; Cormorant Garamond only for larger sizes; wordmark in Jost or Josefin Sans 400 with 0.02em tracking.
directions.motion: Entrance: paper tone fades up, then the plate reveals with a 600ms clip-path from the bottom edge and the paragraph sets in line by line (opacity, 20ms per line). Scroll: native; margin notes are position: sticky inside their paragraph's range so each note travels beside its reference and hands over to the next; the chapter table highlights the current cell and fills cell text ('II. Practice') as sections pass. Micro: hovering a note number draws a hairline from the superscript to the note; links are italic with no underline until hover. Signature moment: the hand-over of margin notes as a new plate arrives, like turning to a new spread. Mobile: notes become inline small paragraphs, the navigator becomes the fixed four-cell bottom bar seen on the exemplar.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Maison Arlo', a two-person cultural-strategy and interior-styling studio in Lisbon founded by a former magazine editor. IA: I. Studio (plate + three justified paragraphs with notes) -> II. Practice (a prose list of engagements, each with a marginal date and place) -> III. Journal (three long captions with plates) -> IV. Correspondence (address, a letter-style enquiry paragraph, signature).
directions.photoBrief: Three to five 3:4 portrait plates in a warm, low-contrast palette: a person arranging a table in a sunlit cafe interior, a figure in a white dress at a timber bar, a still life of ceramics, one flat graphic poster in vermilion for the margin. Soft window light, slight film softness, no saturated blues. Light grade toward paper warmth; no filters or grain overlays. The factory's existing interior photo and painting can stand in for two plates.
directions.whyWorldClass: It commits to book typography on the web with real rigour (justification, indent logic tied to the image, marginal notes, tight leading) and replaces all web chrome with a tiny ruled table. The taste level is in details most sites never attempt.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: bibliophile-spread, bilingual-epigraph, silent-luxury-restraint, manifesto-essay. Those imitate a book object or set display quotes; this is a live, scrolling, justified text page with sticky travelling margin notes and a table-cell chapter navigator, with no book skeuomorphism at all.
directions.buildRisk: Justified web text gets rivers: needs text-wrap: pretty, hyphens: auto with lang set, a 60 to 75 character measure and well-written copy of the right length; test at 390px where justification should switch off below about 34 characters per line or keep it only with hyphenation. Without at least two good plates it reads empty; source the photo pack first.

directions.name: Silhouette room elevation as catalogue
directions.signature: The entire first viewport is one flat elevation of a room drawn only in solid black silhouettes on white: a pendant light, a wall shelf with small appliances, a rail of utensils, a table and chair, a storage tower with a bicycle leaning on it. Every object is a designed product and a link; the only words are the designer's name top-left, 'Menu' top-right, and one word reversed out of an object.
directions.grammar: Grid: a single centred column 1088px wide with 176px side margins and a 1px #555 rule under the 47px header; the elevation occupies a 1088x680 field and shares a floor line; objects are spaced as in a real room with large white wall areas. Type: Helvetica-class grotesque, 19px, weight 600, mid-grey (not black, so the silhouettes own the black). No other text sizes on the home view. Colour: white, #000 silhouettes, #4E4E4E text. Imagery: vector silhouettes with a few knocked-out white details (spokes, dial, crate holes, book spines) and absolutely no outlines, gradients or shadows. Chrome: two words. Absent: photos, captions, grid of products, colour.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Helvetica Neue 600 (Morrison); Helvetica Neue lowercase (nendo); te-20 light (teenage engineering). Free stand-ins: Inter Tight 600 or Switzer 600 (Fontshare) for the Helvetica voice; Archivo 600 as an alternate.
directions.motion: Entrance: objects drop onto the floor line or slide onto the wall one at a time over about 1.2s (60ms stagger, short ease-out, 8px travel), the pendant swings two degrees and settles. Scroll: the elevation pins briefly, then the floor line becomes the top rule of a plain catalogue list below (object name, manufacturer, year). Micro: hovering an object flips it from solid to a 1.5px outline and prints its name + year in grey beside the cursor; the pendant's cord can be pulled (tiny drag) to toggle a night mode where silhouettes turn white on black. Signature moment: that solid-to-outline flip, which makes every silhouette read as a technical drawing for an instant.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Ines Halloran Office for Design', an industrial designer making everyday objects for European manufacturers. IA: silhouette room (each object = product entry) -> chronological catalogue list (year, object, manufacturer, material) -> one-paragraph 'Notes on the ordinary' -> books and exhibitions list -> shop link, contact line.
directions.whyWorldClass: A complete product portfolio communicated without a single photograph, in pure black shapes whose proportions are so right that each object is identifiable. It is witty, instantly memorable and unmistakably the work of an industrial designer rather than a web template.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: isometric-pixel-room, game-map-room-nav, material-cabinet, cutaway-illustration. Those are illustrative, coloured, isometric or game-like; this is a flat orthographic elevation in one colour with zero outline, where restraint and silhouette accuracy are the whole idea.
directions.buildRisk: Lives or dies on silhouette quality: generic icon-like shapes will look like clip art. Dodge: draw 9 to 11 objects as careful SVG paths based on real product proportions (a bentwood chair with slight leg splay, a pendant with a believable cord catenary, spoked wheel with 28 hairline spokes), keep consistent scale against a 2.4m room height, and include white knock-out details. At 390px crop to a three-object vertical composition (pendant, table + chair, bag) rather than shrinking the room.

directions.name: Ruled sheet with ASCII figure and display statement
directions.signature: A white sheet visibly ruled like ledger paper (four full-height hairline columns, faint 17px horizontal lines); a light-grey ASCII-character rendering of a figure or plant occupies the middle; over it, a four-line lowercase statement at about 112px in a monolinear grotesque, first line indented by one column, bleeding to both edges; three bold mono labels at the column tops are the whole navigation.
directions.grammar: Grid: 4 columns of 358px with 5px page margins, verticals at 1px #C8C8C8, horizontals at 1px #F0F0F0 on a 17px baseline; everything snaps to it. Type: display 112px/114px (leading 1.02), lowercase only, regular weight, natural tracking; labels and captions in 14px bold mono; ratio 8:1. ASCII layer is 9px mono in #B0B0B0 so it reads as tone, never as text. Colour: white, black, two greys; colour arrives only through images further down. Imagery: images hang in columns at natural ratio, captioned with filenames. Chrome: a filled 10px square precedes the name. Absent: uppercase, headings, buttons, footer.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Bugrino 112px + Neue Montreal Mono (Kaspar); Fragment Mono (Lebedev); Monument Grotesk + Monument Mono (Quatrieme Etage). Free stand-ins: Space Grotesk 400 for the slightly eccentric monolinear display (or Familjen Grotesk for a calmer read); Fragment Mono or JetBrains Mono 700 for labels; Geist Mono for the ASCII layer.
directions.motion: Entrance: horizontal rules draw top to bottom in 400ms, then the ASCII figure 'prints' row by row (a canvas or pre element revealing 4 rows per frame), then the statement types on by word. Scroll: the ASCII layer is fixed and slowly re-renders (a different density ramp or a 2-frame sway) while images slot into columns; filename captions count up. Micro: moving the cursor over the ASCII field locally swaps characters to a denser ramp (a soft spotlight of darker glyphs); nav labels invert on hover. Signature moment: the statement and the ASCII figure sharing the same space at wildly different scales, with the cursor 'developing' the figure.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'noa lindqvist', an independent web and brand designer in Basel, currently available. IA: statement sheet -> selected work as loose image columns with filename captions grouped by client code -> photos (personal) -> about as a four-column fact sheet (clients, tools, education, contact) set in the 14px mono.
directions.whyWorldClass: It makes the grid itself visible and beautiful, then breaks scale against it. The ASCII layer is used as quiet tone rather than a gimmick, and the confidence of one sentence at 112px in lowercase carries the whole identity.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: ascii-rasterizer, living-note-flavor-graphpaper, manpage, stdout. In those ASCII or the terminal is the spectacle; here ASCII is a pale watermark under a display-size typographic statement on a ruled sheet, with a column system that also organises the portfolio below. No terminal cosplay.
directions.buildRisk: The ASCII figure must be a recognisable, elegant silhouette (a tulip, a hand, a bird), not noise: precompute it from a clean high-contrast source and embed the character rows as text so the scroll-0 screenshot never catches a blank canvas. Keep its grey light enough that the 112px text stays legible. At 390px keep four narrow columns visible and let the statement wrap to five lines at about 60px.

directions.name: Micro-serif work column with a fixed ruled information ledger
directions.signature: The viewport is split 2:1 by a single hairline. Left: two large plates side by side with a three-column caption row in a 12.5px serif. Right: a non-scrolling 'Information' ledger of hairline-ruled label/value rows (clients, collaborators, education, exhibitions) in the same tiny serif, each section marked by a small custom ornament glyph; the name in the top bar is followed by a short run of the same ornaments.
directions.grammar: Grid: left pane 947px with 6px margins and 6px gutters; right pane 474px with a 157px label column and a value column; rules 1px #D9D9D9, some rows' rules only span the value column (stepped rules). Type: one text serif at 12.5 to 14.5px with leading about 1.15 for ledger rows and 1.45 for descriptions; italic for years and titles; no size above 14.5px anywhere. Underlined links with 1px offset. Colour: white, near-black text, grey 60 percent for the fixed copyright line; all colour comes from the plates. Imagery: square-ish plates with 3px radius. Chrome: 'Thumbnail View (+)' toggle; fixed copyright footer. Absent: headings larger than body, sans-serif, hover cards, buttons.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Marist Variable serif + Monument Grotesk Mono + a private dingbat font 'Galaxy Flower' (Takahashi); Jannon + ABC Camera Plain (Dubuis); Reckless (Mac Moss). Free stand-ins: Source Serif 4 at optical size 8 to 12 (Google) or Newsreader with opsz for the micro-serif; EB Garamond for small caps; ornaments drawn as 12 inline SVG glyphs (do not rely on a symbol font).
directions.motion: Entrance: ledger rules draw left to right row by row (20ms stagger), plates fade in at 300ms. Scroll: only the left pane's content moves; the ledger stays, and its 'Latest' row updates to reflect the project in view (a quiet cross-reference). Micro: hovering a collaborator or client name in the ledger dims all plates not associated with it; ornaments rotate 90 degrees on section hover; 'Thumbnail View' collapses the left pane to an 8-column contact sheet with a 250ms layout transition. Signature moment: the dim-by-association filter driven from a 12px text ledger.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Mirei Okafor', a visual artist and graphic designer working with glyph design, paper and moving image. IA: top bar (name + ornaments, view toggle) -> works (each: two plates, title/year, role, 90-word note, credits) -> fixed ledger: contact, latest trails, select clients, collaborators, education, group exhibitions, talks and workshops, press.
directions.photoBrief: Six to eight process and nature images in pairs: macro of pond surface or moss, hands working with paper pulp, a studio table from above, backlit botanical specimens on dark blue. Natural light, phone-camera honesty rather than studio polish, saturated greens and deep blues against the white page. Crop near-square (3:4 or 1:1). If no pack is available, substitute procedural plates (canvas-generated growth patterns) and reclassify as graphic-procedural.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is micro-typography as identity: the confidence to set an entire practice at 12px, organise it with stepped hairlines, and let hand-made ornaments carry personality. Dense, literate and unmistakably authored.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: editorial-index, anchor-annotated-index, private-bank-ledger, split-master-detail. Those are index or dashboard metaphors at normal UI sizes; this is a persistent CV ledger in micro-serif with stepped rules and bespoke ornaments beside a plate column, where the ledger filters the work.
directions.buildRisk: At thumbnail scale 12px text turns to grey texture, so the plates and the rule pattern must carry the screenshot: ensure two strong plates above the fold and visible rule rhythm. On 390px the ledger must become a second 'Info' view behind a top-bar toggle (as the exemplar does: 'Grid / Info'), not a squeezed column. Ornaments need real drawing effort or it reads as emoji.

directions.name: Horizontal card strip with tick-ruler minimap
directions.signature: On a pale grey field, one large white card sits slightly left of centre with the next card cropped at the right edge. The first card carries a six-line 72px statement with alternating indents and a single flat-colour disc overlapping half the text. Top-centre: a 200px ruler of 16 hairline ticks with a small outlined rectangle marking the current card. The cursor is a 1px crosshair.
directions.grammar: Grid: cards 73 percent of viewport width, 70 percent of height, 36px gaps, vertically centred with 130px above and below; text inset 56px inside the card; alternating line indent equals the inset. Type: one neutral grotesque; statement 72px/90px (leading 1.25, unusually open for display), weight 400, tracking -0.01em; labels 13px grey #6F6F6F above each card's top-left corner; ratio 5.5:1. Colour: field #EDEDED, cards #FFF, text #171717, exactly one saturated flat primary per card (yellow, orange, blue) used as a geometric shape. Imagery: none; each card is a typographic or geometric poster (a cropped word at 300px, a pixel glyph, a disc). Chrome: the ruler is the only navigation. Absent: nav bar, logo, footer, images, shadows, radius.
directions.typeStack: Observed: a private grotesque labelled 'X' (Rauno; reads as a Neue Haas / Unica class face); Suisse Intl (Archive for Space). Free stand-ins: Inter Tight 400 or Switzer 400 for the statement; Geist as an alternate; labels in the same family at 13px.
directions.motion: Entrance: the first card scales from 0.96 with the disc sliding in from the right edge of the card over 700ms (ease-out), then ruler ticks draw. Scroll: vertical wheel maps to horizontal translate of the strip with gentle snap to card centres; the ruler rectangle glides tick to tick and widens while moving (velocity stretch). Micro: crosshair cursor shows x,y readout in 10px mono near it on the grey field only; dragging the ruler rectangle scrubs the strip; each card's shape reacts once on hover (disc nudges 8px, cropped word shifts its crop). Signature moment: scrubbing the tiny ruler and watching full-size cards fly past in lock step. Mobile: cards become full-width and stack horizontally with the same ruler at the top; reduced-motion: plain horizontal scroll-snap with a static ruler.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Oda Viik', an interaction designer who writes and builds interface tools. IA as cards: 1 statement -> 2 'Craft' (a cropped word, links to experiments) -> 3 an essay series -> 4 to 9 individual projects each as one geometric poster with a 13px label -> 10 colophon / contact card. No conventional pages.
directions.whyWorldClass: It treats a personal site as a set of Swiss posters on a light table with an instrument-grade navigator. Every element is geometric and exact, and the interaction (ruler + crosshair) expresses the owner's discipline (interaction design) without a single screenshot.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: native-carousel-filmstrip, film-strip, axis-shift-scroll, infinite-canvas. Those are media carousels or scroll-direction tricks; this is a quiet poster-card system on a grey field with a tick-ruler minimap and crosshair, where the cards are typographic compositions and the navigator is the signature.
directions.buildRisk: Scroll-jacked horizontal travel breaks the 'page scrolls on the document root' rule if done with a wheel hijack; dodge by using a tall document with a position: sticky stage and translating the strip from scroll progress (no wheel listeners), which also keeps capture simple. The cards need genuinely good poster compositions (8 or more); weak ones make it a slider. Keep the first card's text large and the disc at scroll 0 so the thumbnail reads.

directions.name: Letterhead at display size
directions.signature: The hero is the letterhead: studio name, principal, a short horizontal rule, street address, city and postcode, telephone, email, each on its own line in a light grotesque at about 7.2vw (104px at 1440) with generous 0.02em tracking and 1.28 leading, flush left at 32px, running past the fold. Above it, the only navigation is six 16px underlined words in a row.
directions.grammar: Grid: one column, 32px left margin, no right margin (lines may nearly touch the edge); images below are full-width minus the same 32px with 140px vertical gaps and no captions other than a one-line title. Type: one grotesque in a light or regular weight; display 104px/134px, nav 16px with 0.1em tracking and underline; ratio 6.5:1; numerals are the star (use a face with handsome figures, lining, proportional). The rule is a drawn 80px line 4px thick, not a typed dash. Colour: white, soft black #231815 (a warm print black), nothing else. Imagery: unstyled photographs, no overlay, no hover. Chrome: none beyond the six words. Absent: logo, slogan, intro sentence, buttons, icons, footer.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Schemata renders a light wide grotesque (not exposed as a webfont; Arial stack reported); Helvetica 18px (Olgiati); Times New Roman (Pezo); Univers Next Pro Light (Pawson). Free stand-ins: Instrument Sans 400 or Hanken Grotesk 300 for the open light grotesque with good figures; Archivo 300 as alternate; for the Pezo-style serif variant use Tinos or system Times.
directions.motion: Entrance: lines appear one per 90ms from top to bottom with no translate (a typewriter-like cadence at line level), the rule draws left to right in 300ms. Scroll: native; as the letterhead leaves, a 16px one-line version of it pins in the header (name + telephone), then images arrive unanimated. Micro: hovering the email or telephone line underlines it with a 4px rule and copies on click with the line briefly reading 'Copied'; local time in the city appended in grey after the city line and ticking. Signature moment: the email address at 104px being a working, copyable control.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Atelier Sonoda / Kei Sonoda', an architecture and furniture studio in Kyoto. IA: Top (letterhead + six recent works as plain images with one-line titles) -> News (dated one-line list) -> Works (year-grouped text index) -> About (120 words + staff list) -> Contact (repeats the letterhead in Japanese and English).
directions.whyWorldClass: Radical honesty about what visitors want (who, where, how to reach) raised to display typography. It is confident enough to make an address the image, and the numerals and @ sign at 104px become graphic form.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: poster-crop, monogram-card, manifesto-essay, readme-manifesto. Those enlarge slogans, monograms or prose; this enlarges purely utilitarian contact data, uses zero rhetoric and no crop tricks, and keeps the rest of the page as unstyled as possible.
directions.buildRisk: With a mediocre typeface or default tracking it looks like an unstyled page: the face, weight (light), tracking and line pitch must be tuned so the block has even texture and the right edge varies gracefully. Fictional address and phone must be clearly non-real. At 390px set the same lines at about 9.2vw so the address still fills the first screen (the exemplar does exactly this); never truncate the email, let it define the size.

directions.name: Single object on a colour field with a white index rail
directions.signature: A quarter-width white rail on the left carries a stacked three-line caps wordmark, five thin grey nav words and a three-item news list pinned to the bottom; the other three quarters are one flat, slightly lit colour field (olive, clay, slate) on which a single everyday object (a lever handle, a kettle, a stool) floats with a soft shadow. Nothing else.
directions.grammar: Grid: rail 25.3 percent (365px) with 80px left inset; field edge to edge. Wordmark at top (78px from top), nav starts at one third height, news block ends 90px from bottom, so the rail has three islands separated by 150px+ voids. Type: wordmark bold condensed-ish grotesque caps 22px/23px with 0.04em tracking; everything else 14px weight 200 to 300, tracking 0.04em, grey #888 turning black on hover; ratio 1.6:1 only. Colour: white rail, one mid-value desaturated field colour per object, the object in neutral metal, ceramic or wood tones. Imagery: one object, roughly 50 percent of field width, shot or rendered straight-on with a single soft key light. Chrome: language switch in the field's top-right at 14px. Absent: headline, tagline, CTA, object caption, grid of products.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Acumin Pro 200 (Fukasawa), Adobe Garamond + custom OGATA caps (OGATA), Helvetica Neue 55 (Industrial Facility), Circular (Analogue). Free stand-ins: wordmark in Archivo Narrow 700 or Barlow Semi Condensed 700; text in Hanken Grotesk 200/300 or Inter 300 with 0.04em tracking; for the OGATA-flavoured variant use EB Garamond 16px/1.8 and Cormorant caps tracked 0.14em.
directions.motion: Entrance: the field colour wipes in from the rail edge (clip-path inset, 800ms ease-in-out), the object fades up with its shadow arriving 150ms later, rail text is already present. Scroll: each scroll section swaps object and field colour with a slow 900ms crossfade while the rail stays fixed and its news block is replaced by the object's data (name, manufacturer, year, material) in the same 14px grey; four dot indicators mirror OGATA. Micro: the object tracks the pointer with at most 3 degrees of rotation or a 6px shadow shift; nav words darken on hover, nothing moves. Signature moment: the colour field change, where one hue silently replaces another behind an unchanged composition. Mobile: rail collapses to a top band (wordmark left, 'Menu' right), field becomes 4:5 with the object, news list beneath.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Tomas Ekberg Design', an industrial design office making hardware and household objects for manufacturers. IA: rail (About, Projects, Publications, News, Contact) -> four featured objects, one per field -> projects as a year-grouped text list -> publications -> contact. Each object has a one-sentence description at most.
directions.whyWorldClass: It reproduces the designer's own value (an object should be quiet and self-evident) as layout: one thing, one colour, almost no words. The proportion of rail to field and the three islands of text are tuned like a book cover.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: silent-luxury-restraint, jeweled-vitrine, luxury-watch-callouts, material-cabinet, supplement-3d-product-stage. Those add callouts, dark vitrines or 3D stages; this has no annotation and no drama: a white index rail, a flat field, a single unlabelled object, with section changes expressed only by field colour.
directions.buildRisk: Entirely dependent on one convincing object. An SVG with layered gradients can do a brushed-metal lever handle, a ceramic cup or an anodised cylinder if built with care (specular band, core shadow, soft contact shadow via blurred ellipse); avoid complex organic forms. If the object looks like vector clip art the page is nothing. Optional three.js lathe geometry with a matcap is a fallback but not required. Prefer a stock product photo cut-out if a licence-free pack is sourced.

directions.name: Quiet page: narrow column, year-ruled index, one live detail
