directions.signature: A single 560px text column on off-white, optically centred: name and a grey 'Updated' date, four short first-person paragraphs with hairline-underlined links, then a ruled index where the year appears once per group in grey, titles in black and dates right-aligned in tabular figures, with one row shown in its open state revealing a small inline preview; a last line gives the live local time and city with a tiny hand-drawn animated glyph.
directions.grammar: Grid: one column 550 to 640px; left edge at about 31 percent of the viewport (not dead centre) on desktop, 24px margins on phone; index uses three sub-columns (108px year, flexible title, 60px date). Type: one UI grotesque at 15 to 16px/1.5; name weight 500, everything else 400; secondary text #8F8F8F; no size change anywhere, hierarchy is weight + grey only (ratio 1:1). Optional single italic serif phrase as the only flourish. Links: 1px underline in #D4D4D4, offset 3px, darkening on hover. Rules: 1px #EBEBEB, indented under repeated years. Colour: paper #FDFDFC, ink #111, two greys. Imagery: none on the page; previews only inside the open row. Chrome: none. Absent: nav, avatar, hero, icons, social buttons, dark-mode toggle, cards.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Inter (Benji Taylor), a private 'Sans' close to Inter (Emil Kowalski), Sohne + Newsreader italic (Paco Coursey), a grotesque + italic serif (Shu Ding). Free stand-ins: Inter with tabular figures and 'ss01' / 'cv11' alternates, or Geist; Newsreader italic for the single serif phrase.
directions.motion: Entrance: none beyond a 200ms opacity settle; the page is instant. Scroll: native. Micro (this is where all the craft goes): link underlines thicken from the left on hover (120ms); index rows expand with a height spring to show a 16:9 preview and two lines of abstract while sibling rows drop to 40 percent opacity; the year labels stick while their group scrolls; the footer clock ticks and its glyph blinks every few seconds; pressing a number key jumps to that index row (shown as tiny grey key hints on wide screens); view-transition cross-fade when opening an entry. Signature moment: the open row, which shows that a page this plain is in fact a finely tuned instrument.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Ilse Maren', a design engineer who builds interface tooling. IA: name + updated date -> four paragraphs (where from, current role, previous work, open-source tools, how to reach) -> 'Writing' index grouped by year (12 to 16 entries) -> 'Projects' as name + one-line description pairs -> live time and place line. No separate pages needed; entries open inline.
directions.whyWorldClass: This is the reference genre for design-engineer taste in 2025 and 2026: total removal of decoration, with quality proven through spacing, colour values two steps apart, tabular figures, and interactions that are felt rather than seen. It is extremely hard to do well because there is nowhere to hide.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: cmd-k-portfolio, readme-manifesto, manpage, mono-ink-restraint, minimal-mono-type. Those lean on a theme (terminal, README, monospace); this has no theme at all: a proportional-type prose page whose only structure is a year-ruled index and whose value is micro-interaction polish.
directions.buildRisk: The scroll-0 thumbnail can look like an empty document. Dodge: bring the ruled index into the first viewport (bio capped at four short paragraphs), render one row open by default with its small preview so the mechanic is visible without interaction, and keep the live clock line above the fold at 900px. The greys and rule colours need to be exact; one wrong value makes it look unstyled rather than refined. Previews must be procedural (CSS / SVG mini compositions), not stock imagery.

directions.name: Warm paper, tiny headline, real-DOM product window on a painted ground
directions.signature: Scroll=0 at 1440x900: warm paper page (#f7f7f4). Top-left a deliberately small two-line headline (26-32px, weight 400) with two pill buttons under it. From y=350 a full-width (1300px) panel filled with a muted painterly landscape; floating on it a real-DOM desktop app window (traffic-light dots, centered window title, left list of 5 tasks with status rings and tiny green/red diff counts, middle agent thread with grey log lines and a numbered question card, right document pane with headings) and a second smaller window overlapping bottom-right. The window is cropped by the fold. On 390px: headline 22px, one pill, the panel shows the left two panes of the window cropped at the right edge.
directions.grammar: Grid: 1300px content, 70px side margins at 1440; nav 52px, logo left, 5 links centered, 3 actions right (text, outline pill, black pill). Type scale is flat: display 26px vs body 16px (ratio 1.6); section heads are one ink line followed by a grey paragraph AT THE SAME 22px size, so hierarchy is colour (ink #26251e vs ~55% grey), never size. Tracking -0.0125em, leading 1.25. Cards: #f2f1ed on #f7f7f4, 1px hairline, radius 4-8px (never 24). One accent (burnt orange) used only for text links with an arrow. Inside windows: 11-13px UI type, 1px warm-grey hairlines, 28px rows, mono for file names, amber chip for the primary action, diff counts in small green/red. Imagery: oil or pastel landscape panels behind windows, or flat grey-lilac panels; shadows one soft layer (0 30px 60px -30px rgba(0,0,0,.3)). Absent: gradients, glows, icon tiles, big type, section dividers, illustrations.
directions.typeStack: Observed: CursorGothic (custom gothic) + Berkeley Mono + EB Garamond; Poolside: Untitled Sans + JetBrains Mono; Paper: Matter + Paper Mono; Granola: Quadrant + Melange. Free stand-ins: Fontshare 'Switzer' 400 (or Google 'Hanken Grotesk') for the gothic; 'JetBrains Mono' or 'Geist Mono' for mono; 'EB Garamond' (Google, the real one) for editorial asides.
directions.motion: Entrance: page text is static; the window rises 12px and fades in 400ms, then PERFORMS: thread lines append one at a time (Thought, Read, Searched) at 500-900ms intervals, a file chip slides in, diff counters tick up, the question card expands, caret blinks in the follow-up field; loop about 14s then cross-fade to a second scenario. Scroll: each feature section keeps its text column sticky while its window crops and scrolls internal content; overlapping window drifts at 0.9x. Hover: list rows get instant background, buttons darken, arrows nudge 2px. Signature motion: the agent thread streaming inside real DOM while the painted ground stays perfectly still. Reduced motion: completed thread state rendered statically.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client 'Halyard', an agentic code-review and release tool. IA: nav; small-headline hero with app window; three split features (sticky text left, cropped window right, alternating flat panel colours); 3x2 flat quote grid (quote, 40px avatar, name, role); 'Stay on the frontier' three text cards with orange links; changelog list (date, title, one line); hiring line; five-column footer.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is the current reference for confident restraint: the product, drawn at true fidelity in DOM, does all the persuading, and the 26px headline signals a company that does not need to shout. The painted ground gives warmth and a human counterweight to an AI product without a single gradient.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: devtools-live-code-hero, saas-dark-metric-hero, agent-chain-of-thought. Differs: light warm paper, sub-32px headline, a full multi-pane application window (not a code block or metric dashboard) over a painterly panel, flat two-tone type hierarchy.
directions.buildRisk: A sparse or fake-looking window ruins it: needs 40+ rows of believable microcopy at 11-13px with strict 1px hairlines. The painted ground must not look like a CSS gradient: use the factory's painting asset desaturated and blurred slightly, or multi-octave feTurbulence over a muted palette. Thumbnail timing: render the thread pre-populated at t=0 and animate additional lines after, so the scroll=0 capture is never an empty window.

directions.name: Flat-dark figure plates: FIG-captioned hairline machines and a linked console
directions.signature: Scroll=0: flat blue-black page (no glow). Bottom-left a 64px two-line headline in off-white. The right 45% holds a large hairline isometric drawing of a machine (a stack of slabs or a rack of sled modules) in 1px strokes at 30% white, with a handful of cells filled in the single accent green; above it a boxed mono tag 'FIG. 1' plus an uppercase caption. A 1px leader line runs from the drawing, with one 45-degree jog, to a small tabbed console panel (CLI / API / CONSOLE) top-left where a command is typed and three response lines print. A hairline with a tiny mono label ('POWERING') closes the fold. On 390px: headline first, then the FIG tag and drawing full width, console below joined by a vertical leader (as Oxide does).
directions.grammar: Margins 40-80px, 12 columns, nav 60-72px with a hairline bottom border. Headline 64px/1.0, weight 400-510, tracking -0.022 to -0.025em, colour #f7f8f8 (not pure white); secondary #8a8f98. Statement paragraphs at 48px/1.1 with the first sentence in ink and the rest grey. FIG triptych: three columns split by 1px rgba(255,255,255,.08) verticals; caption 'FIG 0.1' mono 11px tracked 0.08em at 40% opacity; drawing about 260px; then 15px/600 title and two lines of 15px grey. Vignette row: four #17181c panels (285x200) each showing ONE micro-UI, mono uppercase caption with a small triangle, then three hairline-separated lines where the first two words are white and the rest grey. Boxes: 1px borders, radius 0-4px. One accent only, used for fills in the drawing, the active tab underline and a primary button. Absent: gradients, glows, icons, rounded bento, photography.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Inter Variable (weight 510) + Berkeley Mono (Linear); Suisse Intl + GT America Mono (Oxide); Geist + Geist Mono (Vercel). Free stand-ins: Google 'Inter' variable at wght 510 (or Fontshare 'Switzer') + 'Geist Mono' or 'IBM Plex Mono'.
directions.motion: Entrance: the isometric drawing strokes draw on via stroke-dashoffset over 900ms, 40ms stagger per path, ease-out-expo; then accent cells light up in sequence like modules powering on; the console types its command (30ms per char) and prints three lines. Scroll: the two-tone statement turns from grey to ink word by word as it crosses 60% of the viewport; each FIG drawing separates into an exploded view (layers lift 12px each) tied to scroll progress and re-seats when centered. Hover: a FIG column raises its strokes from 30% to 70% opacity and lifts its top layer 6px; vignettes run tiny state changes (checkbox toggles, sparkline steps, bar fills). Signature moment: the exploded stack breathing apart and together under scroll. Reduced motion: drawings fully drawn, no explode.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client 'Corvid Systems': an on-prem inference appliance plus its control plane. IA: hero (headline, FIG. 1, linked console); customer wordmarks on a ruled line; two-tone statement; FIG 0.1-0.3 principles triptych; four capability vignettes; 'Purpose-built for' 3x2 hairline boxes; spec table with mono values; 'Now' index of three posts with generative monochrome thumbnails; newsletter row; footer.
directions.whyWorldClass: This is what the Linear school matured into once the glow was removed: authority through drafting discipline. FIG captions and hairline isometrics borrow the credibility of a technical manual, and the leader line physically ties hardware to software in one glance.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: blueprint-svg, cloud-devops-blueprint-grid, cutaway-illustration, trace-diagram, saas-dark-metric-hero. Differs: no blueprint-blue theme or graph paper; monochrome 1px hairlines on flat near-black with numbered FIG captions inside a product-marketing IA, two-tone statement typography, micro-UI vignettes, a single accent.
directions.buildRisk: Sloppy isometric geometry reads amateur instantly. Generate the drawings in JS from one iso projection function (true 30 degrees), use vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke, dash the hidden lines. Dark thumbnails can look empty: make sure accent cells and console text are lit in the default render (animation additive), and keep the drawing at least 520px wide at 1440.

directions.name: Drafted frame: construction lines past the edges, serif italic, keycap buttons
directions.signature: Scroll=0: warm grey paper. An 1120px frame is drawn with hairlines that continue past the frame to the viewport edges; diamond nodes sit on every intersection; a second dashed rule runs 110px outside the frame. Row 1: nav inside the frame with keycap-hinted actions. Row 2: a thin news strip. Row 3 (hero cell, about 450px tall): faint graph-paper fill, ghost guilloche watermark, centered 48px serif ITALIC headline in one saturated ink blue, two lines of duospace body, two buttons each ending in a small keycap (D, C). Row 4: three ruled columns (serif title, two mono lines). Row 5: the top of a DOM app window breaking the fold. On 390px: the outer frame and nodes persist with 16px gutters, headline 40px on two lines, buttons full width.
directions.grammar: Frame 1120px centered; rows separated by a double hairline 12px apart (a gutter band) that also extends edge to edge. Display: IBM Plex Serif italic 48px/1.2, weight 340, tracking -0.02em, #0b4fd8. Section heads: serif roman 26px. Body: duospace 16-18px/1.5 in #3a3f4b. Paper #f4f4f1, hairlines rgba(0,0,0,.1), nodes 7px white diamonds with 1px border. Buttons: 4px radius, 1px border, 2px hard bottom edge (a physical key), keycap = 18px bordered square in mono 11px. Quotes: plain text, key phrases behind a pale blue marker highlight; the featured quote is a card with an offset second border (stacked paper). Dense index cards (name, download count, one line, author) in four columns fading out at the bottom. Amp variant: sage paper, dotted column rules, vertical ticks on heads, display serif roman-italic pairing. Absent: shadows beyond 2px, gradients, photos, icons beyond 12px glyphs.
directions.typeStack: Observed: IBM Plex Serif (plexSerif) + iA Writer Quattro ('writer') + Zed Mono; Amp: Sagittaire Display/Text + Berkeley Mono. Free stand-ins: 'IBM Plex Serif' (Google, the real face, use wght 300-400 italic) + 'IBM Plex Mono' at 15px with -0.01em for the duospace body; for the Amp variant 'Instrument Serif' (Google) or Fontshare 'Boska' + 'JetBrains Mono'.
directions.motion: Entrance: construction lines draw outward from the frame to the viewport edges (scale 0 to 1, 700ms, ease-out-quint, 50ms stagger), each node pops 120ms after its two lines meet, then the headline fades up 8px. The watermark rotates once per 120s. Scroll: each row's rules draw as it enters; sticky nav picks up the frame's top rule. Micro: pressing D, C or S on the keyboard fires the matching button with a pressed state (translateY 2px, bottom edge collapses, 80ms) and the keycap inverts; marker highlights sweep left to right over 250ms on hover; index cards fade progressively. Signature moment: real keyboard-driven presses plus the line draw-in. Reduced motion: lines and nodes static, key presses still work without transforms.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client 'Quill', a native editor for code and prose. IA: nav; news strip; hero cell; three principles (Fast, Agentic, Collaborative style); DOM app window; logo row; quote grid with one stacked-paper featured card; 'Just Works' head with roadmap/releases buttons and two screenshot tiles in dashed frames; extensions index (4-col dense cards); 'Built with care' feature rows split by rules; footer in ruled cells.
directions.whyWorldClass: The layout shows its own drafting, which no template does, and pairs it with a literary serif italic and printed keyboard shortcuts: it reads as made by people who care about both typesetting and tooling. Every decorative element is structural.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: blueprint-svg, cloud-devops-blueprint-grid, swiss-grid-serif, patent-plate. Differs: light paper, rules that overrun the frame with intersection nodes as the ornament, serif italic in one ink blue, duospace body, keycap affordances that actually bind keys.
directions.buildRisk: If nodes drift off intersections at any breakpoint the illusion dies: derive every rule and node from the same CSS custom properties on one grid, test at 1440, 1024, 390. The DOM app window must be credible (see warm-paper-agent-window risk). Keep the blue to one hue; adding a second accent breaks the register.

directions.name: Inspector overlay: the page annotates its own typography
directions.signature: Scroll=0: near-white page (#fcfcfc), a 720px left-aligned column. A three-line 60px title (sans, last word in serif italic) is rendered as a live design-tool selection: two cyan guides hug the x-height of line 1 with a mono chip 'x-height' on a dotted leader; one word in line 2 sits in a 1px blue selection box with four square handles and a dimension badge above it; the italic word has a chip naming its font; a token chip names the background colour; between the byline pill and the CTA a pink redline band reads '32 px'; the pill CTA has a dashed padding outline and a 'Call to action' chip. Nothing else above the fold except a small mark top-left and two pills top-right. On 390px the selection box wraps two lines and chips reflow above and below (as observed).
directions.grammar: Column 720px, margins auto. H1 60px/1.0, Inter weight 500, tracking -0.025em, lines alternating #1f1f1f and #4a4a4a, final word Libre Baskerville italic. Chips: mono 12px, white fill, 1px #e5e5e5, radius 6px, padding 2px 6px. Leaders: 1px dashed #cfcfcf ending in a 6px ring. Selection: #3b82f6 1px, 6px white handles with blue 1px border, 6% blue fill. Guides: #22d3ee 2px. Redline: #ec4899 with 10% fill, mono 12px label. Body 18px/1.6 in #555 with single serif-italic emphasis words. Logo wall: 3-column table with dashed rules, 240x120 cells, 55% grey marks. Cards: double ring (1px border, 4px gap, 1px outer), 12px radius, large empty top area with one small glyph. CTA: sky-blue pill with a 1px inner highlight. Absent: hero image, nav links, colour outside the four annotation hues.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Inter Variable + Libre Baskerville + Berkeley Mono (also loaded for specimens: Open Runde, Mondwest, Heldane). Free stand-ins: 'Inter' and 'Libre Baskerville' are both on Google Fonts (use the real ones); mono 'Geist Mono' or 'JetBrains Mono'.
directions.motion: The entrance IS the signature: the title is present plain; a drawn arrow cursor glides in and clicks the word, the selection box snaps on with handles (120ms) and its badge counts up to the measured size; guides slide in from the left (scaleX, 300ms ease-out); chips fade and rise 6px with 90ms stagger while leaders draw by dashoffset; the redline grows from 0 to 32px as its number ticks. After that the overlay is live: hovering any chip outlines its target; hovering any body block shows a measured badge from getBoundingClientRect; dragging a handle actually resizes the tracked word's font-size within limits. Scroll: annotations fade as the hero leaves; inline 'figures' (easing-curve editor, radius slider, layered-shadow toggle) replay on enter. Reduced motion: all annotations rendered static, no cursor.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client 'Kerning Hours', a paid design-engineering magazine by one author. IA: annotated hero with byline pill and subscribe CTA; essay opening ('What makes an interface feel great?'); a ruled strip of four interactive figures; 'Read by N people at' logo table; About the author with two double-ring project cards; three free issues (number, title, read time rows); single price card; FAQ; quiet footer.
directions.whyWorldClass: It turns the invisible craft (x-height, spacing, tokens) into the hero image, so the thumbnail itself proves the author's eye. It is self-referential without being a gimmick because every label is true of the element it points at.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: anchor-annotated-index, annotated-case-study, luxury-watch-callouts, variable-font-axis-playground. Differs: the annotations target the page's own hero typography as a design-tool overlay (selection handles, redlines, measured badges, token chips) and stay interactive; newsletter IA rather than case study or product callouts.
directions.buildRisk: Hard-coded annotation coordinates break on font load and resize: position everything from live DOM rects after document.fonts.ready and on resize, and make the labels report real measurements. The annotated state must be the default render (animation replays on top) so the scroll=0 thumbnail never catches a bare title. Without substantial essay content below, it reads as a trick: write the article.

directions.name: Lab memo: ticked column guides, side rail, margin numerals, serif body
directions.signature: Scroll=0: warm paper. Five full-height vertical hairline guides with short tick marks at the top define the layout. Far-left rail (x=64): a small black mark, five stacked 15px links with a 2px blue tick on the active one, and one square outlined button. Just right of the second guide a 9px margin numeral '01'. Main column (x=410 to 1100): a 36px grotesk two-line statement with one dotted-underlined product name, two paragraphs of 16px SERIF body with one sentence under a hatched highlight, two square buttons (black fill, outline). At y=605 numeral '02' and a grey panel bracketed by four corner ticks holding a 5-column table of grey institutional wordmarks, cropped by the fold. On 390px: rail collapses to mark plus the word 'Menu', outer two guides remain, logos become 3 columns.
directions.grammar: Guides at roughly x=64, 323, 410, 1101, 1274 of 1440 (asymmetric: wide empty right margin). Headline 36px/1.1 weight 400 tracking -0.02em; body serif 16px/1.45 near-black; nav 15px; numerals 9px serif grey. Buttons: 0 radius, 1px black, 28px tall. Links: saturated default-blue (#1f00ff family). Leaderboard: rank numeral, 8px coloured square, name plus grey qualifier, 110px 4px bar track with terracotta fill, right-aligned percent, hairline row rules, 'View leaderboard' text link in blue. Variants to mix: PI's monospace 14px body with a square-bullet timeline and 4px hard-shadow feature boxes; TML's centered 660px serif column with a tracked techno-caps wordmark. Absent: hero art, icons, rounded cards, more than two colours, any section background change except the one grey panel.
directions.typeStack: Observed: NB International + STK Bureau Serif + Geist Mono (Cognition); Chakra Petch + Iowan Old Style BT + GT America (TML); Signifier + system mono (PI). Free stand-ins: Fontshare 'Switzer' or Google 'Hanken Grotesk' for the grotesk; 'Source Serif 4' or 'Newsreader' for body serif ('Literata' for the Iowan feel); 'Chakra Petch' is on Google (real); 'Geist Mono' or 'IBM Plex Mono'.
directions.motion: Near-still on purpose. Entrance: guides draw top-down over 600ms with 60ms stagger, ticks appear last; text fades 300ms with no translate. Scroll: the rail is sticky and its blue active tick slides between links (200ms); margin numerals pin beside their section until it ends; logo cells go from 45% grey to ink as the panel centers. Signature moment: the leaderboard race: on enter, bars fill in sequence while percentages count, and two rows swap places once (FLIP, 350ms) to land on the final ranking. Hover: dotted underline turns solid and the hatch highlight sweeps across; table rows tint. Reduced motion: final table, no swap.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client 'Meridian Research', a small frontier lab that operates an autonomous engineering agent called Atlas. IA: 01 statement and two buttons; 02 institutions table; 03 benchmark explanation plus leaderboard; 04 research timeline (dated mono entries, featured ones boxed with hard shadow); 05 operating principles as numbered serif paragraphs; 06 open roles table (role, team, location); colophon footer with one line of legal.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is the house style of the most serious AI labs in 2026: the site behaves like a typeset memo, and the confidence comes from what is withheld. Cognition's ticked guides and margin numerals show how to make a text-only page look engineered rather than unstyled.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: manifesto-essay, readme-manifesto, minimal-mono-type, biotech-investor-brief, editorial-index, manpage. Differs: a company homepage (not an essay or terminal pastiche) built on visible ticked guides, a left rail, margin numerals, grotesk head over serif body, with a benchmark table as the centerpiece.
directions.buildRisk: The line between 'restrained' and 'unstyled' is exact guides, optical serif sizing and table craft; any default-looking spacing collapses it. Thumbnail risk is a text-only frame: keep the logo panel entering at y=600 and the hatched highlight plus blue tick visible so there is graphic incident above the fold. Do not add an illustration to compensate.

directions.name: Artboard strip with a tick minimap: tool chrome as art direction
directions.signature: Scroll=0: flat #ededed ground. At top center a minimap: one small outlined rectangle (the viewport) followed by about 16 thin vertical ticks. Below, a white artboard (about 1060x635, no shadow, no radius) holds an 80px neo-grotesque statement in six short lines with every second line indented 56px; a huge pure-yellow circle (diameter = board height) is clipped by the board's right edge and sits UNDER the text. A 13px grey label sits above the next board, whose left 150px peeks in at the right edge showing a cropped thick black shape. A thin crosshair marks the pointer. On 390px: boards stack vertically at full width, the minimap becomes a vertical tick rail on the left edge, first board shows statement at 40px over the circle.
directions.grammar: Ground #ededed, boards #fff, gaps 24-36px, labels 13px #666 top-left above each board. Display 80px/90px weight 400 tracking -0.01em pure black; no other text sizes on the first board. Colour: black, white and three unmixed primaries (#ffff00, #ff5800, #0000ff) used as single giant shapes. Cropping is the composition tool: words at 400px+ cut by board edges, circles cut by edges. Devouring variant: sheet inset 144px, 2-column 24px/40px copy at 400 weight, vertical tick ruler with long ticks every 8, a 1px orange playhead spanning the page, mono 11px tags on orange. Index below the strip: 3-column masonry, tiles with 12px radius double-ring, name plus month-year, grey full-width bar buttons. Absent: nav bar, logo, buttons in the hero, shadows, gradients, body copy on the first board.
directions.typeStack: Observed: custom faces named 'X' and 'DD' (Helvetica Now class neo-grotesque) + JetBrains Mono. Free stand-ins: Google 'Inter Tight' 400-500 or Fontshare 'Switzer' for the grotesque; 'JetBrains Mono' (real) for tags.
directions.motion: Scroll: a tall spacer with a sticky stage maps vertical document scroll 1:1 to horizontal translate of the strip (lerp 0.12 for inertia); the minimap rectangle slides in step and the ticks nearest it grow in height by proximity (dock-style falloff), so position is felt before it is read. Entrance: boards slide in from the right 60ms apart; the circle scales from 0.8 with a soft spring. Interaction: click a tick to travel (smooth), J/K or arrow keys step board to board, the crosshair shows coordinates while moving. Devouring-style variant for the long-form section: an orange playhead follows scroll with spring lag and the nearest ruler tick stretches. Index tiles autoplay their prototype on hover only. Signature moment: the proximity-scaled tick minimap. Reduced motion: direct mapping without lerp, or a plain vertical stack.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client 'Ilse Varga', an interaction designer (or a two-person studio, 'Parallel Office'). Boards: statement; current product or course; 'Craft' (cropped word); an essay; posters; contact. After the strip releases: craft index masonry (prototype name, date, View Prototype), a short writing list, a one-line colophon.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is the most imitated personal site of the interface-craft school because the navigation device is the design: a design tool's canvas and scrubber promoted to brand. Swiss primaries plus one typeface keep it timeless rather than trendy.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: infinite-canvas, axis-shift-scroll, native-carousel-filmstrip, swiss-poster, scroll-snap-choreography. Differs: artboard metaphor with labels, a proximity-scaled tick minimap as the only chrome, crop-driven Swiss compositions in unmixed primaries, and a second register (playhead ruler) for long-form.
directions.buildRisk: Vertical-to-horizontal mapping must run on the document root (sticky stage inside a tall spacer) and not trap scroll; test wheel, trackpad and keyboard. Compositions depend on exact crops: fix board aspect ratio and size shapes in board units. If boards beyond the first are weak the concept reads as a one-liner: design six boards, each a poster.

directions.name: Featherweight instrument catalogue: pictogram departments, hairline triptychs, black stage
directions.signature: Scroll=0: pure white. A 110px header made of five department clusters: a solid black pictogram (about 80px: a fan-flower, a flask, an empty square, a magnifier-and-dial cluster) with a 26px ultralight lowercase word to its right and three 12px lowercase sub-links beneath; then a 9px block of dense small-print text and a heavy black geometric logo at far right. Below, a two-line campaign title in massive black geometric caps (cap height about 110px, tight, with stencil-like cuts), to its right a small outlined calendar-style badge with an orange band and a three-row table of model codes with orange version numerals. Under that, the top of a row of three flat front-elevation instruments (cream faceplates, orange and green keys, an LCD, a speaker grille) in hairline-divided columns. On 390px: departments become a 2x3 grid of pictogram plus word, title at 64px on three lines, one instrument full width.
directions.grammar: Type is almost weightless: weights 100-300, lowercase everywhere, sizes 12 / 16 / 26 / 53px; nothing bold except the logo and campaign caps. Colour: black, white, one orange (#ff4f00), plus the product's own cream and dark green. Catalogue rows: three equal columns split by 1px #cfcfcf verticals with no card boxes, ground #f6f8f8, objects about 330px tall as cut-outs with no shadow; rows alternate with full-bleed black 'stage' sections where objects stand in a pool of light and the only text is a 12px product code bottom-left. Product story sections: black, centered, one 53px ultralight line, one 22px light-grey paragraph max 920px wide. Absent: buttons, cards, borders with radius, icons other than the pictograms, any gradient.
directions.typeStack: Observed: te-20 and te-40 (custom ultralight grotesk, body weight 300, display weight 100) plus a custom heavy geometric campaign face. Free stand-ins: Google 'Hanken Grotesk' or 'Inter' at wght 100-300 for text; 'Unbounded' 800-900 (Google) with -0.04em tracking, or hand-drawn SVG letterforms, for the campaign caps; 'IBM Plex Mono' for codes.
directions.motion: Chrome is instant; objects are alive. Entrance: none on text. Pictograms run a stepped (8fps) idle loop on hover: the flower spins, the flask fills, the dial turns. Catalogue objects answer hover with their own function: LCD segments animate a pattern, a knob rotates 30 degrees, an LED blinks, a key depresses 2px. Stage sections: the pool of light fades up over 800ms as the section enters and the object's indicator lights come on last. Product scroll: a tall front elevation slides vertically through a fixed frame as you scroll (the object is longer than the viewport). Signature moment: a playable faceplate: clicking keys lights the LCD and (optionally) fires WebAudio blips. Reduced motion: static objects, hover highlights only.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client 'Kobold Instruments': pocket synthesizers, a field recorder, a radio. IA: department header; campaign title with model/version table; instrument triptych (light); stage triptych (black); 'latest' strip (newsletter, now); guides and downloads index table (model, firmware, pdf size); store deals row; six-column lowercase footer.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is the canonical proof that hardware can be sold with catalogue discipline instead of cinematic hype: the lightest type on the web against the heaviest logo, and products shown as objects of graphic design. Nothing else in the lens is as instantly recognisable from a thumbnail.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: skeuomorphic-mixer, spec-sheet-instrument, atelier-faceplate, mastering-lathe, supplement-3d-product-stage. Differs: a catalogue grammar (pictogram departments, ultralight lowercase, hairline triptychs, white and black alternation) with several flat orthographic instruments, not one skeuomorphic console or spec sheet.
directions.buildRisk: The instruments must be drawn obsessively (4px module, 0.5px strokes, silk-screen legends, real grille patterns) or they read as clip-art: limit to three hero objects of about 150 SVG nodes each and reuse parts. A stock heavy font will look generic for the campaign title: cut the letterforms as SVG paths. Keep type truly light; rendering at weight 300+ everywhere loses the register.

directions.name: Studio seamless with a live-screen object: the product is the only thing on the page
directions.signature: Scroll=0: the whole viewport is a mid-grey studio seamless (#a9a9a9 centre, slightly darker edges, a soft horizon and floor reflection). Top: a small black logo mark left, three columns of two stacked 13px links spread across the width, a square cart glyph right. Centered at y=165 a 20px grey kicker word, under it a 47px medium geometric headline with -0.06em tracking. Below, centered and about 520px tall, a handheld device drawn in CSS/SVG (one white unit behind, one black unit on a dock in front) whose screens run a LIVE four-shade green LCD game on canvas; the devices cast a contact shadow and a faint reflection. No buttons, no body copy. On 390px: one device, 34px headline, links collapse to a two-line row.
directions.grammar: No containers at all on the hero. Headline 47px/1.0 weight 500 tracking -2.8px; dark variant 97px/0.83 weight 700 tracking -4px overlapping the object. Kicker 20px at 60% black. Below the hero: full-bleed image cards inset 29px with 28px radius; circular 44px black arrow buttons; a hairline-framed 'OS' section in a pixel face; two-column spec table with hairlines; colourway swatches. Playdate variant: flat saturated section colour (#ffc500), 72px heavy headings, 28px body, one rotated sticker. Colour comes only from the object's screen. Absent: feature icons, gradient text, cards with borders, testimonial blocks.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Circular XX (weights 500 and 700) + NeueBit pixel face (Analogue); Roobert (Playdate); FK Grotesk Neue (Even Realities). Free stand-ins: Fontshare 'Satoshi' 500/700 or Google 'Figtree' for Circular; 'Onest' 700 for Roobert; 'Pixelify Sans' or 'Silkscreen' for the pixel face.
directions.motion: Entrance: the object settles from scale 0.96 with its shadow sharpening (700ms ease-out); the LCD boots (logo wipe) then runs an attract loop. Scroll: ground lerps grey to black; the pair rotates a few degrees in CSS 3D and the dock unit slides out; image cards rise with 0.92x parallax. Interaction: d-pad and buttons depress on pointer down (inset shadow swap, 60ms) and arrow keys actually play the game; colourway swatches recolour the device via custom properties with a 300ms crossfade. Signature moment: a playable LCD inside a DOM object on an otherwise silent page. Reduced motion: LCD shows a static title screen, no rotation.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client 'Halden' and its FPGA handheld 'Nocturne Pocket'. IA: restock hero; four large image cards (screen, dock, link cable, cartridge wall); OS section with pixel-type captions; spec table; editions (colourways); developer note; announcements list (date, title); single 'Store' line; minimal footer.
directions.whyWorldClass: It reproduces the highest standard of product photography restraint (one object, one seamless, one line of type) and then exceeds a photograph by making the screen live. Analogue and Playdate show that removing everything else is what makes hardware feel inevitable.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: supplement-3d-product-stage, configurator-hero, isometric-pixel-room, playable-terminal-game, dithered-lo-fi. Differs: studio-seamless photographic grammar rebuilt with a CSS object whose LCD is a running game, near-zero chrome, three-column link nav; no WebGL turntable.
directions.buildRisk: A CSS device next to memory of real renders can look toy-like: use a front orthographic elevation, matte material from two or three stacked inset shadows plus fine noise, exact button dishing, a believable contact shadow and a blurred flipped reflection; avoid fake perspective. Draw the LCD game at native low resolution and scale with image-rendering: pixelated. Later sections need imagery too: build them from the same object at different crops rather than stock photos.

directions.name: Bordered-cell layout with a big-pixel colour field and a sprite mascot
directions.signature: Scroll=0: cream page (#fbfbf8) assembled from visible cells with 1px borders. Top row: a small pixel logo cell, seven nav links each in its own cell, a 'Login' cell and a solid black end cell. Left block (1008px wide): a tall empty cell with a 96px two-line grotesk headline anchored to its bottom-left. Right block (432px): a slightly darker cell with a 26px three-line statement near its bottom. Under the headline, a full-width band 360px tall made of 90px square pixels in a five-step sunset ramp (yellow, amber, orange, red-orange, crimson) arranged as a low-frequency gradient, one cell carrying an 11px mono tag, and a small black pixel-art animal sitting on the band's bottom-right edge. Right of the band: three small down-arrows and a 'Featured news' card. On 390px: nav collapses to logo cell plus menu cell, headline 52px, band becomes 6 columns of 65px pixels.
directions.grammar: Everything snaps to a cell grid; borders 1px #e4e4de; radius 0. Headline 96px/1.0 weight 500 tracking -0.02em; statement 26px/1.1; body 16px; tags Space Mono 11-12px uppercase. Palette: cream, black, the five-step ramp (#ffd800, #ffaf00, #ff8205, #fa500f, #e10500). Logo strip: 270px bordered cells with black marks. Case cards: photo or flat colour with dark overlay, white 36px text, mono chip. Model table rows: name, split-pill version badge, 'params / active / context' in mixed ink and grey. Poolside variant swaps the ramp for lilac and blue tints on outlined cells. Absent: rounded corners, shadows, gradients that are not quantised into cells.
directions.typeStack: Observed: ALT Mistral (custom grotesk, 500) + Space Mono + Inter; Untitled Sans + JetBrains Mono (Poolside); Geist + Geist Mono + Geist Pixel Square (Factory). Free stand-ins: Google 'Schibsted Grotesk' or 'Hanken Grotesk' 500 (or Fontshare 'Switzer'); 'Space Mono' (Google, real); 'Pixelify Sans' for pixel accents.
directions.motion: The field is digital, so motion is stepped, not eased. Entrance: cells switch on row by row (40ms per cell) like a display test, then settle into the gradient. Idle: each pixel moves one ramp step on a staggered noise schedule (hard cut, every 600-1800ms) and a diagonal wave crosses every 6s. Pointer: cells under the cursor jump two steps hotter and cool back over 1.2s, leaving a heat trail. The sprite walks the band edge at 6fps, sits when the cursor is near, and looks at it. Nav cells fill black instantly on hover and release in 150ms. Scroll: the headline cell compresses into the sticky nav row. Signature moment: a magnified low-res sunset that reacts to touch. Reduced motion: static gradient, static sprite.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client 'Solene', a sovereign enterprise AI platform. IA: cell nav; headline plus side statement; mosaic band; logo cells; two large customer cards; three product cells each with an 8x8 pixel glyph; model table with split-pill versions; deployment options (cloud, VPC, on-prem) as three cells; news list; footer of cells with a giant pixel wordmark.
directions.whyWorldClass: It gives an enterprise AI company a memorable, ownable image (a pixel-magnified warm colour field and a mascot) while the bordered-cell layout keeps it rigorous and European. It is the tasteful end of the 2026 pixel revival: big, slow, warm pixels inside strict structure.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: dithered-lo-fi, morphing-grid, truchet-tile-generative, css-voxel-data-city, de-stijl-mondrian. Differs: corporate bordered-cell IA with a large-pixel warm gradient field as brand image and a sprite mascot; pixels are huge (90px) and quantised from a smooth gradient, not dither texture or tile pattern.
directions.buildRisk: A random coloured grid looks cheap: drive colour from low-frequency value noise quantised to the ramp so it reads as a magnified image with coherent regions, and align the pixel grid exactly to the layout columns. Sprite quality matters: draw at least 6 frames at 24x24. Implement the field as a CSS grid of divs or a 2D canvas (both capture-safe).

directions.name: Calm-tech hardware: inset golden-hour photograph, flared display type, floating commerce modules
directions.signature: Scroll=0: a silver paper-grain page shows as an 18px border around one photograph with 24px corner radius filling the viewport: a top-down golden-hour shot of a matte tablet lying on grass, rotated about 12 degrees, dappled leaf shadows falling across a paper-like screen that displays a fine botanical engraving, two fallen leaves nearby. Top-left over the photo: a small rounded logo tile, a 60px light flared headline in white with very tight tracking on one line, and a 24px two-line sub. Top-right: a frosted module with three nav words and an amber button, and beneath it a promo card with a circular stamp badge. Bottom-left: a 290x180 video thumbnail with a 2px amber border and play triangle. Bottom-right: a 13px caps stock line and a 320px-wide amber button. On 390px: photo crops to the tablet, headline 36px on two lines, modules stack at the bottom as a sheet.
directions.grammar: Floating modules replace the nav bar and the footer CTA; all modules share 12-16px radius and a 1px amber or white hairline. One accent: amber #ff9d00 with dark-brown text. Display: flared light face 60px/1.0 weight 300 tracking -0.07em; text 16-24px humanist grotesk; microcopy 13px caps weight 600. Second section: silver grain with diagonal light streaks and a 56px statement left-aligned at x=205. Scenes are inset rounded photographs, never full-bleed edge to edge. Palette comes from the photographs: moss, straw, warm grey, amber. Absent: dark UI, device mockups on gradients, spec grids above the fold, icons.
directions.typeStack: Observed: ABC Arizona Flare (300) + ABC Room / Room Extended (Daylight); Messina Sans 300 (Sandbar); Futura PT + Akkurat (Light Phone); Arcadia Display (Mercury). Free stand-ins: Google 'Fraunces' at wght 300, opsz 144, SOFT 0, WONK 0 (or Fontshare 'Zodiak' light) for the flared display; 'Hanken Grotesk' for text; 'Jost' for the Futura variant.
directions.motion: Slow and atmospheric. Entrance: the photograph settles from scale 1.04 over 1600ms ease-out; a leaf-shadow layer drifts across the device on a 20s alternate loop; modules float in with 500ms fades 120ms apart. Scroll: the hero frame insets further and pins while the statement reveals word by word (opacity 0.15 to 1, scrubbed); the light-streak layer shifts a few pixels. Hover: amber deepens, the video thumbnail scales 1.03 and its border thickens. Signature moment: the device screen cycles between three pages with a simulated e-paper refresh (80ms invert flash, then settle), the only fast thing on the page. Reduced motion: static photo, statement fully visible, no flash.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client 'Alder Computer' and its sunlight-readable tablet 'Alder One'. IA: inset photo hero with modules; manifesto statement; three scenes (read, write, outside) as inset photos with one line each; display explainer with an emissive-versus-reflective comparison slider; short spec list; family bundle card; three press quotes; FAQ accordion; persistent order module.
directions.photoBrief: Six warm natural-light photographs. (1) Hero: top-down, a thin matte-screen tablet lying on short grass or linen, rotated about 12 degrees, golden hour, hard dappled leaf shadows across device and ground, device about 35% of frame, room for type top-left. (2) Hands holding the tablet reading outdoors on a bench, shallow depth of field. (3) Desk by a window with hard sun stripes across the screen. (4) Macro of the matte screen edge and bezel texture. (5) A child drawing on the tablet on a wooden floor. (6) Ambient sky or leaves for a quiet band. Treatment: warm white balance, low contrast, 4-6% film grain, no blue screen glow, no studio seamless. Fallback if no product stock exists: composite a CSS/SVG top-down tablet (rounded rect, layered shadows, engraving on screen) over a stock grass or linen texture with an animated SVG leaf-shadow layer in multiply.
directions.whyWorldClass: It is the clearest statement of the humane-hardware register: the product is shown in the life it promises (sunlight, grass, paper) rather than on a pedestal, and the flared display face plus amber make it warm without being twee. The floating-module chrome is distinctive and commerce-ready.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: luxury-resort-cinematic-stillness, mental-health-calm-canvas, ev-automotive-cinematic-hero, silent-luxury-restraint. Differs: a hardware product page with floating commerce modules over an inset photograph, flared display type with -0.07em tracking, an amber single accent and an e-paper refresh motif.
directions.buildRisk: Entirely dependent on the hero image: a generic stock tablet shot makes it a 2021 Shopify theme. Use the composite fallback (drawn device over real ground texture plus leaf shadows) and grade everything to one warm LUT. Keep modules few (four at most) and aligned to one inset grid, or the hero turns into popup clutter.

directions.name: Reading-Line Ruler Manual
directions.signature: Scroll=0: a white sheet floats on a flat #ededed ground (144px side margins, 128px top). Fixed at the far left is a vertical ruler of about 40 hairline ticks, every chapter marked by a longer tick. A 1px orange hairline crosses the ENTIRE viewport at the reading line, starting from a small orange play triangle on the ruler and ending under a mono uppercase orange tag at the sheet's right edge; it visibly strikes through a line of body text. Inside the sheet: a 20px orange dot where a logo would be, a five-line plain nav list on the second column axis, and two columns of 24px text. There is no headline. On 390px the ruler drops, the sheet goes full width, the hairline and tag remain.
directions.grammar: Grid: sheet 1152px on a 1440 canvas; inner padding 128px; two 400px text columns with a 64px gutter (x=272 and x=736). Type: ONE size for nav, lede and body (24px/40px, weight 450 to 500, tracking -0.01em); hierarchy comes from position, a grey (#8f8f8f) tone for cross-referenced terms and a single serif-italic word; captions are mono uppercase 12px with 0.02em tracking. Use text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic so the hairline lands exactly on a baseline at load and plates align to cap height. Spacing: 40px baseline rhythm, 120px between blocks. Colour: ground #ededed, sheet #fcfcfc, ink #000, one accent #ff5500, plates #f7f7f7 with 12px radius and a 1px #eeeeee edge. Imagery: none; small SVG diagrams drawn in black hairline plus the one orange (a toggle with an arrow, nested ellipses with tick hatching, a line minimap, a strip of thin slices), each captioned bottom-left in mono caps. Absent: hero headline, photos, shadows, gradients, icons, buttons other than the hanging tag.
directions.typeStack: Observed: DD (custom neo-grotesk close to Neue Haas / Suisse) plus JetBrains Mono; a serif italic for one emphasised word. Free stand-ins: Inter Tight 450 or Fontshare Switzer for the grotesk, JetBrains Mono or Geist Mono for captions, Newsreader Italic or Instrument Serif Italic for the accent word.
directions.motion: Technique: the hairline is position: fixed and driven by animation-timeline: scroll(root), translating down the ruler's height 1:1 with document progress (linear, no smoothing); scroll-target-group with :target-current darkens the current chapter's long tick; the tag text swaps to the current chapter name through a 200ms cross-fade. Ticks within 4 positions of the pointer lengthen with a dock-style falloff using a linear() spring (bounce 0.2, 400ms). Entrance: sheet rises 12px and fades in over 450ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1); ruler ticks draw top to bottom at 12ms stagger via sibling-index(); the orange dot pops with a spring; the hairline sweeps in from the left over 500ms. Plates: each diagram runs a slow self-demonstrating loop (dot travels the arrow in 1.6s ease-in-out, rests 600ms) with offset phases. Hover: grey cross-reference terms go to black in 150ms. Signature moment: the orange reading line crossing lines of text as you scroll while the ruler tick under it stretches. Reduced motion: hairline still maps to scroll, loops and springs stop.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Tolerance', an interactive reference manual on fit, feel and feedback for people who design physical-digital controls, written by a small design-engineering school. IA native to the genre: Platform (what the manual is), Structure (chapter index as numbered plates: Principles then Prototypes), a preface in two columns, Register (price, what is included), FAQ, Login. No services/work/contact skeleton.
directions.whyWorldClass: It proves a page can have no headline, no image and one type size and still be unmistakable, because the navigation is a measuring instrument and every alignment is exact. It is the clearest current example of scroll-driven CSS producing a signature rather than a trick.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: scroll-timeline-chapter-nav, custom-highlight-reader, manpage, readme-manifesto. Those attach a progress indicator to a conventional long read; here the chrome is the identity (ruler, full-width reading hairline, hanging tag), the page is a sheet on a mat, and there is a single type size. Sibling-lens neighbours tech-craft/artboard-strip-minimap and lab-memo-tick-guides cover the horizontal plate strip and vertical guide lines, not this vertical manual with a reading line.
directions.buildRisk: With one type size and no imagery, any imprecision reads as an unstyled document. Dodge: hard-code the sheet offsets, use text-box trim so the hairline sits on a baseline at scroll=0, and draw at least six genuinely considered SVG plates. The ruler, hairline and tag are fixed, so the thumbnail is safe; make sure the hairline's initial position crosses text rather than whitespace. row-rule is unsupported in the factory Chromium, so draw rules as borders.

directions.name: Word-Tile Corner Morph Headline
directions.signature: Scroll=0: on a cream field, a five-word headline set in a raster grotesk at about 82px is broken into word tiles packed in two centred rows with 6px gaps. Each tile has its own corner geometry (pill, hard rectangle, squircle, scooped, bevelled) and one of three quiet fills (warm grey, lavender, pale pink), and the geometries are visibly mid-exchange: corners morph on a slow rota so no two adjacent tiles ever match. The nav above is the same idea at 12px. Bottom corners hold one line of plain text left and two tiny chips right. On 390px the tiles wrap to four rows and keep their shapes.
directions.grammar: Grid: everything centred on one axis; nav tiles top-centre, logo tile top-left (40px black rounded square), a key hint top-right; 39px side margins. Type: display 82px, tracking about -0.10em, leading 0.9, set tight enough that the tile padding (12px 24px) is the only air; body 18px/27px condensed grotesk; meta 12px mono. Spacing: tiles butt with 6px gaps; one empty band of 100px between headline and footer line; the second section flips to #0d0d0e with a right-aligned 50px raster statement. Colour: #faf6ef ground, #0d0d0e ink, tile fills #ebe7e0, #e9e4f5, #ffd9f7, one #ffe600 chip. Technique: border-radius sets corner size, corner-shape sets geometry (round, squircle, bevel, scoop, notch, superellipse(n)), and because values interpolate through superellipse() the morph is a plain CSS transition. Absent: photography, gradients, shadows, icons, any card.
directions.typeStack: Observed: FK Raster Grotesk (Florian Karsten) for display, Spezia Condensed and Spezia Mono for text. Free stand-ins: Bitcount Prop Single (Google Fonts, variable) or Doto for the raster display; Familjen Grotesk or Schibsted Grotesk for body; DM Mono or Geist Mono for meta.
directions.motion: Entrance: tiles drop in reading order, delay = sibling-index() * 60ms, each scaling 0.8 to 1 with a linear() spring (bounce 0.25, 500ms) via @starting-style; the row beneath compresses 2 percent as each tile lands. Idle: every 2.4s one tile exchanges corner geometry with a neighbour (corner-shape transition 320ms ease-in-out), so the headline is never static but never busy. Hover: the tile under the pointer snaps to the opposite geometry in 180ms and its neighbours nudge 4px away with a 3-tile falloff; press scales 0.97. The greeting chip swaps words every 2s with a 200ms vertical slide. Scroll: tiles drift apart on different view() ranges and the dark section wipes up under them. Signature moment: a pill squaring off while its neighbour rounds, like tokens being re-cut. Reduced motion: static mixed geometries, no rota.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Pocket Mfg.', a two-person studio that designs and manufactures small desk toys and limited hardware. IA: hero statement tiles; Services as three tile rows; Work as a stack of large tiles each naming one release with year and edition size; Store drop with a countdown chip; Connect as two chips (greeting, email). Tone playful but exact.
directions.whyWorldClass: It makes typography physical with no 3D and no images: the words are objects, and the newest layout primitive (corner geometry as an animatable value) is the entire art direction. The raster face plus pastel tiles is current without being nostalgic.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: soft-brutalism, claymorphism, inflatable-balloon-type-hero, memphis-neo-postmodern. None treats each word as a tile with its own corner geometry, and no library template uses corner-shape at all. The ToyFight exemplar adds a 3D handheld; I recommend omitting it (tech-craft/seamless-stage-live-handheld already owns that object) and letting the tiles carry the page.
directions.buildRisk: Slides into childish if the palette or bounce is overdone. Dodge: three muted fills only, one spring, tracking held tight, and a severe black second section. corner-shape is verified supported in the factory Chromium 148; add @supports fallback to plain border-radius values so Safari and Firefox still show pills versus rectangles. Check the raster font at 390px: Bitcount needs about 44px minimum to keep its pixel character.

directions.name: Live Detail Cabinet
directions.signature: Scroll=0: warm paper page. Left rail: a small round mark top-left, three plain words at 24px vertically centred, a two-sentence description and one outlined pill at the bottom. The remaining width is a 3-column masonry of specimen cards, and every stage is LIVE: a ghost arrow cursor holds a button whose fill sweeps and springs back, a tab's inverted corner follows the active tab, a tooltip flips sides as its anchor moves, a number rolls, a list cascades. Stages alternate white and near-black; below each, a grey category word, a 20px title and one sentence. On 390px the rail collapses to a top row and cards go single column with the first two stages visible.
directions.grammar: Grid: rail 312px; three columns of 345px with 24px gaps starting at x=337; cards have 1px #ebe7df borders and 20px radius (squircle via corner-shape), stages 230 to 330px tall, text block padded 24px. Type: one family; rail words 24px/500, titles 20px/500, body 16px/24px #6b6b6b, category 16px #9a9a9a; filter pills 14px in 36px-tall outlined capsules. Colour: #faf8f4 ground, #1a1a1a ink, #111 dark stages, a single signal colour used inside demos only (green caret, blue selection). Each specimen is built on a 2025-2026 primitive so the cabinet doubles as proof: corner-shape scoop for the tab-to-panel join; @starting-style plus interpolate-size for an auto-height disclosure; anchor positioning with position-try for the flipping tooltip; @property number ticker; scroll-state(stuck) mini header; sibling-index() cascade; linear() spring on hold-to-confirm; Web Audio tick on a toggle (muted by default). Absent: hero headline, illustration, gradients, icons beyond the cursor.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Geist with Geist Mono (Detail), Inter (animations.dev). Free stand-ins: Geist and Geist Mono are free (Google Fonts); Inter Tight is the alternative.
directions.motion: Cards enter with an 8px rise and fade over 350ms ease-out, delay sibling-index() * 40ms capped at 400ms. Each specimen loops on a 4 to 6s cycle acted by a ghost cursor (SVG arrow easing between targets with cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), 600ms moves, 120ms press), with phases offset so the grid never pulses in unison; on real pointer enter the ghost fades in 150ms and the demo becomes directly operable. Filter pills reflow the masonry through an element-scoped view transition (each card has a view-transition-name; 300ms, outgoing cards fade in 150ms). On scroll the round logo morphs into a labelled pill and a progressive blur fades in behind the filter row (scroll-state query). Signature moment: nine small interfaces quietly demonstrating themselves at once. Reduced motion: specimens rest in their most legible mid-state and respond only to direct input.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Fettle', a public catalogue of interface details kept by an independent design engineer. IA: filter pills (Design, Interactivity, Motion, Copy, Accessibility, Easter egg), the masonry of entries, Resources (reading list), About. Entry titles are concrete: Hold to confirm, The corner that follows the tab, Tooltip that knows its side, Count that rolls, Header that tucks away.
directions.whyWorldClass: The content is the craft: instead of describing quality it runs it, in miniature, nine times above the fold, on a page calm enough that nothing competes. It is the design-engineer genre at its current best and it teaches the 2026 platform by using it.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: bento, cmd-k-portfolio, starting-style-burst, has-relational-reveal, popover-invoker-glossary. Those are each one platform feature inflated into a page; this is a curated cabinet of many small working details with a paper-and-rail grammar. Sibling lens tech-craft/inspector-annotated-hero annotates one hero like a design tool; this has no hero.
directions.buildRisk: If the demos are static pictures it is just a card grid, which the factory bans. Dodge: commit to nine real specimens and polish six; give each loop a deterministic first frame that already shows a distinct mid-state so the scroll=0 thumbnail reads as alive; keep stages visually varied (light and dark, wide and tall). Budget: this is the most JS-and-CSS-dense direction here, but all of it is capture-safe.

directions.name: Stipple-Edge Two-Tone Field
directions.signature: Scroll=0: the viewport is one flat saturated colour carrying a full-bleed 1-bit composition in a single pale tone: a letter-scale form cropped by the top and left edges whose outline breaks into airbrushed stipple, two swarms of overlapping ellipses that thin out toward the edges, one crisp polygon. Dead centre sits a hard black rectangle (no radius) holding a short paragraph and two giant uppercase link rows with arrows, ruled by hairlines, dates right-aligned in small caps. Top-left: an irregular hand-cut wordmark and a two-line caps tagline. On 390px the black panel goes edge to edge and the forms recrop around it.
directions.grammar: Grid: none for the art (it is a poster); the panel is 840px wide, 24px inner padding, rows 77px tall with 1px #333 rules. Type: paragraph 22px/31px; link rows 36px uppercase with -0.02em tracking; meta 14px uppercase, second line in 60 percent grey; tagline 14px/17px uppercase. Colour: exactly two tones in the art plus black and the pale tone for UI: field oklch(0.76 0.21 152) with an sRGB fallback near #23cc70, forms #e2e2e2, panel #000. Technique: Canvas2D pipeline: draw soft blurred silhouettes to an offscreen canvas, threshold against blue-noise so edges become stipple while interiors stay solid, then stamp ellipse clusters along seeded paths; output is strictly 1-bit and tinted by CSS, so palette changes are free. An SVG feTurbulence plus feComponentTransfer discrete chain gives the same edge with zero JS as a fallback. Absent: gradients, photos, shadows, rounded corners, a third colour.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Figma Sans (a Whyte-like grotesk) and a bespoke blob wordmark. Free stand-ins: Hanken Grotesk or Schibsted Grotesk for text; for the wordmark draw five custom SVG glyphs (cross, flower, stepped N, stacked ovals, spiral) rather than reaching for a font.
directions.motion: The stipple edge crawls: the noise offset advances at a stepped 12fps so it reads as print grain rather than video. Entrance: the field is flat colour, then forms develop by lowering the threshold over 900ms with steps(8); the black panel cuts in with no easing (it is a hard object) 200ms later, rows drawing their hairlines left to right at 60ms stagger. Pointer: the cursor acts as an airbrush that locally raises stipple density with a 300ms decay. Row hover: full-row inversion in 120ms, arrow travels 8px. Scroll: ellipse swarms extend outward in scroll-linked ranges; at each section boundary the two tones swap in one steps(6) wipe through a view transition. Signature moment: the image developing out of flat colour. Reduced motion: static composition at final threshold, no crawl, no airbrush.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Assembly 27', an annual design-and-tools conference with a city edition and a satellite edition. IA: edition picker panel (two rows), dates and place, speakers as a ruled name list, schedule as a three-day table, venue, tickets. One two-tone palette per edition.
directions.whyWorldClass: An entire event identity from two flat colours and one edge treatment, with the generative art behaving like print (cropped, 1-bit, grain-stepped) and the UI behaving like a brutally plain object on top. Confident, cheap to load, unmistakable at thumbnail size.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: dithered-lo-fi, generative-svg-filter, feturbulence-organic-hero, festival-lineup-poster, risograph-print-emulation. Those dither an image or texture a background; this is a composed two-tone poster of macro silhouettes with stipple only at the edges, plus ellipse swarms and a black slab UI. Sibling lens award-studios-now/hairline-cell-ledger-dither confines Bayer dither to table cells; this is free-form and full-bleed.
directions.buildRisk: Random blobs read as noise. Dodge: design three or four deliberate large silhouettes cropped by the frame, fix the seed, and keep interiors solid so only edges stipple. Render the canvas at device pixels with image-rendering: pixelated so the 1-bit edge stays crisp at DPR 1 (the thumbnail scale). Draw the final state synchronously before first paint so the capture never shows flat colour.

directions.name: Smear Portrait with Registration-Mark Chrome

exemplars.site: Breaking the Frame: real-time datamosh with Three.js (Codrops, 2 Sep 2026)

directions.signature: Scroll=0: a full-bleed, heavily grained monochrome field with a soft spotlight behind a centred head-and-shoulders silhouette; where the face should be, columns of pixels are dragged downward in one colour (oxblood red), like a wet print pulled off the plate. Over it: a small white emblem top-left, three tight columns of underlined links each headed by a geometric glyph, a bordered live clock chip, and near the bottom a three-line statement at 30px framed by four small square registration marks, with the year range below. A black button with four rivet dots sits bottom-left. On 390px the nav collapses to emblem, clock and one word; statement and marks stay.
directions.grammar: Grid: 18px outer margin; nav columns at x=260, 490, 720; statement block 460px wide centred; marks are 8px squares at the block corners, 4px hollow dots inside button corners. Type: body 12px/15.6px at -0.04em; links 15px underlined (1px, 3px offset); statement 30px/31px at -0.04em, centred; captions 18px/22px; one serif word spliced into a sans sentence. Light section: ground #e0dedd, images in a 1:1:2 row with 2px gaps and no radius, captions directly beneath in two lines. Colour: #000 to #9a9a9a spotlight, one red #b3202a in the smear, dock tiles #8a1820, ink #000 on #e0dedd. Chrome: a persistent bottom-centre dock of three 40px tiles (emblem, Directory with a two-line glyph, Sound with level bars). Technique: Canvas2D column smear (for each x, copy a source strip and stretch it downward by a noise-driven length) or a small fragment shader; SVG feTurbulence grain overlay; Web Audio for hover ticks routed through one GainNode behind the Sound tile. Absent: colour beyond the one red, rounded cards, big headline, icons.
directions.typeStack: Observed: ReplicaLL (Lineto) for display lines, Reckless Neue (Displaay) for the serif splice, Suisse Intl Book for text. Free stand-ins: Hanken Grotesk or Familjen Grotesk for Replica, Fontshare Switzer for Suisse, Newsreader or Fontshare Gambetta for Reckless.
directions.motion: Entrance: grain first, silhouette fades up from black over 900ms, then the smear grows downward column by column over 1.4s ease-out; the four registration squares start at the block centre and travel to their corners in 500ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) as the statement lines mask-rise. Idle: smear lengths breathe slowly (8s) and respond to pointer velocity with 400ms decay. Scroll: hero dims, the ground flips to light grey in one cut, the dock persists; images scale 1.08 to 1 inside fixed frames on view(). Hover: underline redraws left to right in 250ms, each with a soft tick if sound is on; dock tiles press to 0.97; the Sound tile's bars animate only when enabled. Directory opens as a same-document view transition from the dock tile (300ms). Signature moment: the face smearing as the page loads. Reduced motion: static smear, no pointer response, instant section cuts.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: an independent art director and colourist with a one-person practice. IA in the exemplar's three-column register: Repertoire (Works, Insights), Narrative (About, Brand story, Connect), Liaison (For brands, For agencies); a referral coupon graphic with a rip line and barcode; a pager (1/3) for audience-specific pitches.
directions.photoBrief: One hero portrait: head and shoulders, backlit against a soft grey spotlight so the face falls into near-silhouette, centred, shot or graded to monochrome with heavy grain; subject in a plain dark tee. Three work images for the 1:1:2 row in a shared black, red and cream palette (a glossy object on a red ground, a tight beauty crop, a product still life). If no portrait is sourced, a procedural bust silhouette (radial gradients plus blur) carries the smear acceptably.
directions.whyWorldClass: A portfolio that withholds the face and makes the withholding the brand, then backs it with a complete chrome system (glyph-headed nav, registration marks, riveted buttons, docked controls, sound). It won attention in 2026 for presence and restraint rather than volume of effects.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: glitch-datamosh, mono-ink-restraint, spotlight-noir, slit-scan-temporal. glitch-datamosh is an interaction effect on media; here the smear is a still, art-directed identity mark, and the distinct contribution is the registration-mark chrome and the persistent dock with sound, in a grey-and-oxblood palette.
directions.buildRisk: Without a strong portrait the hero is a red smudge. Dodge: source one backlit portrait or build the procedural bust carefully; draw the final smear synchronously on load so scroll=0 never captures the pre-smear frame. Keep the red to the smear and the dock only. Canvas2D is sufficient and keeps it capture-safe; do not reach for WebGL here.

directions.name: Wide-Gamut Strand Ribbon with Featherweight Display
directions.signature: Scroll=0: a pale warm-grey page. Top-left, a two-line headline at 100px in a featherweight grotesk (weight 250, tracking -0.04em, leading 0.85) in deep aubergine, hard against a 16px margin; date and venue as two small text columns far right. Below, one full-width rounded panel (24px radius, slightly darker grey) contains a twisted ribbon made of thousands of hair-fine strands whose hue runs red to orange to magenta to violet to blue along its length, the strands fanning out and fading to transparency at one end so the form feels combed, not solid. Nothing else. On 390px the headline drops to 44px on three lines and the ribbon panel becomes a 4:5 crop of the densest crossing.
directions.grammar: Grid: 16px outer margin; 12 columns; the agenda and speaker blocks start at column 5 (x=485) leaving the left third for giant labels. Type: display 100px/85px weight 250; section labels 56px weight 250; day names 24px; body 16px/24px weight 400; all in one variable family; text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic on the display so it sits exactly on the margin and the panel top. Spacing: 32px between headline and panel; 170px between sections; hairline rules #d9d5d5. Colour: #f9f7f7 ground, #20033c ink and pill button, panel #e6e2e1, strands in display-p3 via oklch with chroma above sRGB (for example oklch(0.65 0.29 25) to oklch(0.55 0.28 285)) behind @media (color-gamut: p3) with sRGB fallbacks; optional dynamic-range-limit: constrained on the panel for HDR screens. Technique: Canvas2D with colorSpace display-p3: 2000 to 3000 polylines sampled along a parametric twisted band, per-strand hue from length position, alpha tapering by strand index, multiply blend on the light panel. Small components: flag chips (coloured flag glyph plus label in a 1px border, 4px radius), 2px-gap logo tiles. Absent: icons, gradients in CSS, shadows, any second typeface.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Sohne variable (Klim) at weights 250 to 400. Free stand-ins: Geist at weight 200 to 300 with -0.04em tracking, or Fontshare Switzer Light; Inter Tight ExtraLight as a third option.
directions.motion: Entrance: headline lines rise 24px with fade over 700ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), 80ms apart; the ribbon then draws along its length over 1.6s ease-out, strands starting a few milliseconds apart by index so it reads as a single combed sweep. Idle: the band twists with a 40s period; pointer proximity parts nearby strands by a few pixels with 500ms recovery. Scroll: the top nav is plain text until stuck, then becomes an inset rounded bar with backdrop blur through a scroll-state(stuck) container query (200ms); agenda rows reveal once with their hairlines drawing left to right in 500ms; flag chips pop with a tiny spring. Hover: the pill button lightens in 120ms; tiles lift nothing, they only swap tone. Signature moment: the ribbon combing itself into existence. Reduced motion: ribbon drawn complete and still; reveals become instant.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Meridian 27', a three-day conference on the ocean economy. IA: hero with date and venue; keynote film with name caption; Agenda at a glance (three days, flag chips); Speakers as a tile wall of organisation wordmarks plus past-talk rows with a Watch now link; Venue; FAQs; Register.
directions.whyWorldClass: The whole brand is two decisions held with total discipline: type so light and so tightly tracked it feels engraved, and one generative form with colour beyond sRGB. It is the best current example of wide-gamut colour used as luxury rather than loudness, on a light ground.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: procedural-bezier-ribbon, elastic-ribbon, property-gradient-brand, conference-schedule-grid. Library ribbons are thick bands on dark grounds built as mechanics; this is thousands of hair-fine P3 strands on pale grey, paired with a featherweight 100px display and a ruled three-column agenda, and it is the first direction to use wide-gamut canvas and scroll-state nav.
directions.buildRisk: A sparse or thick-lined ribbon looks like a 2019 gradient blob. Dodge: at least 2000 strands at 0.6 to 1px with alpha taper, drawn once to an offscreen canvas and then animated cheaply (transform or redraw at 30fps); paint the completed ribbon synchronously for the thumbnail. Headless screenshots are sRGB, so choose fallbacks that still look rich. Weight 250 needs a true variable font: Geist goes to 100, so it holds.

directions.name: Flat-Lay Measured Desk Object Launch

exemplars.site: IVRESS brand site (Utsubo, FWA SOTM May 2026)

directions.signature: Scroll=0: the camera looks straight down at a maker's desk. A gridded cutting mat with printed numerals fills most of the frame, rotated a few degrees; one humble object sits at its centre casting a soft contact shadow; three or four tools (pencil, blade, clip) enter from the edges out of focus. A cream bold-caps wordmark about 190px tall overlaps the top-left of the mat with a small caps strapline above it; a bold 24px sentence sits right of the object; a frosted card bottom-left credits the maker with a dotted rule and a deadpan line. On 390px the object centres under the wordmark and one prop remains.
directions.grammar: Grid: DOM text on a 12-column overlay with 45px margins; wordmark spans columns 1 to 6; paragraph columns 9 to 12. Type: wordmark 190px weight 700 geometric caps, tracking -0.02em; chapter lines 48px caps; paragraph 24px/36px weight 600; micro labels 13.5px caps weight 500; mono 12px for HUD chips; one serif for long quotes. Colour: warm scene (wood #b98a5a, mat #3f6b45, cork #c9793a), text #ffedd7; chapters cut to #100904 void. Chrome: text nav top-right with a dotted underline on the active item, vertical tab on the right edge, round SCROLL TO CONTINUE cue. Technique: three.js scene with a procedural mat (grid and numerals in a shader or canvas texture), noise-bumped cork, soft shadows and depth of field; the exemplar uses WebGPURenderer plus TSL, a build should use WebGLRenderer for capture and keep TSL optional. HUD chips are DOM positioned over the canvas. Absent: gradients, particles, UI cards beyond the one frosted credit.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Halyard Display variable (Adobe) for all caps and paragraphs, Literata for serif, DM Mono for chips. Free stand-ins: Outfit 600 to 700 or Fontshare General Sans Bold for Halyard; Literata and DM Mono are free on Google Fonts.
directions.motion: Entrance: the camera settles about 6 percent closer over 1.2s with an over-damped curve while focus racks from the props to the object; the wordmark rises through a mask. Idle: pointer parallax under 1.5 degrees with lerp 0.08; the object can be nudged and slides back. Scroll (scrubbed): the scene darkens to the void as the object lifts off the mat and rotates about 70 degrees onto its edge; chapter text swaps left and right with 20px mask slides; a macro chapter desaturates the material and a HUD chip counts a mock measurement while the user drags. Signature moment: top-down flat-lay to edge-on hero lift. Reduced motion: a static top-down render with chapters as plain stacked sections.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'LODE-1', a solid brass paperweight launched with flagship-phone gravity by a prop-making studio. IA of the mock keynote genre: Intro (the flat-lay), Features (three deadpan chapters, each with one HUD metric), Product (spec table: mass, alloy, tolerances), Contact or pre-order with an edition count.
directions.whyWorldClass: It spends frontier rendering on the least important object imaginable and treats it with total seriousness: the craft is in light, material and comic timing, and the opening composition is a photograph-quality still life before any motion happens. It was the reference 3D site of spring 2026.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: satirical-product-void, supplement-3d-product-stage, luxury-watch-callouts, configurator-hero. Those stage an object in a void or studio; the distinct move here is the overhead flat-lay on a measured mat with props as the scroll=0 composition, then the lift. Sibling lens award-studios-now/occluded-split-type-object takes a different composition from the same exemplar (split giant type occluded by the object on fog grey), so the two do not collide.
directions.buildRisk: This lives or dies on material and light: flat-shaded primitives will look like a 2018 demo. Dodge: bake the mat and wood as canvas textures, add contact shadow and a little depth of field, keep the object simple (a lathe-turned disc). navigator.gpu is absent in the factory's headless Chromium, so do not depend on WebGPU; ship a CSS and SVG flat-lay poster (gradients plus feTurbulence grain) as first paint and as the reduced-motion and no-GL fallback so the scroll=0 thumbnail is never blank.

directions.name: Glyph Vector Field with Slab Chrome
directions.signature: Scroll=0: the hero is a wall of saturated colour (a slow mesh moving from signal yellow through pink and violet to blue and orange-red) covered edge to edge by a regular grid of small white typographic marks, each chosen and rotated to show the local direction of an invisible flow, so the field reads like wind on a weather map. A solid black rectangle overlaps the top-left third and holds a version crumb, a three-line bold headline with its first word in yellow, two hard-edged buttons and a row of outlined platform chips. A thick yellow bar inset from the edges is the nav. A ruled strip of four labelled columns closes the fold. On 390px the slab goes full width over the top half and the field shows beneath.
directions.grammar: Grid: 72px content margins; nav bar inset 42px, 72px tall; slab 520x510 with 48px padding; below the fold a 4-column hairline cell grid (1px rgba white 12 percent rules), cells 324px wide with a 200px demo stage, a two-digit index, an 20px title with an arrow, two lines of 13px copy and a mono code crumb. Type: headline 42px/44px weight 700 at -0.04em; UI labels mono 12px uppercase with 0.12em tracking; body 13 to 16px. Colour: #0e1312 ground, #fcd60d signal yellow, ink #ededec, field colours specified in oklch and animated through registered @property stops so interpolation stays clean. Technique: the mesh is pure CSS (stacked radial gradients on @property-animated positions); the glyphs are a Canvas2D grid sampling a curl-noise field and choosing among six characters by angle, drawn in white with a light difference blend. Hatched borders on version numerals via repeating-linear-gradient. Absent: rounded corners (everything is square), photography, shadows, icons other than arrows.
