directions.typeStack: Observed: TASA Orbiter (display and text) with Geist Mono. Free stand-ins: TASA Orbiter is itself open source (Google Fonts as TASA Orbiter); otherwise Bricolage Grotesque Bold or Familjen Grotesk; Geist Mono for labels.
directions.motion: Idle: the flow field advects slowly (one full drift in about 25s) and glyphs re-pick their character with a stepped update at roughly 10fps so the texture ticks like a split-flap rather than flowing like video; the mesh beneath drifts on a 30s loop. Pointer: a 160px radius bends the field toward the cursor with 600ms relaxation. Entrance: slab cuts in first with no fade, headline lines rise 16px at 60ms stagger, glyphs populate in a diagonal wave over 700ms. Scroll: feature cells reveal with sibling-index() * 40ms and the active cell floods yellow in 150ms; changelog numerals count up once. Hover: buttons invert instantly, arrow glyphs step 6px. Signature moment: the pointer combing the glyph field. Reduced motion: static field and mesh, instant reveals.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Gust', an open-source wind and weather simulation library for the browser. IA of the developer-tool genre: hero slab with install line and version; a ruled strip of platforms; numbered capability cells each with a live micro demo and a code crumb; examples gallery; changelog with hatched version numerals and Added, Changed, Fixed lists; latest articles.
directions.whyWorldClass: It gives a developer product a real graphic identity: typographic marks behaving as data over uncompromising colour, with brutally square chrome. It is loud and still precise, which is rare, and the field is cheap, deterministic and legible at thumbnail size.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: ascii-rasterizer, flow-field-still-portrait, property-gradient-brand, devtools-live-code-hero. The library pieces are single mechanics on dark grounds; this combines a direction-encoding glyph field over a wide-gamut mesh with a slab-and-bar chrome system and a ruled, numbered cell grid as a full page grammar.
directions.buildRisk: Colour can go garish and the glyphs can turn to noise. Dodge: limit the mesh to five hues with yellow dominant near the slab, keep glyph size at 12 to 14px on a 16px grid with one weight, and pre-compute the first frame so the capture is populated. Keep every corner square; one rounded element breaks the system.

directions.name: Fit-Width Headline with Anchored Chip Actors

exemplars.site: Getting Started with Anchor Positioning (Josh W. Comeau)

directions.signature: Scroll=0: a single-line headline is fitted exactly to the viewport width (three words and one inline glyph at about 109px, tracking -0.04em), sitting in the lower part of a pale tinted band about 320px tall. Three small highlighter chips (pink, yellow, red) are stacked on a diagonal above the final word, visibly tethered to it. A plain text header runs across the top in four positions (wordmark, two-line descriptor, comma-separated nav, underlined contact). The rest of the fold is a full-bleed contact sheet: a grid of frames with black gutters and tiny red timecodes. On 390px the headline wraps to three fitted lines and the chips hang off the last one.
directions.grammar: Grid: 16px margins; header items at columns 1, 4, 7 and 12; the contact sheet is 4 by 3 frames at 3:2 with 20px black gutters. Type: headline about 7.6vw weight 400 at -0.04em, leading 0.79; header 14px/20px with a bold first line; chips 14px on 4px-padded rectangles with no radius; statement sections 36px/43px centred at 590px measure with a ghost line of 200px type at 4 percent contrast behind. Colour: #f8f8f8 ground with a #fdeef0 wash, ink #232323, chips #f39ac1, #f5d04a, #ef3b2d; sheet gutters #0a0a0a. Technique: the headline is fitted with container query units (font-size in cqw from a measured ratio, because text-fit is not yet supported in the factory Chromium); each chip is anchor-positioned to a word span (anchor-name on the word, position-area on the chip) so they follow reflow at any width; as sections change, chips re-target new anchors and travel there. Absent: cards, icons, rounded corners, shadows.
directions.typeStack: Observed: TWK Lausanne 400 and 700. Free stand-ins: Inter Tight 400 and 700, Fontshare Switzer, or Hanken Grotesk.
directions.motion: Entrance: the headline words slide up through a line mask at 70ms stagger (600ms, cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1)), the inline glyph spins one turn, then the three chips drop onto their anchor one by one with a small spring (bounce 0.2, 350ms). Scroll: the chips are the page's recurring actors. They detach from the headline and drift down with slight lag into the next section, where each re-anchors to a new word (city names, then service names); implemented as position-anchor changes inside a view transition or a scroll-linked interpolation between two anchor rects. The contact sheet frames play short loops with offset starts and scrub slightly with scroll; the ghost line translates horizontally at 0.3x. Hover on a frame: timecode runs. Signature moment: three chips leaving a headline and landing as labels somewhere else. Reduced motion: chips appear in place at each anchor, no travel.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Second Unit', a small film and content production company with two bases. IA: fitted headline with chips (what, type of company, year); contact sheet of work as frames; a centred recognition statement with city chips; services list where the chips land as category labels; selected films table; contact line. The contact sheet can be CSS-drawn frames with gradient stills if footage is not available.
directions.photoBrief: A contact sheet of 12 frames, 3:2, from a shared event or shoot: stage lighting, backs of heads, screens, hands, warm tungsten and one saturated colour per frame; slightly soft, handheld, like frames pulled from phone video. Short loops preferred, stills acceptable. If unavailable, generate procedural frames (blurred gradient shapes with grain and timecodes) and declare the direction graphic-procedural.
directions.whyWorldClass: Width-fitted type is common; making small anchored labels into travelling characters that tie the sections together is not, and it turns anchor positioning from a tooltip utility into choreography. The top-of-page economy (one line, three chips, one sheet) is exactly the 2026 award register.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: anchor-annotated-index, kinetic-broken-grid, film-strip. anchor-annotated-index pins static notes to a list; here anchored chips are persistent actors that migrate between anchors across sections, on a fitted single-line headline over a contact sheet. Sibling lens award-studios-now/contact-sheet-one-size uses contact-sheet density with one type size and no chips.
directions.buildRisk: The fit must be exact at every width or the headline looks accidental. Dodge: compute the cqw ratio from the chosen font and words, and verify at 1440 and 390; do not rely on text-fit (unsupported in Chromium 148). Chip travel between anchors is the hard part: start with a scroll-linked interpolation between two measured rects in JS and keep anchor positioning for the resting states. Without footage the contact sheet must be convincingly procedural.

directions.name: Axonometric Colour-Font Word
directions.signature: Scroll=0: one saturated flat field crossed by hair-thin isometric construction lines. A single word about 18vw tall stands in an extruded axonometric colour font: selectable live text whose faces, sides and highlights are separate gradient layers inside the font, recoloured to a restrained two-hue palette (bone faces, graphite sides on ultramarine, or terracotta on cream). Its extrusion depth is caught mid-growth, deeper on the left letters than the right. Under it, a heavy 48px line and a 24px byline in a plain grotesk, left aligned to the word. On 390px the word breaks into two stacked rows.
directions.grammar: Grid: 128px left margin for word and titles; body in a two-column 144 / 732 split on a #f1f1f1 ground below the field. Type: the colour word at 18vw; title 48px weight 800 to 900; byline 24px; body 20px/27px; small bold side heads. Colour: one field per section (ultramarine, then pale grey, then a second field) with the font palette redefined per section through @font-palette-values (override-colors) and blended between sections with font-palette: palette-mix(in oklch, ...). Construction lines are inline SVG at 20 percent lighter than the field. Technique: a COLRv1 variable colour font (Nabla on Google Fonts, axes EDPT extrusion depth 0 to 200 and EHLT highlight 0 to 24) animated with font-variation-settings; no canvas, no WebGL, no filters. Absent: images, shadows, any 3D engine.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Nabla (Typearture and Just van Rossum, free on Google Fonts) with Degular (Adobe) for text. Free stand-ins: Nabla itself; Bricolage Grotesque ExtraBold or Fontshare Cabinet Grotesk for Degular. Alternates in the same technique: Honk, Bungee Spice, Kalnia Glaze, Bitcount ink styles.
directions.motion: Entrance: letters start flat (EDPT 0) and extrude left to right, delay sibling-index() * 90ms, 800ms each with a gentle linear() spring; the highlight axis sweeps 0 to 24 and settles at 10; construction lines draw outward from the word by stroke-dashoffset over 900ms. Scroll (scrubbed): depth eases from 160 down to 30 as the hero leaves, and the palette cross-blends into the next section's palette through palette-mix. Hover: the letter under the pointer pops to depth 200 in 300ms and relaxes. Signature moment: flat lettering growing into solid blocks. Reduced motion: static at depth 100, palette changes by cut.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Axon', an architectural model-making workshop. IA: the word; three practices each with its own palette field (competition models, exhibition models, restoration); process plates drawn as dashed-guide diagrams; a colophon naming the typeface and palettes.
directions.whyWorldClass: Dimensional, coloured, animated lettering with zero images or WebGL, still selectable and accessible, at a few hundred kilobytes: a capability almost nobody is using in production yet. I rate it lower than the others because my exemplars are specimen sites from the font's makers rather than 2026 client work, so the taste case is unproven.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: inflatable-balloon-type-hero, chrome-mercury-letterpress, variable-font-axis-playground, isometric-atelier-plan, spatial-perspective-type-wall. Those fake dimension with filters, shadows or 3D transforms; here depth and colour live in the font file (COLRv1 gradients, a depth axis, palette overrides and palette-mix), which no library template uses.
directions.buildRisk: Default Nabla colours read as an arcade cabinet. Dodge: always override the palette to two restrained hues and keep everything else severe. Await document.fonts.ready before first paint so the capture never shows fallback text; font-palette and palette-mix are verified supported in the factory Chromium 148, Safari support for COLRv1 variable palettes is weaker, so provide a flat single-colour fallback via @supports not (font-palette: ...). Only one style exists, so the word must be short and the rest of the page must not lean on it.

directions.name: Technical-plate specimen with ruler scrubber
directions.signature: At scroll=0 a four-letter abbreviation of the product name set at about 43vw (619px at 1440, weight 800, tracking -0.05em, leading 0.75) in one spot ink (#FF4CB2) on warm white #F8F8F6, with a tiny diamond monogram overlapping its lower-left stem. Directly beneath, still inside the first viewport, a row of three hairline-bordered plates: a mint (#CCE3D9) plate with a cone-and-spheres diagram labelled MONO / SEMI / POLY, an outlined lowercase glyph plate with a corner tag, and a stepped pink-outlined plate of acid-yellow (#E7F80A) discs each holding one letter. On a 390px phone the abbreviation breaks into two rows of two letters and the plates stack full width.
directions.grammar: 40px outer margins; a 12-column base expressed as plates of unequal width with 10px gutters. Every plate has a 1px stroke in dark green or pink, square corners with an occasional 40px-radius plate. Flat fills only: mint #CCE3D9, pale-pink graph paper #FFE8F8 with an olive 1px grid at about 40px pitch, cornflower #6A96ED, acid yellow #E7F80A, olive #838C19 for giant glyphs; no black text anywhere. Labels are mono caps 14-16px, tracking 0.05em, in olive, green or pink. Display glyphs run 400-600px inside plates and are cropped by the plate edge. Diagram vocabulary: concentric-ring target (weights T L R M B H BL on the rings), gauges, segmented progress bars, crosshair circles, a dial. Overprint: 600px pink numerals pass over blue plates with multiply blending while staircase readouts repeat down the page. Fixed bottom bar 60px tall, bordered, with a pink disc dial at left, a tick-mark ruler carrying section names plus numeric stations, and three outlined pills at right. Absent: photography, shadows, gradients, body copy longer than five lines.
directions.typeStack: Observed: GT Mechanik VF only (display 619px/800, body 16/24, all labels). Free stand-ins: Recursive (Google Fonts; real MONO axis 0-1 plus wght 300-1000, so the mono/semi/poly idea can be rebuilt literally) for labels, specimens and body; Martian Mono (Google; wdth 75-112.5, wght 100-800) at condensed ExtraBold for the giant abbreviation if Recursive at 1000 reads too soft.
directions.motion: Entrance: plate strokes draw in sequence (stroke-dashoffset, 60ms stagger), the abbreviation arrives letter by letter with steps() timing, labels type on. Scroll: the ruler needle tracks document progress and the station number counts; plates drift at two parallax rates; staircase readouts ('97.7 - POLY') print one character per step. Micro: hovering a plate swaps its ink pair; the weight list (LIGHT to BLACK) highlights the current weight in pink while the matching target ring thickens; dial rotates with pointer X. Signature moment: the overprint collision, a 600px pink section numeral sliding across a cornflower glyph plate with mix-blend-mode multiply while the readout cascade runs. Reduced motion: all plates drawn, needle jumps per section.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Kessel', a mono-to-proportional type family, or abstracted to any precision product (a modular synth, a measuring instrument, a mechanical keyboard). IA: abbreviation hero > concept plate (three modes diagram) > mode 01 / 02 / 03 chapters, each with a giant numeral, a glyph plate and one short paragraph plate > weights target > character-set plate > tester strip > buy bar. The ruler nav stations are the chapters.
directions.whyWorldClass: Every device is derived from the typeface's concept (spacing modes become gauges and cones), each plate is a different small invention yet the stroke weight, ink set and mono labels hold it together, and scroll position is turned into an instrument reading. It is playful and rigorous at once, which is the hardest register to fake.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: spec-sheet-instrument, blueprint-svg, specimen-lab, cloud-devops-blueprint-grid, trace-diagram. Differs: daylight spot-ink palette on warm white instead of dark or monochrome blueprint, plates of mixed scale with overprint collisions, and a scroll-as-ruler fixed nav. None of the listed slugs combines candy colour with technical drawing.
directions.buildRisk: Falls flat if the plates become uniform cards or the diagrams are generic icons. Needs 10+ genuinely different inline-SVG diagrams, strict 1px strokes at DPR 1 (vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke) and no black. Multiply blending over several large layers can cost FPS: cap at two or three blended layers. Recursive's heaviest weight is softer than the original, so test Martian Mono for the hero. Make the drawn final state the default so the scroll=0 thumbnail never catches a half-drawn frame.

directions.name: Index-tab navigation over flat colour slabs

exemplars.site: Exat by Hot Type (microsite by Studio Size, 2026)

directions.signature: A 40px light-grey (#E8E8E8) strip across the top holds file-folder tabs: one active tab at left in the section colour (#FE3500), visually fused to the slab below it, and two grey tabs (try / buy) at right. Below, a full-bleed #FE3500 slab carries the lowercase product name at 200px, tracking -0.025em, black, left-aligned on a 40px margin, then a three-column row of circled-numeral headings (1 design, 2 system, 3 platform), each above a 380px black lowercase 'a': the first with its bezier nodes drawn as ringed dots, the second layered with an offset outlined copy, the third plain. On mobile the three columns stack and the node-handled 'a' fills the width.
directions.grammar: 40px margins; 12 columns; hero three-up at about 460px per column. Everything lowercase. Display 200px/1.0; chapter headings 48px bold with circled numerals; body 18/22 medium in two narrow 330px columns pushed to columns 5-10 with the left third left empty. Each chapter is a full-bleed slab in one flat colour (orange-red #FE3500, black, white) and owns a tab in its own colour (red, black, yellow #F4C70A); tabs are about 113px wide with 6px top radii and 16px labels. Diagram cells use 1px black borders, 9px mono captions and numbered tick units along the base; the weight ladder is rows on hairlines with tiny right-aligned labels; a red dot rides a vertical-line grid as the slider; occasional giant numerals in pure blue and red. Absent: imagery, uppercase, rounded cards, shadows, icons other than circled numerals.
directions.typeStack: Observed: GT Standard, GT Standard Mono, GT Standard Icons (display 200px, tracking -5px; body 16/24). Free stand-ins: Archivo (Google; wdth 62-125 and wght 100-900, which makes the width ruler real) or Inter Tight 700 for display; Geist Mono or JetBrains Mono for 9px captions.
directions.motion: Tabs rise into the strip when a chapter's slab reaches the top and stay there, building an index you can click back through; the active tab takes the chapter colour. Slab changes are hard cuts via sticky stacking (the next slab covers the previous). Micro: node handles on the 'a' are draggable and the outline redraws; hovering a width-ruler cell interpolates that m; dragging the red dot runs the weight ladder. Signature moment: on load the nodes travel from scattered off-curve positions to rest on the outline (600ms, cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1)) while the first tab clicks into place. Reduced motion: tabs appear without travel, nodes static.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Norma', a systematic grotesque, or abstracted to any standard, spec or design-system launch. IA: name slab > about (two offset columns) > 1 design (concept, construction diagrams) > 2 system (width ruler, weight ladder, mono) > 3 platform (variable axes, languages, features) > try (tester) > buy.
directions.whyWorldClass: The navigation metaphor accumulates meaning as you read, the colour discipline is absolute, and every diagram teaches something about the product. It looks like a Swiss manual and behaves like software.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: swiss-international-typographic, swiss-poster, variable-font-axis-playground, scroll-timeline-chapter-nav. Differs: folder-tab chrome that accrues per chapter, lowercase-only voice, one saturated slab per chapter, and glyph-anatomy diagrams with ringed nodes rather than a slider playground or a poster grid.
directions.buildRisk: Fake node handles placed by eye look wrong instantly: hand-author one SVG glyph path and derive node positions from its actual path vertices in JS. Sticky stacking must run on the document root. If the slabs carry too little content the page feels like three posters: each chapter needs two or three real diagrams. The tab strip must be pixel-fused to the slab (no gap, matching colour) or the folder illusion dies.

directions.name: Ruled weight ladder with glyph inspector
directions.signature: One word repeated four times, centred, stepping from 70px Light to about 250px Black down the viewport on a mid-grey #CDCDCD ground in #141414, with three full-width 1px rules at fixed 250px intervals that cut straight through the letters (each row's type is taller than its band, so glyphs overlap the rules). A 60px header row sits above: maker name at left, product name starting exactly at the page centre line, two text links at right. A final ruled band carries a one-line credit starting at the centre line and a small down arrow at the far right. On mobile the two largest rows overflow and crop at both edges, which reads as intentional.
directions.grammar: A strict two-column split at 50% (20px margins; the right column starts at x=726 at 1440) plus full-bleed hairlines; hero bands 250px tall. Header type 24px medium, tracking -0.01em. Section two inverts to #060606 with #CCCCCC text: left column a two-line 24px tagline, right column 24/29 paragraphs with a 48px first-line indent. Media row: two images of unequal width top-aligned to the column edges. Glyph inspector: left half shows one glyph at about 300px across five labelled metric hairlines with 9px labels and values, plus a five-row key/value table at 12px; right half is an 11-column grid of 62px cells with 1px #222 borders and 28px glyphs, closed by a 24px 'See full glyphs' link. The header appends the current section name in grey after the product name. Absent: any colour, filled buttons, icons, cards.
directions.typeStack: Observed: CcTimeline (custom grotesque; display 156px weight 500 tracking -0.02em, leading 0.9; body 24/31). Free stand-ins: Inter (variable wght 100-900) or Hanken Grotesk for the ladder and text; Fontshare Switzer is also close. Use a variable file so the ladder can interpolate.
directions.motion: Entrance: rules draw left to right, then the four rows interpolate from weight 300 to their targets (font-variation-settings, 900ms, 120ms stagger, ease-out). Scroll: rows slide horizontally at different rates (largest moves most) and the theme inverts in a single 200ms step at the section boundary; the header's section label swaps. Micro: hovering a glyph cell swaps the inspected glyph and re-animates the metric lines; pointer X over the hero breathes the weight ladder (left light, right black) while the rules stay fixed. Signature moment: the ladder weight sweep against immovable hairlines. Reduced motion: static ladder, instant theme change.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Meridian Sans' from a new foundry, or abstracted to any product sold in tiers or generations. IA: ladder hero > overview (tagline + essay) > image pair > history in three eras (three columns: metal, photo, digital) > weights list > glyph inspector > OpenType features > in use > trials / buy footer.
directions.whyWorldClass: The product idea (a timeline of weights) is the layout, the hero is image-free yet instantly legible as a thumbnail, and the inspector is real working UI rather than decoration. Mid-grey as a ground colour is a quiet, expensive-feeling choice almost nobody else makes.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: specimen-lab, variable-font-pressure, swiss-grid-serif, mono-ink-restraint. Differs: mid-grey ground, a single word as an optical ladder cut by fixed rules, centre-line header alignment and a functional metrics inspector with a bordered glyph grid.
directions.buildRisk: The scroll=0 thumbnail can catch the weight animation mid-flight: make the final ladder the CSS default and only animate after first paint or on pointer. Metric lines must match the real font: compute from canvas TextMetrics (fontBoundingBox / actualBoundingBox) instead of hard-coding. With Inter the hero risks looking like a default: the craft is in exact band heights, rule alignment and the centre-line grid, so measure against the reference.

directions.name: Half-page jumbo navigation with dashed cards
directions.signature: The left half of the viewport is the navigation itself: five words stacked at 164px, medium weight, tracking -0.09em, leading 0.76, black on white, pinned for the whole page. The right half is a column of 6px-radius cards with 1px dashed borders, each opening with a title at the same 164px scale wrapping to two or three lines, followed by 11px monospace body copy with underlined links. A hand-scribbled outline logo sits top-left at about 80px and a ringed two-letter language toggle top-right. On mobile the five nav words fill the first screen at about 19vw and the cards follow.
directions.grammar: Two columns 50/50, 16px margins, 18px between cards, 12px card padding. No rules other than the dashed card borders. Type contrast is roughly 15:1 (164px display against 11/16.7 mono). Pure #000 on #FFF, no greys. Links are underlined mono; the only shapes are a circle button and the scribble logo. Card bodies are short (three paragraphs) and end with two 'see more' links. Absent: images on the home view, colour, icons, headers or footers in the usual sense.
directions.typeStack: Observed: custom display grotesque (tight neo-grotesque, 164px, tracking -14.8px) and custom mono at 11px. Free stand-ins: Inter Tight 500-600 at -0.09em (or Fontshare Switzer Medium) for display; JetBrains Mono or Geist Mono at 11px for text.
directions.motion: Left nav is sticky while the right column scrolls. Micro: hovering a nav word tightens it further and snaps a dashed outline around it; card titles reveal with a per-line clip; underlines draw. Signature moment: as you scroll past the first screen the five stacked words compress in leading and scale (164px to 96px) to make room, then spring back at the top; gallery write-ups also describe live text thumbnails that loop the title on a 3D cylinder on inner pages (not seen in my capture). Reduced motion: nav fixed at one size.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Compagnie Nord', a contemporary dance company, or any cultural institution with a programme. IA: jumbo nav (Programme, Company, Artists, Calendar, Search) > cards: Direction, Company, Associate artist, Residency studio, Touring, Tickets > calendar list in mono at the foot.
directions.whyWorldClass: An institutional homepage with zero imagery that is unmistakable in a thumbnail: the navigation is the poster. Scale contrast and extreme negative tracking do all the work, and the dashed cards give it a provisional, rehearsal-room character.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: kinetic-broken-grid, swiss-poster, festival-lineup-poster, soft-brutalism. Differs: split layout with a sticky jumbo nav as half the page, -0.09em tracking, dashed cards and an 11px mono voice; it is institutional and calm rather than poster-loud.
directions.buildRisk: Inter Tight at -0.09em collides on some letter pairs: tune tracking per word and check accents. Nav words must fit a half-width column at 1440 and at 1280: size with clamp() against the column, not the viewport. If card copy is lorem-grade the page dies: write specific, dated institutional copy. Dashed borders render unevenly across zoom levels: use an SVG dashed rect or background-image dashes for exact rhythm.

directions.name: Image-free episode index with ringed-letter names
directions.signature: A masthead spanning the full width at about 150px: a bold grotesque word, then a solid black disc with a white inner ring standing in for a letter O, then the rest of the title in a wide typewriter slab. Under it a two-line 15px descriptor, then full-bleed hairline-ruled rows 97px tall: an 'EP 02' label in 15px sans at the far left, a 15px serif series line above a 40px serif title (tracking -0.04em) starting at x=122, guest names right-aligned on two lines with every letter set inside its own 20px ring, and the running time at the far right. The final row is greyed out as upcoming. No images anywhere.
directions.grammar: Ground #F1F1F1, ink #000, grey #BDBDBD for the future row. 16px margins. Row columns: 100px label / fluid title / right-aligned ringed names / 80px duration. Rules are 1px black edge to edge. Title serif 40px at leading 0.9; labels 15px sans; the masthead is three typographic voices on one baseline. Mobile recentres every row: label, series line, 40px title on two lines, ringed names, duration, each on its own line with generous 60px row padding. Absent: thumbnails, play buttons at rest, colour, cards, icons.
directions.typeStack: Observed: ABC Diatype (sans labels), HAL Timezone (serif titles, 39.5px, tracking -0.04em) and HAL Timezone Mono (masthead slab). Free stand-ins: Inter or Fontshare Switzer for the sans; Newsreader (opsz) or Fontshare Zodiak for the serif; Cutive Mono or Libertinus Mono for the masthead slab. Build ringed letters as inline-flex spans with a 1px circular border, not Unicode enclosed alphanumerics (accented letters are missing there).
directions.motion: Entrance: rules draw, titles rise 12px out of a clip, rings pop in letter by letter (25ms stagger). Hover on a row: background inverts to black, rings fill and letters knock out, the EP label swaps to a play glyph and the duration starts counting. Click expands the row accordion-style into a two-column transcript excerpt. The masthead disc doubles as a mute toggle and turns like a tape reel while 'playing'. Signature moment: ringed letters flipping in sequence like a split-flap board when a row activates (40ms stagger). Reduced motion: instant inversion, no flips.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Open Mic', a studio's talk series, or any programme list (lecture season, tasting menu, syllabus, release schedule). IA: masthead > descriptor > rows grouped by season or theme > upcoming rows greyed > subscribe row > colophon. Expanded row holds guests, a pull quote and links.
directions.whyWorldClass: A complete, memorable site built from one typographic idea: names set in rings supply the texture other sites buy with photography, and the masthead's three voices give it a brand in a single line. The mobile layout is as considered as the desktop one.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: editorial-index, music-release-hub, conference-schedule-grid, transcript-screenplay. Differs: a three-voice masthead with a disc glyph, ringed-letter name setting as the recurring texture, warm-grey monochrome and an expanding row model rather than a schedule grid.
directions.buildRisk: Reads as a plain table if the serif stand-in is bland or the tracking is left at default: pick a serif with character and set -0.04em. Ringed letters need optical centring (caps only, about 0.62em inside the ring, consistent ring gap). Six rows do not fill a page: design the expanded state and a second season so the scroll has substance.

directions.name: Defocused glyph macro with text-setting waterfall
directions.signature: The first viewport is a 20px frame of saturated orange (#D33C03) around a single image: an extreme, heavily defocused macro of one letterform, off-white on dark green (#193F1A), so blurred it reads as abstract soft shapes (a counter becomes a green almond). The only sharp elements are a 48px nav row of 16px text (maker, section, product at left; a select, a theme toggle, a text link and one red chip at right). On mobile the same frame and blur fill the screen with the nav reduced to maker name and menu.
directions.grammar: After the hero the entire page takes the frame colour with black text. Product name at about 330px bold, cropped beneath the nav. An 'Information' label (20px bold at x=20) with a 23/32 text column at x=255, 680px wide. Then the waterfall: full-width blocks of hyphenated running text in 3, 2, 3 columns at 15-22px with tight leading, each introduced by a five-value spec row (style name, weight, columns, size, tracking) in 16px regular spread across the grid. Nav items gain black tick separators over colour. 20px margins throughout. Absent: images after the hero, cards, rules, more than two colours per theme.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Soehne for UI (16/24) and Die Grotesk VF for specimens. Free stand-ins: Hanken Grotesk or Geist for UI; Inter Tight (variable 100-900) or Fontshare Switzer for the specimen and the blurred glyph.
directions.motion: Signature moment: a scroll-linked focus pull. Over the first 80vh the blur resolves from about 60px to 0 while the macro scales down from roughly 12x to reveal the whole word, and the frame thickens until its colour floods the page. Idle: the blurred macro drifts very slowly (20s loop) like a rack-focus hold. Micro: spec-row values are scrubbable (drag a number to change weight, size, columns, tracking) and the text block resets instantly; the theme toggle swaps the two-colour pair. Entrance is otherwise still. Reduced motion: hero shows the blurred state, the word appears sharp on the next screen with no interpolation.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Auer Grotesk', or abstracted to any single-product essay page (a fragrance, a chair) where the hero is a defocused silhouette of the object. IA: macro hero > name > information essay > setting waterfall (8 blocks) > styles list > features > credits > buy.
directions.whyWorldClass: The hero withholds almost everything and is still unmistakable; then the page proves the product in real text at real sizes with editable specs. It is the confidence of a foundry that does not need to sell.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: variable-font-pressure, specimen-lab, text-clip-reveal, sticky-iris-expansion. Differs: defocus as the hero idea, a colour frame that floods the page, and dense running-text blocks with spec rows instead of big display samples.
directions.buildRisk: A live 60px CSS blur on a 2000px text layer will drop frames on scroll: pre-render three blur levels to canvas bitmaps once and cross-fade and scale those instead. The scroll=0 thumbnail can read as an empty blob: keep the coloured frame and the sharp nav, and crop so a counter and a stem are recognisable. The waterfall needs real, well-hyphenated text (hyphens: auto with lang set) or it looks like filler.

directions.name: Black tile style matrix with label-chip navigation
directions.signature: A charcoal (#141414) page. Down the left edge runs a staggered stack of white rectangular label chips (34px tall, 19px text, 4px apart) where the active chip is orange-red (#CD390B) and its children are indented and coloured green (#50923B) and grey (#868686), ending in two white circular icon buttons. To the right, three columns of pure-black 6px-radius tiles: each tile is the complete style list of one family, every line set in its own style at about 22px in white, with script extensions marked by ringed counts, and each tile is captioned above by one 11px line of dry wit. On mobile the chips collapse to a single top chip and tiles run one column.
directions.grammar: Tiles 382px wide with 32px gutters starting at x=192; tiles of the same family butt together with 4px gaps; captions 11px with about 40px of air above; 'NEW' tags right-aligned in 10px caps; small ringed numerals and globe or variable icons at the tile's right edge; circular theme and view buttons pinned to the bottom corners. UI text 16-19px with +0.02em tracking. Three tones only (#141414, #000, #FFF) plus the three chip colours. Home variant: a split of two halftoned black-and-white images with a centred white card of five centred serif lines. Absent: thumbnails, prices at rest, hero, headings.
directions.typeStack: Observed: Unica78 LL for UI (16-19px, tracking 0.02em) with every catalogue family loaded live inside its tile. Free stand-ins: Inter or Fontshare Switzer at +0.02em for UI; for the tiles a set of six to eight contrasting variable families (Archivo, Fraunces, Newsreader, Bricolage Grotesque, Big Shoulders Display, Space Mono, Unbounded, IBM Plex Sans Condensed).
directions.motion: Entrance: chips slide out from the left edge with a 30ms stagger; tiles fade in column by column once fonts are ready. Micro: the active chip's colour snaps, sub-chips unfold; a tile inverts to white on hover and the hovered style row shows weight and price at right; captions type on. Signature moment: the view button switches every tile from style names to a sample sentence at once, and typing in one field retypes the entire wall live. Scroll: columns may drift at slightly different speeds. Reduced motion: no slide, instant swaps.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Kontor Type', or any range where each product has many variants (paint colours, vintages, speaker models, course modules). IA: chip nav (Typefaces > Collection / New Releases / Serif / Monospace; Articles; Bespoke; Editions; Timeline; Information; Shop) > tile wall grouped by caption > footer chips.
directions.whyWorldClass: The densest elegant catalogue on the web: the whole range is legible at once with zero thumbnails, every tile is its own specimen, and the label-maker chips give the chrome a physical, studio-drawer character.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: editorial-index, anchor-annotated-index, cmd-k-portfolio, specimen-lab. Differs: a dark wall of self-specimening style lists plus staggered colour-coded chip navigation; those slugs are single-face indexes on light grounds.
directions.buildRisk: Font weight: six to eight variable families is the ceiling for a single file; gate the reveal on document.fonts.ready so the thumbnail never shows fallback text. The chip stagger must be exact (consistent indent step) or it looks sloppy. With free fonts the tiles can feel like a Google Fonts page: choose families with real contrast between tiles and write the captions well.

directions.name: Saturated-field full-screen type tester
directions.signature: The viewport is a single electric-violet (#5B04E7) field framed by a 1px pale hairline inset 8px from every edge. Inside, three centred lines of an inscriptional serif at 261px, leading 0.95, in pale grey #D9D9D9, editable in place. A small 'Close' cell is notched into the frame's top-right corner. Along the bottom a 78px control strip is built as a hairline table: an optical-size slider, a weight slider, four checkbox cells and three action cells, every label in 13px small caps of the same typeface. On mobile the sample auto-fits to four or five lines and the control table wraps to a two-row grid.
directions.grammar: One colour plus one tint per screen; all chrome is 1px lines with no fills; sliders are a hairline with a 14px disc and a numeric value beneath in old-style figures; checkboxes are 16px outlined squares; the sample text auto-fits the frame width. No nav, no logo beyond the labels. For the template the frame persists while later screens change the field (violet, bone, black) and the optical size: Display at 261px centred, Text at 20px in two columns, Micro at 12px in four columns, each with the same bottom table. Absent: sans-serif anywhere, icons, buttons with fills, imagery.
directions.typeStack: Observed: GT Pantheon and GT Pantheon Italic only (display 261px, weight 400; labels in true small caps). Free stand-ins: Fraunces (Google; opsz 9-144, wght 100-900, SOFT 0, WONK 0) or Playfair (Google variable with opsz 5-1200), either of which makes the optical-size slider real; Cormorant Garamond is closer in inscriptional spirit but has no opsz axis. Labels via font-variant-caps: small-caps from the same family.
directions.motion: Sliders drive font-variation-settings live with no easing; 'New Sample' swaps the text with a per-line clip and refit (300ms). Entrance: the frame hairline draws clockwise, then lines set one by one. Scroll: the frame stays fixed while the field colour hard-cuts per section. Signature moment: the optical-size zoom, where scrolling shrinks the sample from 261px to 14px while the opsz axis tracks it, so hairlines visibly thicken and spacing opens as the text becomes a paragraph. Reduced motion: discrete steps between the three sizes.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Aurelian', a serif in three optical sizes, or a luxury house manifesto the visitor can retype. IA: tester hero > Display room > Text room > Micro room > italics and small caps > features table > manual download > licence row.
directions.whyWorldClass: Luxury delivered with one audacious colour and classical type, where even the controls are typeset rather than 'designed'. The interface is so reduced that the letterforms are the entire experience.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: variable-font-axis-playground, silent-luxury-restraint, illuminated-hours, specimen-lab. Differs: a single framed saturated field with a hairline-table control strip in small caps and an optical-size narrative; it is a quiet luxury object, not a widget playground.
directions.buildRisk: Range inputs and checkboxes must be fully custom (hairline track, disc thumb, outlined box) and keyboard accessible. contenteditable plus fit-to-width can jitter: debounce and refit on input only. The chosen stand-in decides everything: Playfair leans Didone, Fraunces leans soft, so test both at 261px against the reference before committing. Overlaps the existing axis playground if the frame, table and colour field are not executed precisely.

directions.name: Greyscale contact-sheet archive with density stepper
directions.signature: A white page packed edge to edge with about 180 greyscale thumbnails in a 13-column grid (108x60 cells, 1-2px gaps, portrait images letterboxed in white inside their cell), all visible at scroll=0. Above it a single 16px old-style serif line: the studio name plus one grey sentence at left, four nav words centred, a bracketed '[ Search ]' at right, and a bracketed '[ Filter ]' centred on a second line. A pale grey consent strip at the bottom uses the same bracket syntax. On mobile the grid drops to 5 columns and the serif line wraps to three.
directions.grammar: 15px margins; row pitch 62px; no captions, borders or hover chrome at rest. Serif 16/18 at weight 450; brackets with wide inner spacing are the only buttons. Greyscale is total until interaction. Density stepper states: 13, 8, 5 and 3 columns. An Index mode replaces the grid with a text table (year, client, discipline) in the same serif. Absent: hero, headings, featured projects, colour, any hierarchy among the work.
directions.typeStack: Observed: JJannon at 16/18, weight 450 (DIA); Base Grotesk light caps at 10-18px in boxed buttons (Base). Free stand-ins: EB Garamond 500 or Cormorant Garamond 500 for the serif line and index; Inter or Geist Light caps if a boxed UI variant is used.
directions.motion: Entrance: thumbnails 'develop' in a randomised wave (opacity 0, 0.3, 1 in steps, 8ms stagger across the cells). Hover: the cell snaps to colour and a 3x preview pins to the cursor with a one-line serif caption. Filter: non-matching cells blank to white in place, leaving holes instead of reflowing. Signature moment: the density stepper, where plus and minus animate the grid between 13, 8, 5 and 3 columns with FLIP transitions so every thumbnail travels to its new slot. Click expands a cell in place across five rows. Reduced motion: instant density change, no wave.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Office for Systems', a studio archive of 180 projects from 2012 to 2026, or a label or museum back-catalogue. IA: one archive page with Work / About / Process / Index modes; filter by discipline; project detail expands inline; About is a single serif paragraph overlay.
directions.photoBrief: If built photo-led instead: 150-200 small images of identity work in the world (posters on walls, signage, books, screens, event stages, packaging, team snapshots), mixed landscape and portrait, shot plainly with flat light; all converted to greyscale with slightly lifted blacks; colour originals kept for hover.
directions.whyWorldClass: It shows fourteen years of output in one screen with total confidence and no hierarchy; the only 'design' is a serif line with brackets, and that is enough. Density itself becomes the brand statement.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: infinite-canvas, museum-collection-explorer, voronoi-cell-gallery, morphing-grid, draggable-scatter. Differs: fixed tiny contact-sheet density, greyscale until touched, bracket-serif chrome, a density stepper and a hole-punch filter rather than pan, zoom or morph mechanics.
directions.buildRisk: Procedural thumbnails look samey and fake at this density: needs 10+ distinct generators (type posters, moire, grids, mock signage, book spreads, kinetic stills) and ideally a few real photos mixed in. 180 separate canvases cost memory: draw one offscreen atlas and slice it with background-position. Without real project names the hover captions feel empty: generate a believable client and year list.

directions.name: Equatorial navigation over a single film still
directions.signature: A full-bleed, slightly soft 16mm-looking still (an oblique close crop of a red lacquered table edge and an aluminium leg) with the entire navigation set on the exact vertical centre of the viewport as one line: the studio name in 19px mono caps at the left margin, three menu words with trailing commas at fixed grid columns, and a contact link at the far right, all in white 10px mono caps. Hanging from the third menu word, a seven-line paragraph in a 16px monospaced Garamond with italic emphasis and a stepped left indent. A live clock with the city in square brackets sits bottom-right and a three-language switch bottom-centre. On mobile the equator holds the name and a menu word; the paragraph sits below it.
directions.grammar: No header and no footer. White type directly on the image with no scrim. Two voices only: 10px mono caps at about 0.05em tracking, and 16/17.6 monospaced serif with italics. 12 columns with items at columns 1, 3, 4, 7 and 12; 18px margins. The home is barely more than one screen; the nav line stays fixed at 50% while paragraphs scroll through it. Trailing commas turn the menu into a sentence. Absent: logo mark, buttons, borders, cards, any colour beyond the photograph.
directions.typeStack: Observed: WT Garamono (a monospaced Garamond, 16px) and LL Grey Mono (10-19px caps). Free stand-ins: Libertinus Mono (Google) for the monospaced serif, with Courier Prime as fallback; DM Mono or Geist Mono for the caps labels.
directions.motion: The still is really a 6-10s loop with near-imperceptible movement (focus breathing, light drift). Entrance: image fades from black over 1.2s, then the paragraph sets line by line (80ms stagger). Hover on a menu word unfurls its list along the equator to the right, comma separated, and each item cross-dissolves the background still (1.2s ease-in-out). Scroll: following stills wipe vertically behind the fixed equator while text blocks travel up through it. Signature moment: the equator line as the only constant while everything behind it changes. The clock ticks each second. Reduced motion: static poster, instant image swaps.
directions.contentModel: Fictional client: 'Maison Verre', a photo and film production bureau, or an atelier, architect or agent. IA: equator nav (Projects, Talents, About, Contact) > about paragraph > projects as a comma-separated list with years > each project a full-bleed sequence captioned on the equator > talents roster > contact line.
directions.photoBrief: 6-8 full-bleed stills or 6-10s loops with a low-contrast filmic grade: close, oblique crops of objects and furniture edges (lacquered wood, brushed aluminium, glass, heavy fabric), shot from low or unusual angles with shallow depth of field; one saturated colour per frame (oxblood, bottle green, cobalt) against dark neutral ground; soft tungsten or window light, gentle grain and halation; no faces to camera; 16:10 at 2400px or wider, with a calm dark band across the vertical middle so white 10px text stays legible. The factory's existing interior and car stills could cover two frames if regraded and cropped tight.
directions.whyWorldClass: Luxury through absence: one typographic decision (where the navigation sits) makes the site unmistakable, and the monospaced serif is a voice almost no one else is using. It trusts a single image completely.
directions.noveltyVsLibrary: Nearest: silent-luxury-restraint, luxury-resort-cinematic-stillness, one-take, mono-ink-restraint. Differs: navigation on the horizontal centre axis with comma-sentence syntax, monospaced serif text hanging from it, and no header at all; those slugs keep conventional top chrome.
directions.buildRisk: Entirely dependent on image quality: generic stock kills it, so source or grade stills to the brief. White 10px text needs images with a dark middle band, or a very subtle local darkening behind the equator. At 390px the single line cannot hold five items: design the two-item mobile equator deliberately. Use a poster frame so the scroll=0 thumbnail is never black.
